Outcome: surviving/healthy spouse's labour force participation and earnings
Outcome: household income from transfers, pensions and insurance; liquid wealth
Heterogeneity: household liquidity, income loss, age
sample_size: 310,720 treated and 409,190 control households (fatal shocks); 37,437 treated and 54,887 control households (non-fatal heart attacks and strokes)
sample: Danish married and cohabiting couples with both spouses aged 45–80 in the year of the (actual or placebo) shock; the non-fatal shock sample is limited to spouses under 60 surviving at least three years.

definitions.definition: Households in which one spouse died between 1985 and 2011 and was aged 45 to 80 in the year of the (actual or placebo) event. Treatment households are matched to control households from the same cohorts that experienced the same event five years later (Delta = 5); summary statistics measured at t = -2. Prime-age subsamples restrict to households before the Early Retirement Age of 60.
registers: Cause of Death Registry; population/household registers
definitions.codes: Age at death 45-80; event years 1985-2011; Delta = 5 years
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.1 notes; Figure C.1 notes

definitions.definition: Households in which one spouse experienced a heart attack or a stroke for the first time between 1985 and 2011 and survived for at least three years, with both spouses under age 60. Controls are households from the same cohorts experiencing the same event five years later.
definitions.codes: First-ever heart attack or stroke; survival >= 3 years; both spouses < 60; years 1985-2011 (no ICD list given in appendix)

definitions.variable: Control group: same shock five years later
definitions.definition: Each treatment group of households shocked in year tau is matched to households from the same cohorts that experience the same shock in year tau + 5 (Delta = 5), who are assigned a placebo shock at t = 0 with t = year - tau; effects are identified up to four years after the shock via difference-in-differences relative to a baseline period (t = -2 in summary statistics).
Indicator for having any positive level of annual earnings.

From IDA, constructed from employee ATP pension contributions (available for individuals under 60): full-time means working at least 30 hours per week all 12 months of the calendar year (full-time full-year); part-time means working at some point in the year but fewer than 30 hours per week or fewer than 12 months.
Household income including income from any source: earnings, capital income, annuity payouts and benefits from any social program.

Third-party reported liquid wealth balances measured annually on 31 December, 1984-2011, including bank-account balances and lump-sum transfers from insurance companies; used in robustness checks to account for life insurance payouts.

definitions.variable: Potential income loss from spousal death
definitions.definition: Household income from any source in t = 1 holding the surviving spouse's earnings and social benefits (labor income, Social DI and Social Security) at their t = -1 level, divided by household income in t = -1, then normalized for treated households by the corresponding control-group mean.

For each municipality and year, the average Social Disability Insurance (Social DI) benefits received by non-working surviving spouses is computed; each widow in the treatment group is assigned her municipality-year leave-one-out mean. Benefits in annual DKK 1,000. Sample: widows under 67 (age of transition into Old-Age Pension) in years before 1994, when there is a data break in the reporting of survivors benefits received through Social DI. Controls: municipality unemployment rate and average earnings (interacted with Treat, Post, Treat x Post), widow age, year and municipality FE; post periods 2-4.
registers: Transfer income registers; municipality of residence
definitions.codes: Widow age < 67; years < 1994; leave-one-out municipality-year mean

definitions.definition: Binary indicator equal to 1 if the sick spouse was hospitalized for 10 days or more following the heart attack/stroke and 0 if hospitalized for fewer than 10 days; 10 days is the 75th percentile of the distribution of hospitalization days associated with the shock in the treatment sample.

definitions.variable: Primary vs secondary earner status of deceased spouse
definitions.definition: Deceased spouse is classified as primary (secondary) earner if the share of his/her average pre-event labor income in the household's average pre-event labor income was higher (lower) than one half.
definitions.codes: Share of household labor income > 0.5 = primary earner
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Figure C.1 and Table C.2 notes

definitions.definition: Indicator for whether the deceased husband worked throughout the entire five-year period preceding his death (periods -5 to -1); sample restricted to husbands who either worked in all five years or did not work at all in that period.

authors: Henrik Jacobsen Kleven and Esben Anton Schultz
title: Estimating Taxable Income Responses Using Danish Tax Reforms
summary: Uses a series of Danish tax reforms between 1984 and 2005 and full-population tax records to estimate the elasticity of taxable income. Elasticities are small for labour income (around 0.05) and larger for capital income and for top earners, and they are larger for big reforms than small ones.
data: Income Tax Register (tax return information)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Authors' own tax simulator of the Danish tax system, 1984–2005
variables: Outcome: three-year changes in taxable labour income and capital income (positive and negative)
Treatment: change in simulated marginal net-of-tax rate
Instrument: mechanical (predicted) change in marginal tax rate from tax reforms
Controls: pre-reform (base year s−1) income levels
Key reforms: 1987 and 1994 Danish tax reforms
period: Data since 1980; tax simulator and estimation 1984–2005 (three-year intervals 1984–1987 to 2002–2005)
sample_size: about 37 million observations (stacked three-year differences; about 49 million before sample restrictions)
sample: Full Danish population aged 15–70 who are fully tax liable and whose base-year income is not primarily welfare benefits, 1984–2005.

definitions.definition: Tax-code labor income: salary, wages, honoraria, fees, bonuses, fringe benefits and business earnings. Main outcome is the three-year growth rate (s to s+3) in real labor/wage earnings; regressions weighted by labor income and restricted to positive labor income.
definitions.source_location: Table 1; Section II; Table notes for labor income elasticity tables

definitions.definition: Interest income, rental income and business capital income minus interest on debt (mortgage, bank loans, credit cards, student loans), excluding stock income; analysed separately as positive and negative capital income because they are taxed very differently.

definitions.variable: Personal, stock and taxable income (PI, SI, TI)
definitions.definition: Personal income PI = LI + transfers, grants, awards, gifts, received alimony minus labour market contribution and certain pension contributions; stock income SI = dividends and realized capital gains on shares; deductions D = commuting, union fees, UI contributions, other work expenses, charity, paid alimony; taxable income TI = PI + CI + SI - D (differs from the tax-code label, which excludes SI).

Marginal tax rate on income component j computed with the authors' own Danish tax simulator (1984-2005) as [T(z_j + 100) - T(z)]/100, i.e. by raising that component by DKK 100; accounts for spousal jointness of exemptions and the marginal tax ceiling.

log(1 - tau_{s+3}(z_s)) - log(1 - tau_s(z_s)): change in the marginal net-of-tax rate simulated by applying year s+3 tax law to base-year s incomes; analogous mechanical change in virtual income instruments for the change in log virtual income.

Stacked three-year intervals 1984-1987 to 2002-2005, keeping taxpayers also observed in year s-1 (used for pre-reform income controls: splines of log s-1 income and the log deviation between s-1 and s incomes); restricted to ages 15-70, fully tax liable in Denmark, excluding those whose base-year income comes primarily from welfare benefits (about 37 million observations).
definitions.source_location: Section II; Section V table notes

definitions.definition: Taxpayers with income within DKK 5,000 of the top kink, DKK 3,000 of the middle kink or DKK 2,000 of the bottom kink (excluded in robustness checks).
definitions.source_location: Notes to labor income elasticity table (Section V)

definitions.definition: Treatment group: taxpayers experiencing an increase in the marginal net-of-tax rate on labor income (or on positive capital income) due to the 1987 reform over 1986-1989; control group: those experiencing a reduction; large-treatment group has net-of-tax rate increases of at least 15 percent.

authors: Claus Thustrup Kreiner, Søren Leth-Petersen and Peer Ebbesen Skov
title: Tax Reforms and Intertemporal Shifting of Wage Income: Evidence from Danish Monthly Payroll Records
summary: The 2010 cut in the top marginal tax rate was announced in advance, and monthly payroll data show top earners shifting wage income from December 2009 into January 2010. Shifting is concentrated among managers and employees of small firms, and it inflates short-run elasticity estimates.
data: Monthly payroll records (eIndkomst / eIncome register) from the tax agency SKAT
Background registers on individuals and firms at Statistics Denmark (incl. firm size, liquid assets)
Telephone survey on awareness of income-shifting opportunity (January 2011), merged to eIncome register
variables: Outcome: percentage change in monthly gross wage relative to 2008 average
Treatment: private-sector employees with 2008 monthly earnings above DKK 35,000 (top-tax incentive from 2010 reform)
Control group: monthly earnings DKK 30,000–35,000
Heterogeneity: firm size, liquid assets, earnings percentile
Elasticity of taxable income with and without shifting component
sample_size: 328,679 individuals, of which 219,179 in the treatment group; survey sample of 878 taxpayers
sample: Private-sector employees with a wage record in every month of 2008 and positive income in all years, earning above DKK 30,000 per month in 2008.

definitions.definition: Percentage change in individual monthly gross wage income (year t, month m) relative to the individual's average monthly gross earnings in 2008; percentage changes are used instead of logs because monthly earnings may be zero or near zero.

Robustness variants of the control group by average monthly 2008 earnings: narrow C-group DKK 32,000-35,000, wide C-group DKK 24,000-35,000; doughnut sample excludes individuals with average monthly 2008 earnings DKK 33,000-37,000; alternative baseline year 2009 (groups and income differences relative to 2009); alternative post-reform year 2011. T-group by percentile bins of average monthly earnings: [P80,P90), [P90,P95), [P95,P99), [P99,+].
definitions.codes: Narrow C: 32,000-35,000 DKK/month; wide C: 24,000-35,000 DKK/month; doughnut excl. 33,000-37,000 DKK/month (2008)
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A2 notes; Figure A1

definitions.definition: Individuals employed throughout 2008 (a wage record in every month of 2008) with positive income in all years, observed January 2008 - December 2011; includes people who are both wage earners and self-employed. Sensitivity: excluding employees with any exit to unemployment during 2009-2010.

Equals one if income in a month is high (more than 50 percent above) relative to its level in the same month of 2008 and income in the preceding month is low (more than 50 percent below) relative to its 2008 level; zero otherwise. Robustness with 25%-25% and 75%-75% cutoffs; a stricter version also requires November 2009 income to be unusually low.

Financial assets (money in bank accounts and value of shares and bonds) at end of 2008 relative to 2008 annual disposable income; groups below one month, between one and two months, and above two months of disposable income.

definitions.variable: Firm size groups and top-five paid
definitions.definition: Firm size groups: fewer than 25, 25-99, 100-499 and 500+ employees; large firms defined as more than 100 employees (top decile by number of employees); top-five paid employees within each firm used to isolate top management.

Survey respondents are classified as informed about the opportunity to shift income if they answered Q1 = 'After New Year' and Q2 = 'Legal' in the Capacent Epinion telephone survey (588 T-group and 290 C-group respondents).
registers: eIncome monthly payroll register (SKAT) linked to telephone survey

definitions.definition: Controls: age dummies, gender dummy, marriage dummy, 5 regional dummies, 10 sector dummies (as in paper Table 2) and 4 company-size dummies (as in paper Figure 7).

authors: Claus Thustrup Kreiner, David Dreyer Lassen and Søren Leth-Petersen
title: Liquidity Constraint Tightness and Consumer Responses to Fiscal Stimulus Policy
summary: The 2009 payout of Special Pension savings worked as a fiscal stimulus. Measuring constraint tightness by the marginal interest rate households pay, the spending response is highest for households facing high marginal rates and otherwise small, which supports targeting stimulus at the credit constrained.
data: Telephone survey of SP account holders on spending of the 2009 SP payout (Epinion, January 2010)
ATP register of Special Pension (SP) savings accounts (balances on 1 May 2009)
Income tax register with incomes, assets and liabilities, 1998–2009
Account-level deposit and loan records with interest payments from the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT), 2007–2009
Demographic registers (Statistics Denmark)
variables: Outcome: self-reported share of the SP payout spent
Key regressor: household marginal interest rate in 2008 (from account-level loan and deposit data)
Policy: 2009 early release of Special Pension (SP) savings
Controls: payout size, income, liquid wealth, demographics
Validation: register-based measures of net savings and pension savings
sample_size: 5,037 completed interviews with respondents who took out the SP balance
sample: Random sample of Danish Special Pension account holders who withdrew their SP savings in 2009, linked to administrative registers.

definitions.definition: Interest on marginal liquidity, computed from register data on all loan and deposit accounts of the household obtained from the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT), measured in 2008, in percent.
registers: Danish Tax Agency account-level loan and deposit data

definitions.variable: Propensity to spend the SP payout (survey)
definitions.definition: Survey (Epinion) question: considering the increase in disposable funds from the SP payout, how did you allocate it: 1) increase spending, 2) increase free savings, 3) reduce debt, 4) increase pension savings; spending share in [0,1] (96% of answers 0 or 1). Main sample includes only respondents who withdrew the SP balance (N = 5,037); extended sample adds 215 non-withdrawers coded as zero spending. Probit robustness codes share >= 0.5 as 1.
registers: Telephone survey linked to registers on CPR
definitions.codes: Probit: 0 if share in [0,0.5], 1 if in [0.5,1]

definitions.definition: SP payout is the (potential) payout, i.e. the Special Pension account balance less taxes; enters as SP payout / 2008 disposable income (percent).

Change in net bank assets (bank deposits minus bank debt, including credit card debt, recorded on the last day of the year) between t and t-1 from the income-tax/wealth register; used to validate survey answers for 2005-2011.
Disposable income minus net savings (change in net bank assets) minus private pension contributions, c = y - dW - p, following Browning and Leth-Petersen (2003).

Indicator equal to one if the individual holds liquid assets worth less than one month's disposable income (threshold chosen for highest predictive power); a continuous liquid-assets-to-disposable-income ratio is also used.
Indicator equal to one if debt service is 15 percent or more of disposable income; also used as a continuous debt-service-to-disposable-income ratio.

Individuals with total deposit-account balances exceeding one month's disposable income are labelled as having a balance (to net out salary accounts credited just before 31 December); used to define the group holding both assets and debt.
Liquid assets (deposits, shares and bonds) in 2008 as percent of 2008 disposable income; underlies the low-liquid-assets indicator.
registers: Statistics Denmark income and wealth registers

definitions.definition: Debt service, defined as total interest payments on loans, in 2008 as percent of 2008 disposable income; underlies the high-debt-service indicator.
Average of (register) income over 1998-2008, entered in logs; income controls also include ln(2008 register income) and the standard deviation of ln(income).
Short, medium and long education correspond to vocational training, college BA level, and college Master and PhD level, respectively; reference group is high school or less.
definitions.codes: Short = vocational; medium = BA; long = Master/PhD; ref = high school or less

definitions.definition: Survey questions on whether total 2009 income evolved better/worse than expected (5-point scale plus don't know), changes in expected 2010 income, and changes in expectations about the possibility of borrowing money in 2010 (5-point scale from much more optimistic to much more pessimistic).

authors: Helena Skyt Nielsen, Torben Sørensen and Christopher Taber
title: Estimating the Effect of Student Aid on College Enrollment: Evidence from a Government Grant Policy Reform
summary: A 1988 reform raised Danish student grants for students from higher-income families. Roughly 1,000 dollars of extra aid raised enrolment by about 1.35 percentage points, a response that is consistent with modest credit constraints rather than binding ones.
data: Register-based dataset covering the entire Danish population, 1983–2005 (Statistics Denmark)
Educational event histories (education registers), 1973–2005
High school GPA records
Parental income used for student-aid means-testing (tax records)
Parental liquid assets from wealth/tax records
variables: Outcome: college enrollment within one year of high school graduation
Treatment: stipend (fraction of full student grant) the individual is eligible for
Variation: 1988 Danish student grant reform and kinked means-tested aid schedule
Running/ranking variable: parental (social) income percentile
Borrowing-constraint proxy: low parental liquid assets
Controls: high school GPA, sex, age, region, parents' education
period: 1983–2005 (population register data); high school graduation cohorts 1983–1990, estimation on cohorts 1985 and 1988–1990
sample_size: 108,933 high school graduates in the final selected sample; 54,843 observations in the main probit estimates (cohorts 1985, 1988–1990)
sample: Danish graduates of the ordinary academic high school track who graduated at ages 19–20 in 1983–1990, with observed GPA and parental information.

definitions.definition: Indicator for accumulated enrollment in any college (short-, medium- or long-cycle higher education) by one year after high school graduation, taken from educational event histories 1973-2005; one-year horizon chosen so pre-reform cohorts decided before the reform was announced.
definitions.source_location: Section II; Section V.B and Table 3

definitions.definition: Pre-reform means-testing measure X = mother's taxable income + father's taxable income - a x number of siblings below the age limit + f(parents' wealth); in 1985 a = 16,600 DKK and f(W) = 0.1(W-447,700)1[W>447,700] + 0.15(W-895,400)1[W>895,400] + 0.25(W-1,492,100)1[W>1,492,100]. Since social income no longer exists in the registers after 1988, a best post-reform analogue is computed accounting for wealth and number of siblings; analyses use the social income percentile within cohort.
definitions.source_location: Section II eq. (1) and footnotes 6, 12; Section IV end

definitions.definition: Stipend the individual would be eligible for under the 1985 rule: compute X, find its quantile within the current cohort, take the corresponding quantile of X in the pre-reform cohort, and apply the 1985 grant schedule (maximum stipend if X < DKK 156,400, none if X > DKK 256,200 in 1985). Stipend measured as four years of grant.
definitions.source_location: Section II footnote 6; Section II procedure steps (1)-(4) and footnote 13

definitions.definition: Basic indicator D1 = 1 if parents' liquid assets at time of high school graduation fall short of one month's income; extreme indicator D2 = 1 if below two months' income. Liquid assets are all non-housing assets: cash, shares, bonds, mortgage deeds and other assets; children of self-employed parents (liquid assets not registered) are set to D1 = D2 = 0.

High school graduates from the ordinary (academic) high school track in 1985-1990 (assets not observed before 1985) who graduate at 'normal' ages 19-20, with observed GPA, non-missing parental income and education, excluding those with divorced parents at graduation; the 1986 and 1987 cohorts are dropped because of anticipation of the reform and an earlier change in the means-testing age limit. Final sample 108,933.
High school grade point average on the Danish 13-point scale (grades 0, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13; 6 and above passed); only observed for the traditional academic high school track.

authors: Christian Dustmann, Rasmus Landersø and Lars Højsgaard Andersen
title: Refugee Benefit Cuts
summary: A 2002 reform cut welfare benefits for newly arrived refugees by roughly half. Employment rose modestly in the short run and then faded, while disposable income fell sharply. The cut raised crime among adults and harmed children's school enrolment and outcomes.
data: Danish Immigration Service residence permit records
Income register from tax authority records (earnings, transfers, taxes)
Hourly wage and occupation data
Labour market register (employment status)
Population register (BEF)
Crime registers: police and court records of charges and convictions
Job openings data from Jobindex.dk
variables: Treatment: residency granted after the July 2002 Start Aid benefit cut
Running variable: date residency was granted relative to the reform
Outcome: employment, labour earnings, transfer and disposable income
Outcome: crime convictions (property crime)
Heterogeneity: local labour demand in assignment municipality (low-skill job openings per unemployed)
period: Residency granted 2001–2003; outcomes up to 10 years after residency
sample_size: 4,843 individuals
sample: Refugees and family-reunified refugees granted residency in Denmark between January 2001 and December 2003 aged 18–55, excluding Afghans, former Yugoslavs and re-migrants.

definitions.definition: Refugees and persons family-reunified with refugees granted residency 1 January 2001-31 December 2003 aged 18-55 (Danish Immigration Service permit records), excluding Afghans and former Yugoslavs and those re-migrating within 9 years (4,843 adults). Treatment: residency granted after 1 July 2002 (Start Aid); running variable is the exact residency date relative to the cutoff.
registers: Danish Immigration Service residence permit records

definitions.definition: From the income register, measured from the first year post residency: labor earnings (pre-tax), transfers (pre-tax), pre-tax gross income (= labor earnings + transfers for this sample), and post-tax disposable income (= gross income minus tax payments). Public expenditure on refugees = transfer payments minus tax payments.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix B.2 Data Construction and Definitions

definitions.definition: Register hourly wage rate estimated as annual labor earnings divided by annual hours worked; distributional effects estimated using dummies 1[wage <= x] for x from $0 to $40.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix B.2; Figure A.4 notes

definitions.definition: Three mutually exclusive states (employment, unemployment, not in the labor force) as defined by the ILO, from the register-based labour force statistics (RAS). In the 2012 repeal analysis employment is instead defined as non-zero labor earnings in a calendar year.

Occupations (ILO ISCO) grouped into seven categories by type and skill intensity: (i) high skills/manager, (ii) medium skills/office related, (iii) sales/services, (iv) vocational work requiring medium/basic skills, (v) construction/primary sector work requiring basic skills, (vi) unspecified self-employment, (vii) unskilled manual labor requiring few/no skills. 'Jobs requiring some skills' = (i)-(vi); 'unskilled manual labor' = (vii).
registers: Occupation codes (ISCO) from Statistics Denmark employment registers

definitions.definition: Convictions for offences against the criminal code (Central Police register labels, e.g. 'theft from supermarket'), defined as court rulings or pre-court settlements of guilt resulting in a sentence (fine, suspended sentence or imprisonment), dated by the exact offence date; 'crime in year 1' = offences committed within the first 365 days after residency. Crime types used: all crime, property crime, theft in supermarket, violence.
definitions.codes: Sentence = fine, suspended sentence or imprisonment

definitions.variable: Local labor demand: low/unskilled job openings per unemployed
definitions.definition: Job openings for low- and unskilled work posted on Jobindex.dk (from 2002) counted by postal code and aggregated to municipality, divided by the municipality's stock of unemployed (population register residence x labour market register unemployment), averaged over 2002 and 2003. Because postings only exist from 2002, the ratio is predicted from 1999-2001 municipal employment conditions (average employment rate, non-Western immigrant employment rate, unskilled employment rate, immigrants' average labor earnings and their interactions). Municipalities ranked 0-1 and split at the unweighted median (low-demand ~0.17, high-demand ~0.32 openings per unemployed).
registers: Jobindex.dk postings; population register (BEF); labour market register
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix B.2 and Figure B.1

definitions.definition: Fraction of 20-60-year-old non-Western immigrants in a municipality who are employed, 1999-2001, using population-register data recorded on January 1 (country of origin, age, municipality) merged with individual employment from labour market registers; municipalities ranked 0-1 and split at the median (low ~0.39 vs high ~0.55).

Adults aged 18-55 at residency who received residency 2008-2014. For year-1 outcomes the treatment group is those granted residency 2012-2014; for year-2 outcomes it is those granted residency 2011-2013. Employment = non-zero labor earnings in the calendar year; outcomes only for two years after residency.
registers: Danish Immigration Service records; income register

definitions.definition: Indicators for having post-tax disposable income below $500, $750 and $1,000 per month, where monthly income = annual disposable income (year 1, year 2, or years 3-5) divided by 12.

definitions.variable: Type A / Type B refugee couples
definitions.definition: Type A couples: both spouses receive residency after the Start Aid reform (July 2002). Type B couples: one spouse receives residency before and one after the reform.
registers: Danish Immigration Service residence permit records
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.1 notes; Figure A.3

definitions.definition: Donut sample excludes two months of residency dates on each side of the reform; reduced bandwidth +/- 12 months; placebo reforms from -5 to +5 months each using +/- 18 months around the placebo date; extended sample adds Afghan and ex-Yugoslavian refugees.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.11 notes; Figure A.5 notes

definitions.definition: Labor migrants not eligible for Social Assistance/Start Aid: non-EU/EEA citizens with a work visa (requiring a pre-existing job contract in Denmark) and EU/EEA citizens excluding students; first migration to Denmark only; employment = any employment in Denmark in a given year.

authors: Jeppe Druedahl and Alessandro Martinello
title: Long-Run Saving Dynamics: Evidence from Unexpected Inheritances
summary: Sudden parental deaths deliver unexpected inheritances. Heirs' wealth jumps and then declines over roughly a decade back toward its pre-inheritance path, which implies a moderate marginal propensity to consume out of wealth and informs the calibration of buffer-stock saving models.
data: Wealth data from yearly third-party financial institution reports in the income/wealth registers (IND/FORMUE: BANKAKT, KURSANP, etc.)
Individual tax returns / Income register (IND) for disposable income
Housing and land registers (property values, number of housing units)
Birth registers / parent-child links (BEF)
Mortality register / Register of Causes of Death (ICD-10 cause of death)
variables: Outcome: net worth normalized by permanent income
Outcome: liquid assets, housing equity, financial investments, uncollateralized debt
Treatment: timing of sudden parental death (ICD-10 I21–I22, V, X, Y, R96)
Potential inheritance: deceased parent's net worth split among children, net of inheritance tax
Permanent income: weighted average of past five years' disposable income
sample_size: 6,286 heirs
sample: Heirs aged 25–50 at inheritance whose unmarried parent died suddenly between 1995 and 2012, with potential inheritance exceeding one year of permanent income, excluding the wealthiest 1 percent.

definitions.definition: Sum of housing equity, liquid assets and financial wealth minus uncollateralized (bank) debt, at year end, CPI-deflated (2010=100) and divided by permanent income; pension funds and durables (cars, boats) excluded. Each component floored at 0 in code; individuals with net worth outside the 1st-99th percentile in any year are dropped.
definitions.codes: totassets = stocks(KURSANP+KURSAKT) + bonds(PANTAKT+OBLAKT) + KOEJD + BANKAKT; totdebts = mortgage(OBLGAELD+PANTGAELD) + BANKGAELD; networth = totassets - totdebts
definitions.source_location: data/server/rawbuild.do ('Wealth' block, 'SAMPLE SELECTION'); CEBI WP 02-17 Table D.1

definitions.definition: Sum of cash and savings accounts held in Danish banks (BANKAKT), floored at 0, normalized by permanent income.

Value of owned real estate (KOEJD) minus collateralized debt (mortgage bonds OBLGAELD + other mortgage debt PANTGAELD, at market value of associated bonds at year end), normalized by permanent income.

Financial wealth = market value of directly held stocks, bonds and mutual funds (KURSANP+KURSAKT plus PANTAKT+OBLAKT in code; WP lists KURSANP+KURSAKT+OBLAKT); uncollateralized debt = bank debts not associated with a bond (BANKGAELD). Both normalized by permanent income.
definitions.codes: finw = max(0, KURSANP+KURSAKT + PANTAKT+OBLAKT); liqdebts = BANKGAELD

definitions.definition: Weighted average of current and four lagged years of disposable income: 0.45, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05 for t to t-4; disposable income = BRUTTO + SKATFRIYD + AKTIEINDK - SKATMVIALT_NY, CPI-deflated; floored at DKK 60,000 in code. Inheritance is normalized by permanent income in the year before parental death.
definitions.codes: dispinc = brutto + skatfriyd + aktieindk - skatmvialt_ny; perminc = filter(dispinc), coef(45 25 15 10 5) lags(0/4) normalise

definitions.definition: Parental death (1996-2012) is sudden if the primary cause of death has the listed ICD-10 codes. The WP states I21*-I22*, V*, X*, Y*, R96*; the replication code additionally includes I23, I24 and I46.
definitions.codes: WP: ICD-10 I21-I22, V*, X*, Y*, R96; code: substr(doedsaars1,1,3) in I21,I22,I23,I24,I46,R96 or first letter V, X, Y
definitions.source_location: rawbuild.do ('DEATHS AND INHERITANCE'); CEBI WP 02-17 fn. 7 and Appendix D

definitions.definition: Deceased parent's gross bequest (max(0,housing equity) + financial wealth + liquid assets - uncollateralized debt, floored at 0, in the last observed year) split equally among all children (from FTDB), net of inheritance tax: if estate exceeds the exemption bundfr, net = (0.85*(estate - bundfr) + bundfr)/n_heirs. Where both parents die, the largest inheritance is kept. Normalized by heir's permanent income; main sample has potential inheritance > 1 year of permanent income.
definitions.codes: gross_bequest; n_heirs; bundfr (yearly exemption, e.g. 264,100 DKK in 2010); inhgroup==2 if inheritance>1
definitions.source_location: rawbuild.do ('Remove taxes from inheritance'); main_analysis.do line ~96; WP Appendix D, Table D.3

definitions.definition: Heirs aged 25-59 in observed years, aged under 50 at the parental death (alder_atshock<50), with non-missing inheritance; net-worth outliers (outside p1-p99 in any year) dropped. WP: parents die unmarried between 1995 and 2012.
definitions.source_location: rawbuild.do ('SAMPLE SELECTION'); main_analysis.do lines 14-29; WP Section I

definitions.variable: Labour income, salary and pension contributions
definitions.definition: Labour income = ERHVERVSINDK (labour-market income incl. bonuses, compensations and self-employment income); salary = LOENMV (salary only); pension contributions = private (qpripen) plus labour-market (qarbpen) pension contributions.
Count of distinct properties (ejendom number x municipality) owned by the individual in the ownership register (EJER), plus total ownership share.
definitions.codes: bnr = group(ejdnr komnr); n_owned; pct_owned = total(ejerpct)

authors: Paul Bingley and Lorenzo Cappellari
title: Correlation of Brothers' Earnings and Intergenerational Transmission
summary: Decomposes the earnings correlation between Danish brothers into the part explained by fathers' earnings and the part due to other shared family and community factors. Intergenerational transmission accounts for a larger share of sibling similarity than simple father-son elasticities suggest, once permanent earnings and life-cycle bias are handled.
data: Civil registration system / population register with parent-child links (BEF)
Income Statistics Register (IND): annual pre-tax labour earnings from tax returns
variables: Outcome: annual pre-tax labour earnings (sum over all employments), ages 25–60
Family structure: father/first-son/second-son triads
Life-cycle: 3-year birth cohort groups and age
sample_size: 303,231 men in 101,077 families; 5,488,445 earnings observations
sample: Danish fathers born 1935–1961 and their first and second sons (born 1959–1985) with the same mother, with at least five consecutive positive earnings observations.

definitions.definition: Annual pre-tax labour earnings from income tax returns, summed over all employments in the year, 1980-2014, deflated to 2012 DKK with a year-specific index (earn/R*6768). In code: IDA person variable lonind for 1980-2009, corloen for 2010-2011 and from the IND register for 2012-2014; negative values recoded to 0.
definitions.source_location: triplet-data-creation-20160706.do ('collect earnings histories'); IZA DP10761 Section III

definitions.variable: Earnings sample trimming and age window
definitions.definition: Person-year observations kept at (cohort-central) ages 25-60; missing and non-positive earnings dropped; the lower and upper 0.5% of earnings dropped by family member type (father, son 1, son 2) and year; individuals must have at least 5 consecutive years of earnings observations.

Fathers born 1935-1961 (code frame 1935-1969) with two sons by the same mother, linked through the fertility database (ftdb2010, father pnrf and mother pnrm) restricted to madopt=='1'; twins/multiple births dropped; only sons of the same mother-father match as the father's first son kept; sons who are themselves fathers in the sample are dropped; families whose triplet birth order is inconsistent with population birth order are purged; fathers younger than 18 (216 months) at first son's birth dropped; brother spacing must be 12-144 months; first sons born 1959-1985, second sons 1962-1985.
definitions.source_location: triplet-data-creation-20160706.do; inspection.do; IZA DP10761 Section III

definitions.definition: Individuals are grouped into 3-year birth cohorts (central years 1936, 1939, ..., 1984), with the cohort's central birth year used to compute age (ageco = year - cohort).

Years of completed education computed as int(HFPRIA/12) from the latest available education register record (1980-2009), recoding 0-7 to 7 and 18-21 to 18; father's schooling linked through the fertility database father identifier.

Numbers of older/younger brothers and sisters with the same father and with the same father-mother pair, computed over all children of the father (twins ordered randomly), for robustness to sibling composition.
definitions.codes: nobsf, nybsf, nobsfm, nybsfm, nossf, nyssf, nossfm, nyssfm

authors: N. Meltem Daysal, Marianne Simonsen, Mircea Trandafir and Sanni Breining
title: Spillover Effects of Early-Life Medical Interventions
summary: Extra medical treatment for very-low-birth-weight newborns, identified from a birth weight threshold, improves not only the treated infant but also the outcomes of older siblings, who do better in school. Family resources and parental time respond to the child's health.
data: Medical Birth Register (MFR): birth weight, gestational age, parity
Parent and sibling links (BEF)
9th-grade exam test score register (reading and math)
Education/enrollment registers
Prescription drug register (antidepressant use, from 1995)
Health registers for diagnoses (intellectual disability, ADHD) and mortality
Income and labour market registers for parents
variables: Running variable: focal child's birth weight relative to 1,500-gram VLBW cutoff
Outcome: siblings' standardized 9th-grade reading and math test scores
Outcome: sibling enrollment beyond compulsory education by age 19 and high-school track
Mechanisms: focal-child mortality and mental health; maternal antidepressant use; parental income, employment, days worked
sample_size: 5,827 sibling observations (siblings of 3,677 focal children)
sample: Siblings (same mother) of Danish children born 1982–1993 with birth weight between 1,300 and 1,700 grams.

definitions.definition: Focal child's birth weight (bw) centred at 1,500 grams; treatment indicator vlbw = 1 if birth weight < 1,500 g; local linear RD with separate slopes on each side and triangular weights 1-|bw-1500|/bandwidth.
definitions.source_location: 09 Final data preparation and analyses.do, lines ~568-574

definitions.definition: Grades from the 9th-grade school-leaving exams (proeveform 'Prøvefag 2002-2006' or 'Bundne prøvefag', not teacher 'Standpunkt' marks) in Danish oral (Mundtlig) and Mathematics written/problem-solving/skills; set to missing for cohorts born before 1986 or after 1997. In indices, non-test outcomes are standardized by birth year.
definitions.codes: UDFK2013: GRUNDSKOLEFAG in ('Dansk','Matematik'); FAGDISCIPLIN 'Mundtlig' (Danish) / 'Skriftlig','Matematisk problemløsning','Matematiske færdigheder' (math); proeveform in ('Prøvefag 2002-2006','Bundne prøvefag')

definitions.definition: Ongoing education (IGUDD) from the education registers mapped to DST audit groups; ac_track = enrolled in general upper secondary (gymnasium) at any age 14-19; voc_track = enrolled in vocational education at ages 14-19; ac_track_at_18 = gymnasium enrollment at age 18; enrolled_beyond = ac_track or voc_track.
definitions.source_location: 06e Adding educ track rev.sas, lines ~128-217; 09 do-file line 674

definitions.definition: Annual change in cumulative labour market experience ERHVER (measured in 1/1000 years) converted to days: dif_erhverv/(1000/260); person-years with negative changes (e.g., stays abroad) dropped; measured 0-15 years after the child's birth.
definitions.source_location: 06 Adding parental labor outcomes rev.sas, lines ~470-705

definitions.definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the annual change in cumulative experience ERHVER is non-zero in the year, 0 if zero.
definitions.codes: M_extsup = 1 if dif_erhverv ne 0; 0 if dif_erhverv = 0
definitions.source_location: 06 Adding parental labor outcomes rev.sas, lines ~700-705, 855-860

definitions.definition: Wage income LONIND from person data deflated to 2004 prices with the CPI; negative values set to missing; measured by years since the child's birth.
definitions.source_location: 06 Adding parental labor outcomes rev.sas, lines ~18-100

definitions.definition: Purchases of antidepressants (ATC N06A) from the prescription register (LMDB), aggregated by person and year (accumulated DDD); available from 1995.
Hospital diagnosis of mental retardation in any diagnosis field (action, secondary, psychiatric) by age 10.
Any psychiatric diagnosis in hospital registers: ICD-8 codes 290.09-315.99 or any ICD-10 chapter F (DF) code in any diagnosis field.

authors: Martin Browning and Søren Leth-Petersen
title: Imputing Consumption from Income and Wealth Information
summary: Tests whether consumption can be imputed from register data as income minus the change in wealth, by comparing the imputation with expenditure survey responses for the same households. The imputation works well for most households but is noisy for those with housing transactions or large stock holdings.
data: Danish Expenditure Survey 1994–96
Administrative income and wealth (tax) records: disposable income and year-end asset holdings
variables: Outcome: survey-reported total household expenditure
Imputed consumption: disposable income minus change in wealth
Year-end holdings of different assets
period: 1994–1996 survey years, linked to register years around the survey year
sample: Households in the 1994–96 Danish Expenditure Survey linked to their administrative income and wealth records.

definitions.definition: Total expenditure imputed at the household level as disposable after-tax income minus the change in net wealth between end of year t-1 and end of year t (c = y - dW). Validated against total expenditure reported in the 1994-96 Danish Expenditure Survey linked to the households' register records. Relies on wealth-tax register information, which ends after the wealth tax was abolished in 1997.
registers: Income and wealth tax registers (Statistics Denmark)
definitions.source_location: Section 4 (Expenditure imputation), eq. (1) and footnote 1 - restatement of the Browning and Leth-Petersen (2003) definition by the same authors

definitions.definition: Sum of gross income including interest income, housing transfers and dividends from share capital, minus taxes on income, taxes on shares, surplus on owner-occupied housing and tax-exempted interest expenses.
definitions.source_location: Section 4 (Expenditure imputation) - restatement of Browning and Leth-Petersen (2003)

definitions.definition: Assets minus liabilities measured at year end; assets are the market value of share capital, bank deposits and the market value of bonds and securities; liabilities include mortgage and bank debt.
definitions.source_location: Section 4 (Expenditure imputation) - restatement of Browning and Leth-Petersen (2003)

authors: Jakob Roland Munch, Michael Rosholm and Michael Svarer
title: Are Homeowners Really More Unemployed?
summary: Tests the Oswald hypothesis that home ownership raises unemployment. Danish homeowners are less geographically mobile, but they find local jobs faster, so their unemployment spells are shorter overall. Ownership does not raise aggregate unemployment.
data: Administrative register data on unemployment spells for a 2.5% random sample of the Danish population
Regional unemployment measure from the Institute for Local Government Studies (1987–2000)
variables: Outcome: unemployment duration in weeks
Outcome: exit destination (new job locally, job in another commuting area, other states)
Key regressor: home ownership indicator
Controls: age, gender, children, household type, immigrant status, education, UI fund membership and replacement rate
sample_size: 18,992 persons with 52,738 unemployment spells
sample: Flow sample of all unemployment spells in 1997–2000 for individuals aged 19–66 in a 2.5% random sample of the Danish population.

definitions.definition: Flow sample of all unemployment spells in 1997-2000 for individuals in a 2.5% random sample of the Danish population, restricted to inflow into unemployment of workers aged 19-66; spell duration measured in weeks (18,992 persons, 52,738 spells).
definitions.source_location: Section 3 (Data and the Danish labour and housing markets), pp. 9-10

definitions.definition: Destination after an unemployment spell: new job in the local labour market, new job in another commuting area, or other states than employment and unemployment. A worker is geographically mobile if he or she gets a job and moves to another commuting area up to 8 weeks before and 52 weeks after the start of the job spell (exact moving dates known).

Local labour markets are commuting areas built from geographically connected municipalities such that the internal migration rate is 50% higher than the external migration rate (Andersen 2000); the 275 municipalities are merged into 51 commuting areas.

Measure constructed by the Institute for Local Government Studies (AKF): unemployment rate in an area around each municipality, defined by how far a resident can commute without a daily commuting cost exceeding DKK 60 (1987 prices); available 1987-2000.
registers: Institute for Local Government Studies regional unemployment data

definitions.definition: Indicator for being a home owner (living in owner-occupied housing) versus renting (private rental, social or cooperative housing).

definitions.variable: UI fund membership and replacement rate
definitions.definition: Indicator for membership of an unemployment insurance fund and, for members, the UI replacement rate; other controls are age, gender, number of dependent children aged 0-17, two-adult household, immigrant from a non-OECD country, municipality size and education.

authors: Rasmus Landersø, Helena Skyt Nielsen and Marianne Simonsen
title: School Starting Age and the Crime-Age Profile
summary: Children born just after the school start cut-off begin school almost a year later. Starting school older lowers crime at young ages, especially for boys, by shifting the crime-age profile rather than permanently reducing crime, consistent with an incapacitation and maturity channel.
data: Population register with exact birth dates and parent links (BEF)
Criminal charge register (charges for property, violence and other crimes, with dates)
Birth records: birth weight, gestational length, APGAR score (likely Medical Birth Register, MFR; not named in paper)
Education registers (age in 8th grade as proxy for school starting age)
Parental education and labour market registers
variables: Outcome: criminal charge at a given age / at or before a given age (from age 15)
Treatment: school starting age (7.6 vs 6.6)
Instrument/running variable: birth date relative to January 1 cut-off (±30 days)
Heterogeneity: gender; crime type (property, violence, other)
sample_size: 48,546 and 50,383 children (the two gender groups) at age 15, born in December or January (Table 1)
sample: Danish children born in December or January between December 1981 and January 1993 (main bandwidth ±30 days around January 1).

definitions.definition: Indicator for being charged with a crime between one birthday and the next (memoryless measure), from age 15 onwards. Charges rather than convictions are used to gain three additional years of data; results are robust to using convictions.

definitions.variable: Crime at or before a given age
definitions.definition: Accumulated indicator for having been charged with a crime at or before a given age (from age 15), keeping track of earlier incidences; also number of crimes for the intensive margin. Outcomes aligned by age are measured exactly at the birthday.

Three broad categories: property crime (most frequently shoplifting, burglary, vandalism), violent crime (ordinary and aggravated assault, threats, violence towards public servants) and residual other crime (dominated by traffic-related crime such as driving without a licence, then drug or weapon crime).

Timing of school start is not observed for these cohorts, so age in 8th grade is used as an approximation; SSA is modelled as a binary indicator for school starting age 7.6 versus 6.6 (old-for-grade), with robustness to a continuous measure. Validated with exact ages at all grade levels observed from 2007 onwards.

Instrument is being born after the January 1 cut-off (January=1); main sample uses children born within +/-30 days of January 1, cohorts born mid-1981 to mid-1993, controlling for a flexible function of distance in days to the cut-off and cohort fixed effects. Covariates are centred on cut-off dates, comparing January year t with December year t-1.
Child birth weight, gestational length and APGAR score (0-10, based on appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration) used as background controls; register not named in the paper.

Parents' education and labour market outcomes measured one year prior to the child's birth, aligned to cut-off (e.g. children born Dec 1981 or Jan 1982 use parental characteristics from 1980); also mother's age at first birth.
registers: Parental education and labour market registers

authors: Simon Halphen Boserup, Wojciech Kopczuk and Claus Thustrup Kreiner
title: Born with a Silver Spoon? Danish Evidence on Wealth Inequality in Childhood
summary: Third-party reported wealth records of children show that wealth inequality is as high in childhood as among adults, with top shares driven by transfers from parents and grandparents. Wealth at age 18 predicts wealth in adulthood, and intergenerational wealth correlations are present from early ages.
data: Individual wealth data from tax return records (Danish Tax Agency SKAT, via Statistics Denmark)
Population register with parent identifiers (BEF)
Education and income registers
variables: Outcome: child wealth and wealth rank in adulthood (age 45)
Key regressor: childhood wealth (age 18) and parental wealth rank
Inferred inter vivos transfers and bequests (bunching at gift-tax allowance)
Portfolio components (deposits, securities, real estate, debt)
sample_size: Pooled cross-section: on average close to 650 thousand observations per one-year age group; panel regressions: 36,102 observations
sample: All individuals aged 1–40 in 2000–2011 with living parents (pooled cross-section), plus a panel of the 1965 birth cohort with both parents alive in 2011, followed 1983–2011.

definitions.definition: Value of assets minus liabilities measured on the last day of the year from administrative tax return records (SKAT), 1983-2011; mostly third-party reported by banks and financial institutions. Assets include deposits, stocks, bonds, real estate and deposited mortgages; liabilities include bank debt, mortgage credit debt, card debt, student debt, debt to municipalities, unpaid taxes, etc. Pension funds are not included; self-reported items (cars, boats, etc.) are excluded after the 1996 abolition of the wealth tax.

Public (tax-assessed) values of real estate are adjusted upwards each year using the average relative difference between selling price and public value of real estate traded that year, following Leth-Petersen (2010).

From 1995 onwards complete portfolio information on bonds, stocks, cash in banks, real estate, mortgage loans and the sum of other loans; childhood holdings summarised as bank deposits, securities and real estate.

Percentile rank computed within child age-year specific wealth distributions (parents ranked on total parental wealth observed at the same time); ties, notably zero wealth among young children, are randomly broken. Adult outcome is the child's rank at age 45 (27 years after age 18).
For each child, wealth at a given age minus the present value of earnings up to that age (real interest rates 0%, 3%, 6%), censored at zero, as a lower bound on transfers received.

First time an individual (ages 1-12) has positive wealth, wealth at that point treated as the transfer; distance to the gift-tax basic allowance (DKK 58,700 in 2011) and to twice that amount (two donors) is plotted to look for bunching.

PCD: pooled cross-section of all individuals aged 1-40 in 2000-2011 with parents alive (parent IDs registered for Danes born from 1960). PD: panel of the 1965 birth cohort with both parents alive in 2011, followed 1983-2011 (ages 18-46). Monetary values deflated by CPI (2011 prices).

authors: Claus Thustrup Kreiner, Søren Leth-Petersen and Louise Charlotte Willerslev-Olsen
title: Financial Trouble Across Generations: Evidence from the Universe of Personal Loans in Denmark
summary: Loan-level records on all personal loans show strong intergenerational persistence in financial trouble: children of parents who default are far more likely to default themselves, and the correlation is present already in early adulthood and is not explained by income or education.
data: Loan register from the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT): all personal loan accounts with default status (60+ days late)
Population register (BEF) for parent-child links
Income-tax register and other administrative registers on labour market history, income and wealth
Credit bureau bad-payer files (Experian, Debitor Registret), 2009 snapshot
Survey of 1,748 individuals on risk willingness, patience and impulsivity (2014)
variables: Outcome: child default on personal loans (60+ days late)
Key regressor: parental default status
Preference measures from survey (risk willingness, patience, impulsivity)
Controls: income, wealth, education, GPA
sample_size: 28,027,610 parent-child-year observations on 2,501,088 individuals
sample: All Danes aged 18–45 in 2004–2011 with at least one living parent, organized as parent-child-year cells.

definitions.definition: An individual is in default if at least one interest-bearing personal loan is at least 60 days late with payments at the end of the year, as reported by banks and other financial intermediaries to the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT); annual data 2004-2011 covering all loan accounts. Mortgage loans are supplied in separate files; loan type is otherwise not observed.
Alternative severity measures defining default at defaulted loan levels exceeding DKK 0, 10,000, 50,000 and 100,000 (the defaulted amount may reflect several smaller loans).
definitions.source_location: Figure notes (Panel B, defaulting at loan levels)

definitions.definition: Recorded in the bad-payer files of credit bureaus Experian or Debitor Registret (snapshot of persons registered in 2009); people can be recorded after at least three reminders and a warning letter, for at most five years per missing payment.

All individuals aged 18-45 in 2004-2011 with at least one living parent, linked via CPR to parents in the population register; unit of observation is the parent-child-year cell (separate child-mother and child-father observations; new partners of divorced parents ignored).

Unemployment spell of at least three months in event year 2007, 2008 or 2009 for individuals employed with no unemployment spells in the five preceding years, aged 18-38 at t-5; controls are similar individuals without a shock in t. Amounts index-adjusted to 2009-DKK within cohort.

Financial wealth = stocks + bonds + bank deposits; indicator for having financial assets at end of year below one month's worth of average disposable income over the five years preceding the shock year.

Ratio of parental financial assets to average disposable income for each year 1987-1996; parents are assigned to behavioural types by within-cohort decile of the average asset-income ratio over the ten years, used to instrument parental default in 2011.
Within-cohort deciles of grade point average from the 9th grade graduation exam in Danish and Mathematics, available for those completing 9th grade in 2001/2002 or later.
definitions.source_location: Section 3.2 and Figure on GPA deciles

definitions.definition: January 2014 telephone survey of 1,748 individuals asking respondents to place themselves and both parents on a 1-10 scale for risk willingness, patience and impulsivity; linked to register data.

authors: Raj Chetty, John N. Friedman, Tore Olsen and Luigi Pistaferri
title: Adjustment Costs, Firm Responses, and Micro vs. Macro Labor Supply Elasticities: Evidence from Danish Tax Records
summary: Uses bunching at kinks in the Danish tax schedule to show that observed earnings responses are shaped by search costs and by firms coordinating hours around tax thresholds. Once adjustment frictions are accounted for, the structural labour supply elasticity is around 0.3, far above the small elasticities from individual-level micro studies, which helps reconcile micro and macro estimates.
data: Income tax register / Income Statistics Register (IND)
Population register (BEF)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA) with firm ID and occupation
variables: Outcome: bunching (excess mass) of taxable income at the top-tax kink
Treatment: marginal tax rate changes at bracket cutoffs (tax simulator)
Key variable: firm and occupation-level bunching (hours constraints / firm responses)
Key variable: size of tax change across kinks
Comparison: wage earners vs self-employed
sample_size: 17.9 million observations of wage earners (6.8 million within DKr 50,000 of the top tax cutoff; 1.8 million self-employed observations)
sample: Danish wage earners aged 15–70, excluding the self-employed and pensioners, with self-employed studied separately.

definitions.definition: Individuals aged 15-70 in the tax register 1994-2001 classified as wage earners by IDA employment status, excluding self-employed, pensioners, wage earners with self-employment income and wage earners with unemployment; much of the analysis uses wage earners within DKr 50,000 of the top tax cutoff. Self-employed analysed separately.

definitions.variable: Tax simulator and marginal tax rates
definitions.definition: Authors' tax simulator computing tax liabilities and marginal tax rates from own and spouse's tax variables and previous-year municipality of residence; it matches actual municipal, regional, bottom, middle and top taxes within DKr 5 for 95% of observations.
definitions.codes: pnr, henv (spouse), glskkmnr (municipality), pfrdst, berfrdst (personal exemption), perindkp, berpi (personal income), kapindkp, berkap (capital income), lignfrdp (special deductions), kappens, fosfufrd (individual pension contributions), arbpen14, arbpen15 (employer capital pension contributions), underhol (alimony)

definitions.definition: Wage earnings from the tax register; net deductions = deductions minus non-wage income (accounting for spousal deductions), equivalently wage earnings minus taxable income; in the top-tax base, net deductions = wage earnings needed to start paying top tax minus the statutory top tax cutoff. Small-deduction group: net deductions below DKr 7,500 in magnitude.
definitions.codes: wage earnings qlontmp2; self-employment profits qovskvir, virkordind

definitions.definition: Excess mass b = number of individuals in a window around the kink in excess of a counterfactual density, relative to the average counterfactual density in the window; the counterfactual is a seventh-degree polynomial fitted to binned counts of the earnings distribution excluding a DKr 15,000 window centred on the kink (q=7, R=7).
definitions.codes: q=7 (polynomial degree), R=7 (bins on each side), excluded window DKr 15,000

definitions.variable: Firm bunching and occupation earnings modes
definitions.definition: Occupation-year modes = DKr 5,000 wage-earnings bin with most workers in each 4-digit ISCO occupation-year (occupation-years with under 7,000 workers excluded). Firm bunching b_F = excess mass at the statutory top-tax cutoff for workers with more than DKr 20,000 in deductions; individual bunching b_I = excess mass at the pension kink for the same group; compared across 2-digit ISCO occupations.
definitions.codes: occupation discok (ISCO 4-digit; 2-digit for Figure 18); deductions > DKr 20,000

definitions.definition: Cap on tax-deductible pension contributions (about DKr 33,000 on average) means workers contributing up to the cap enter the top bracket at wage earnings about DKr 33,000 above the statutory cutoff; bunching there is used to measure individual (job-search) bunching.

authors: Sharon Traiberman
title: Occupations and Import Competition: Evidence from Denmark
summary: Estimates a dynamic occupational choice model on Danish worker histories in which workers accumulate occupation-specific human capital that is lost when they switch. Occupations explain 57 percent of the dispersion in worker outcomes from trade, sectors only 16 percent, and rising import competition from 1995 to 2005 lowered lifetime earnings for about 5 percent of workers.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA/IDAS) with ISCO occupation codes
Firm and establishment statistics (FIRE, FIRM) for industry codes
Customs trade data (UHDI)
UN Comtrade (CEPII BACI), Danish national accounts, Danish CPI, LIBOR
variables: Outcome: annual salary income from November employer
Choice variable: two-digit occupation by sector
Shock: import prices / import competition by industry
Worker skill groups: low, medium, high education
Occupational tenure
period: 1996–2007 worker panel (tenure built from 1990–1996); import competition 1995–2005
sample_size: 18,513,301 observations in sample frame (33,502,593 in raw data)
sample: Danish individuals aged 23–59 in IDA, 1996–2007, used to estimate an occupational choice model.

definitions.definition: Two-digit ISCO (DISCO) code taken from the four-digit occupation code in IDA, using only codes whose quality flag indicates they come from administrative surveys or pension funds (not imputation or lagged information). Missing codes are imputed if the worker has the same occupation at t-1 and t+1, or from t+2 after a firm switch; managerial codes 10-13 are combined into one, legislators and military are dropped, and small occupations are merged by skill group (e.g. 52 into 51, 92 into 61 for all skill groups).
definitions.codes: DISCO/ISCO two-digit; quality flag codes 1, 2, 4, 10 kept; ISCO 10-13 combined; high-skilled merges 42->41, 52->51, 72->71/74, 81->82/83, 91->93 per Appendix table; 21/22 merged for low/medium skill
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix D.1, Data Cleaning: Occupations (and footnote 11)

definitions.definition: NACE 1.1 four-digit industry codes assigned to plants (FIRE; firm-level FIRM data used when plant data not available) and matched to workers, aggregated into four sectors: Manufacturing (incl. construction, agriculture, utilities), FIRE, Public Services (labelled Health & Education), and Other Services.
definitions.codes: NACE 1 2-digit 0-45 = Manufacturing; 64-74 = FIRE; 75, 80, 85-90 = Public Services; all remaining = Other Services
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix D.1, Data Cleaning: Industry (full mapping in appendix Table 16)

definitions.definition: Three skill groups from completed education in IDA: low = high school or short-cycle education; medium = vocational or medium-cycle education; high = bachelor's degree or more. Education is never allowed to decrease (higher earlier level imputed) and missing values are filled from the previous year, else the next reported year.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix D.1, Data Cleaning: Skill

definitions.definition: Tenure measured at the occupation-sector pair level, constructed for early cohorts using data from 1990-1996, and censored above at 6 years to keep the measure comparable across cohorts; tenure resets upon switching occupations.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix D.1, Occupational Tenure; Appendix model section

definitions.definition: Total salary-based income reported by IDA in November of each year, covering the worker's primary and any secondary occupation; all of it is attributed to the reported (primary) occupation. Hours are not used because they are often imputed. Deflated by the 2000 Danish CPI (1000s DKK).
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix D.1, Income; notes to Table A.7

definitions.definition: A worker is counted as employed in year t if employed in November of t (IDA November position).
Raw data are all individuals in IDAS aged 23-59 in 1996-2007; the final sample applies the occupation/education imputation and cleaning and drops workers non-employed for the whole sample period.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.7 notes; D.1

definitions.definition: Variety-corrected CES import price index per industry built following Broda-Weinstein/Feenstra (Sato-Vartia weights on the common set of goods, adjusted for new and disappearing varieties) from customs data aggregated to the country-product level; a similar index is built from Comtrade, and the geometric mean of the customs, Comtrade and national-accounts indices is used as the path of foreign prices.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix, calibration of labour demand side (foreign prices, incl. footnote 14)

authors: Thomas Epper, Ernst Fehr, Helga Fehr-Duda, Claus Thustrup Kreiner, David Dreyer Lassen, Søren Leth-Petersen and Gregers Nytoft Rasmussen
title: Time Discounting and Wealth Inequality
summary: Links incentivised time-discounting experiments to the wealth positions of a large sample of middle-aged Danes in the registers. Patient individuals sit markedly higher in the wealth distribution, and the association survives controls for education, income profiles, school grades, initial and parental wealth, credit constraints and risk preferences, which points to saving behaviour as the channel.
data: Incentivised online convex time budget experiment (February 2015) linked on CPR
Income and wealth registers based on third-party reports (1980–2015)
Population register (BEF) for sampling and demographics
Education and family registers
Survey of time discounting for the 1952–1955 cohorts at ages 18–21
variables: Outcome: individual's percentile rank in the net wealth distribution
Main regressor: experimentally measured patience (time discounting)
Controls: education, income, parental wealth, risk attitudes
Heterogeneity: credit-constrained vs unconstrained individuals
period: Experiment in 2015; register data 1980–2015 (wealth ranks tracked 2001–2015)
sample_size: 3,620 experiment participants (of 27,613 invited); 2,548 survey subjects in the 1952–1955 cohorts
sample: Danes born 1973–1983 who lived in Copenhagen municipality at age seven and completed the online experiment.

definitions.definition: In the respondent vs non-respondent comparison (2015 values), wealth = real estate, deposits, stocks, bonds, mortgage deeds in deposit, cars and pension accounts minus all debt except debt to private persons; tax-assessed housing values adjusted by the average ratio of market prices to tax-assessed values among traded houses of the same property class, location and price range. Robustness variants: market-adjusted housing; adding car stock (available from 2014); adding pension wealth; household-level wealth; liquid financial wealth only (stocks, bonds, deposits).
definitions.codes: Car and pension wealth only available from 2014
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A5 notes; Table A10

definitions.definition: Within cohort x year percentile rank in the sample; robustness versions use averages over 2013-2015, 2011-2015 and 2009-2015, and household-level wealth.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Figure A10 notes; Table A11

definitions.definition: Holding liquid assets worth less than one month's disposable income (measured in 2014 and over 2001-2015).
registers: Third-party reported wealth and income registers
definitions.codes: Liquid assets < 1/12 of annual disposable income

definitions.variable: Marginal interest rate (interest on marginal liquidity)
definitions.definition: From tax-authority loan-level data: interest rate per loan r = interest paid in 2014 / (0.5 x (balance end-2013 + balance end-2014)); only non-mortgage loans, minimum denominator DKK 1,000, rates censored at the 5th and 95th percentiles. For respondents with loan accounts the marginal rate is the highest loan-specific rate; for respondents with only deposit accounts it is the smallest account-specific deposit rate. Distribution: p5 0.00, p25 0.97, p50 6.25, p75 12.73 percent.
registers: Danish Tax Agency (SKAT) account-level loan and deposit data
definitions.codes: Non-mortgage loans; denominator >= DKK 1,000; censored p5/p95

definitions.definition: (Dividend income + realised capital gains/losses during the year) / market value of stocks, averaged over 2008-2014; plus an indicator for owning stocks during the period.

Parental wealth decile = parents' position in the parental wealth distribution measured within the respondent's cohort when the respondent was 18; initial wealth decile = own position in the within-cohort wealth distribution at age 18.
Gross income = annual income excluding capital income (DKK).

3,620 respondents (3,552 with controls) with full register variables; robustness subsamples: both parents alive (2,367); in labour force every year and never unemployed 2011-2015 (2,265); stable relationship status 2011-2015 (2,704); socioeconomic status never indicating poor health 2008-2015 (3,030). Inverse probability weights based on respondents vs invited non-respondents or vs population, using education-year dummies, income deciles, income growth, parental wealth, wealth at age 18, age, gender, single and dependent-children dummies.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Tables A5, A10, A11

definitions.definition: Patience groups by tertiles of the non-parametric patience measure with cut-offs Low [0.0,0.5], Medium [0.5,0.8], High [0.8,1.0]. Survey alternative (follow-up of 2,096 respondents) uses the 1973 Danish Longitudinal Survey of Youth job-profile question: average salary from start (low), low salary first two years then high (medium), very low salary first four years then very high (high).
Robustness replaces years-of-schooling indicators with indicators for 59 general educational subject groups (e.g. comparative literature studies, economics, physics).

authors: Anders Humlum, Jakob R. Munch and Pernille Plato
title: Changing Tracks: Human Capital Investment after Loss of Ability
summary: Uses quasi-random work accidents in Danish administrative data to show that injured workers enrol in bachelor's programmes that build on their previous training. Exploiting differences in how stackable degrees are, higher education moves injured workers from disability benefits into full-time jobs paying 25 percent more than before injury, and reskilling subsidies pay for themselves four times over.
data: Industrial Injury Register (Arbejdsskaderegisteret) / workers' compensation claims from AES
National Patient Register (LPR)
Health Insurance Register (Sygesikringsregisteret)
Prescription Drug Database (LMDB)
Education Register (UDDA)
Course Participant Register (VEUV)
Danish Register for Evaluation of Marginalization (DREAM)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA), linked to O*NET
Population register (BEF/POP)
variables: Treatment: work accident causing loss of earning capacity (vs. matched non-injured workers)
Outcome: enrollment in and completion of formal degrees and courses
Outcome: earnings, hours and occupation (task content)
Outcome: disability and other social transfers
Severity: assessed earning capacity loss and personal impairment
sample_size: 14,481 injury events (14,369 distinct individuals); 4,568 events (4,528 individuals) for workers with vocational degrees with access to higher education
sample: Full-time employed Danish workers (excluding military) who suffered an accepted physical work accident with positive earning capacity loss, compared with matched non-injured workers.

definitions.variable: Work accident causing loss of earning capacity (treatment)
definitions.definition: Work accidents recorded by the Labour Market Insurance (AES) that caused a loss of earning capacity, restricted to physical (not psychological) injuries, non-military workers, and workers with full-time employment in each of the three years before the accident. An injury qualifies for compensation if personal impairment exceeds 5% or earning capacity loss exceeds 15%.

definitions.variable: Injury severity (earning capacity loss, personal impairment)
definitions.definition: Earnings capacity loss = loss of earning capacity in percent as assessed by The Labour Market Insurance (AES); personal impairment = degree of personal impairment in percent based on injury diagnosis. Temporary injuries = accidents AES assesses did not cause permanent loss of earning capacity or personal impairment. Non-injured controls are assigned the injury year of their matched injured worker.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Table A.1, rows 26-28; temporary-injury figure notes

definitions.definition: Injured workers matched one-to-one to non-injured workers in cells of event year, pre-event occupation, age, gender and level of education (baseline specification 5); occupational earnings premium computed within Year-Occupation-Industry-Education-Age-Gender match cells.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Table C.2 and Figure C.1 notes; Table F notes

definitions.definition: Direct access to higher education through a high school diploma or a vocational degree. Travel time to higher education = shortest car travel time (minutes) from residence zip code to the zip code of the nearest facility offering a relevant higher degree (as in Harmon 2015), measured separately for Craft, Care and Other educational groups; imputed for non-access workers as a residence-zip weighted average.

Degree courses = formal education programmes in the Education Register (UDDA); non-degree courses = Course Participation Register (VEUV); courses classified as Basic (primary/high school), Vocational, Higher (post-secondary). Training rate = share enrolling in a higher degree within six years after the accident; participation flow = enrollment in higher degrees in the year; stock = accumulated enrollment. Reskilling (2SLS treatment) = pursuing a higher degree within ten years after the accident; completers vs drop-outs defined by completion within ten years.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Table A.1, rows 31-38; Section D.1; Figure D notes

definitions.definition: Effects on transfers (incl. disability and unemployment benefits) are scaled with transfer rates linked to the transfer codes of the DREAM register; education costs include tuition (~$16,500 per full-time student-year, from government rate catalogs) and SU and reskilling benefits; 6% real discount rate.

Physical ability requirement = standardized average O*NET importance of Static Strength, Explosive Strength, Dynamic Strength, Trunk Strength and Stamina. Cognitive ability requirement = standardized average importance of Fluency of Ideas, Originality, Problem Sensitivity, Deductive Reasoning, Inductive Reasoning, Information Ordering, Category Flexibility, Mathematical Reasoning and Number Facility. Physical jobs = physical requirement > 0.5 SD above the mean. Occupational injury rate = accepted (not necessarily compensated) work accidents per full-time employee.
registers: O*NET mapped to DISCO occupation codes; AES accident records
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Table A.1, rows 21-23; Section D.6.2 figure notes

definitions.definition: Hospitalisations (inpatient and outpatient) with diagnoses from LPR, contacts with primary-care physicians and specialists from the Health Insurance Register, and prescription drug purchases (e.g. antidepressants, painkillers/opioids) from LMDB, 1995-2017.
2008-2017: yearly number of paid hours. 1995-2007: yearly labor income divided by hourly wage rate.
Total labor market income, including bonuses, amenities, wages paid under sick and parental leave, and employer contributions to pension saving schemes.

2008-2017: yearly total labor income divided by yearly hours worked. 1995-2007: average hourly wage rate in the November job; reliable only for individuals working more than 20 hours a week in that period.
Number of consecutive years in which the main job in November is registered with the same firm identifier.
Labor market experience measured in years since 1964.
Dummy for work within the public sector, measured by 2-digit industry codes.
Dummy for union membership, measured by a positive deductible amount (union fees) reported by unions to the tax authorities.

Share of weeks within a year in which the individual (or the employer) received sickness benefit transfers; the sick-leave labour-market state is a dummy for more than 15% of weeks in the year on sickness benefits.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Table A.1, rows 18 and 43

definitions.variable: Labor market states (Employed, School, Sick Leave, DI, Other)
definitions.definition: Employed = full-time work while not in school, on sick leave or receiving DI; School = enrollment in a higher degree in the year; Sick Leave = >15% of weeks on sickness benefits; DI = any weeks in the year receiving disability insurance; Other = residual (mainly part-time work, other unemployment and non-participation).
definitions.codes: Sick leave > 15% of weeks; DI any weeks

definitions.definition: Debt = debt to banks, pension funds, insurance and financial companies, credit card debt and study loans in banks, divided by labor income. Savings = mainly liquid savings: bank deposits, bond values and value of mortgage deeds, divided by labor income. Property owner = public cash valuation of owned property > 0 DKK.

Years of schooling = prescribed years of study of highest completed degree counting from grade 1. Primary = pre-school, primary, preparatory courses or Danish language courses at language centers; Vocational = VET, qualifying programmes or AMU labour market educations; High School = upper secondary; Post-Secondary = short-cycle higher, vocational bachelor, bachelor, master or PhD.
Overall GPA = average of all grades given in grade 9 (compulsory) and grade 10 (non-compulsory), normalized to 0-100; Math GPA = same for the subject Math.

definitions.variable: Hospital visits and days in hospital
definitions.definition: Number of hospital visits (admissions, outpatient treatment and ER visits); days hospitalized, with admission and release dates for admitted patients and outpatient/ER visits coded as 1-day visits.

definitions.variable: Long-term displacement and manual jobs (mass layoffs)
definitions.definition: Mass layoffs defined as in Davis and von Wachter (2011). A worker is long-term displaced if he enters long-term unemployment (official definition: 52 consecutive weeks) within two years of the mass layoff; manual jobs = Autor-Levy-Murnane manual ability requirement > 0.5 SD above the mean; automation exposure = Webb (2019) robot exposure > 0.5 SD above mean; offshoring exposure = non-offshorability index (average of O*NET decision-making and face-to-face) > 0.5 SD below mean.
registers: IDA; unemployment registers; DISCO occupation codes

authors: Henrik Kleven, Claus Thustrup Kreiner, Kristian Larsen and Jakob Egholt Søgaard
