Children missing any outcome or control are dropped (missing parental occupation and education allowed), as are children whose parents were not in the population at birth.

Groups based on the parents' country of birth in BEF: two parents born in Denmark (reference), two parents born outside Denmark, one parent born in Denmark and one abroad, and at least one parent born in Greenland or the Faroe Islands. Origin regions: Middle East = MENAP+MENAT (incl. some North African countries, Israel, Turkey, Pakistan, Afghanistan); Europe split into Nordics, EU-15 ex. Nordic (incl. UK), EU-13 (incl. Cyprus) and non-EU (incl. Yugoslavia).
definitions.codes: Country list per region in Online Appendix Table OA.1
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix OA.1 and Table OA.1; paper Section II.A fn. 4

definitions.definition: A first-generation local is 'low income origin' if at least one parent comes from a country whose 1980 GDP per capita (World Bank, supplemented with UN data) was below 4,000 USD at 2022 prices. Parents with only continent observed are assigned by the majority in that continent.
Aggregate labour market income including wage income and profits from self-employment in the year the child turns 30, in 2013 prices (CPI-deflated). Also used as an income rank, IHS and log.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix OA.1; paper Section III

definitions.definition: Hourly wage from monthly hours and monthly earnings for employees in the monthly register (available from 2008; self-employed excluded), in 2013 prices. Jobs are excluded if the hourly wage is above 5,000 or below 30 DKK, annual hours are above 3,500 or below 7.4, or total wages are above 10,000,000 or below 1,000 DKK.
Not working for at least half of the year and not being retired (child at age 30; parents' years of unemployment counted over the child's first 21 years).

Yearly sum of all transfers primarily financed by government institutions, including all unemployment benefits, child benefits, housing support, student benefits and all public pensions, in 2013 prices.
Indicator equal to one if the child has ever been sentenced to prison, suspended or unsuspended, by the end of the year in which they turn 30.

Counts by end of the year turning 30 of guilty charges and of charges dropped without conditions or ending in a not-guilty verdict (following the Danish Institute for Human Rights 2022). Charges dropped with conditions (e.g. payment of a fine) count as guilty. Traffic Law (Faerdselsloven) offences are excluded. The share dropped/not guilty is computed among those with at least one charge.

For each parent: aggregate income (2013 prices) over the child's first 21 years; years of unemployment over those years; occupation as 2-digit ISCO88 of the primary job when the child is 21, with extra categories for retired, unemployed and unknown; and years of education when the child is 21 (UDDA, foreign education from the arrival survey, rounded to an integer).
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix OA.1; paper Section II.C

definitions.definition: Completed years of education by age 30 from the education register; foreign education of immigrants is registered on arrival via a survey, which causes missingness. Rounded to the nearest integer in regressions.

authors: Jonathan Gruber, Amalie Sofie Jensen and Henrik Kleven
title: Do People Respond to the Mortgage Interest Deduction? Quasi-Experimental Evidence from Denmark
summary: A major reform that scaled back the mortgage interest deduction for middle- and high-income households had a precisely estimated zero effect on home ownership. It did reduce the size and price of houses bought, lowered household indebtedness and pushed down equilibrium house prices.
data: Income tax records (incomes, taxes, deductible interest expenses)
Housing register (homeownership, property characteristics, home size)
Tax authority property value appraisals (for imputed rent and wealth tax)
Population registers with spouse/cohabitant and child links
variables: Policy: 1987 tax reform reducing the value of the mortgage interest deduction for top-rate taxpayers
Treatment: top-bracket taxpayers vs. below-top/middle/bottom groups (difference-in-differences)
Outcome: homeownership
Outcome: home size (square metres) and home value
Outcome: total deductible interest expenses (debt)
Elasticity with respect to the net-of-tax rate (1−τ)
sample_size: about 40 million individual-year observations; 34,440,869 observations in the main homeownership regression (below-top controls)
sample: Semi-balanced panel of Danish individuals aged 20–80 observed in every year 1980–1996, excluding children living with parents.

definitions.definition: Baseline measure from housing records (living in an owner-occupied home) validated against the tax-record measure based on housing wealth available from 1987, for the population above age 20; housing-register measure is slightly lower in level because it misses owners not residing in their owned property. A variant uses only 'clean' cases (defined in main text).
Area of the house in square metres used for habitation, from the housing register.
Appraisal of the property by the Danish Tax Authorities made for assessing imputed rental income and taxable wealth.
Interest paid on mortgage debt, consumer debt and other loans (all deductible), for homeowners; mortgage interest cannot be separated over the whole period.

A taxpayer is assigned to the top bracket if she or her spouse is in the top bracket, to the middle bracket if either is in the middle and neither in the top, and to the bottom bracket if both are in the bottom. Treated are those in the top bracket in every year 1984-1986; controls are in the middle or bottom bracket in every year 1984-1986.

(1 - tau) R, where tau is the marginal tax rate on negative capital income; the 1987 reform set this rate to 51 percent in all brackets (pre-reform top about 73, middle 62, bottom 48 percent in the average municipality), raising the net-of-tax rate by 81 percent for the top group, 29 percent for the middle and reducing it 6 percent for the bottom.
Individuals observed in every year 1980-1996 while aged 20-80 (entering at 20, leaving after 80), giving 7 pre-reform and 10 post-reform years; about 40 million person-years.

Very-long-run home size analysis uses a balanced panel of individuals observed in all years 1980-2011 (vs. main semi-balanced panel 1980-1996). Pre-trend robustness: group-specific linear trends estimated on 1983-1986 and residualized out.

authors: Esteban García-Miralles and Jonathan M. Leganza
title: Public Pensions and Private Savings
summary: A Danish reform raising the social security eligibility age, studied with a regression discontinuity in administrative data, increased contributions to personal and employer pension accounts when later eligibility kept people working longer. Inertia in previous savings behaviour and firms' default contribution rates are the key mechanisms.
data: Population registers (date of birth, demographics)
Labour-market and income/asset registers (tax-reported bank and stock balances, property values, pension contributions)
Monthly earnings register (eIncome / eIndkomst)
Voluntary early retirement pension (VERP) contribution and benefit records
variables: Running variable: birth date relative to 1 January 1954 cutoff
Treatment: higher pension eligibility ages from 2011 reform
Outcome: contributions to employer-sponsored and personal retirement accounts
Outcome: changes in bank and stock account balances and property values
Outcome: pre-tax earnings and monthly retirement age
sample_size: 40,042 individuals (analysis sample); 12,020 individuals (RD estimation sample)
sample: Non-self-employed Danes born within six months of 1 January 1954 who regularly contributed to the VERP early retirement scheme before the reform.

definitions.definition: Those born on or after 1 January 1954 learned in 2011 that their early retirement age (ERA), incentivized retirement age and full retirement age (FRA) rose from 60, 62 and 65 to 60.5, 62.5 and 65.5; those born one day earlier were unaffected. Running variable is birth date relative to the cutoff; RD sample is those born within 56 days (8 weeks).

Four cumulative restrictions: (1) Danes born within six months of the cutoff date January 1, 1954 (71,095 individuals); (2) regular participatory VERP contributors, defined as making contributions in 70% of pre-announcement years 2001-2010 (47,047); (3) balanced panel: present in the data in every year 2006-2018 (43,348); (4) drop the self-employed, defined over the pre-announcement period using Statistics Denmark's definition of an individual's main source of income (final analysis sample 40,042).
registers: Statistics Denmark main source of income classification
definitions.codes: birthdate within +/-6 months of 1954-01-01; VERP contributions in >=70% of years 2001-2010; balanced 2006-2018
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.1 and notes

definitions.variable: Contributions to employer-sponsored and personal retirement accounts
definitions.definition: Annual contribution flows to employer-sponsored DC accounts in levels (winsorized at the 95th percentile by year) and indicators for positive contributions to personal retirement accounts (also indicators for contributions of various sizes).

definitions.variable: Changes in bank, stock and property values
definitions.definition: Year-t minus year-(t-1) year-end values of bank account balances and stock market account balances (reported by financial institutions to tax authorities) and of property cash values as assessed by tax authorities; winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles each year (also 10th/90th).
Income on which individuals pay the 8 percent labor market tax, winsorized by year at the 95th percentile; 2010 prices, 5.56 DKK per USD.
Absorbing-state measure from the monthly eIncome register (2008-2017): age in the last month with positive earnings before earnings permanently fall to zero.
Annual Voluntary Early Retirement Pension (VERP) benefit payments.

All individuals over 18 are assigned to workplaces in 2010; individual contribution rate = employer-sponsored plan contributions divided by earnings; the firm default rate is the median contribution rate among the firm's workers in 2010. Predicted contributions = current earnings times the 2010 firm default rate.

Participatory VERP contribution in a year is measured as an indicator for making qualified (VERP) contributions to unemployment insurance (UI) funds in that year; VERP eligibility requires contributions in 25 of the previous 30 years.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.7 notes; Appendix C.2

definitions.definition: Baseline RD controls: indicator for being male, indicator for being married in 2010, and indicators for region of residence in 2010 (five regions: Hovedstaden, Sjaelland, Syddanmark, Midtjylland, Nordjylland). Regressions use separate linear polynomials in birthdate on each side of the cutoff with triangular weights.

Control group (born before cutoff): first spike = retirement age between 60y0m and 60y5m; second spike = 62y0m to 62y5m. Treatment group: first spike = 60y6m to 60y11m; second spike = 62y6m to 62y11m. 15.8% retire at the first spike and 10.6% at the second as defined.
Subsample of individuals who had used personal retirement plans before the reform announcement: those who made contributions to personal plans in two or three of the years 2008-2010.

Anticipation-period outcomes are averaged over 2011-2013 and pre-announcement placebo outcomes over 2008-2010; robustness uses stricter winsorization at the 10th and 90th percentiles; an additional robustness subsample excludes individuals with real estate transactions.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Tables A.5-A.6, placebo table notes

authors: N. Meltem Daysal, William N. Evans, Mikkel Hasse Pedersen and Mircea Trandafir
title: Do Medical Treatments Work for Work? Evidence from Breast Cancer Patients
summary: A Danish guideline change shifted which breast cancer patients received radiation therapy, giving quasi-experimental variation in treatment. Radiotherapy reproduces the survival gains found in trials and has economic returns: ten years after diagnosis it raises employment by 37 percent and earnings by 45 percent, undoing most of the post-diagnosis employment drop.
data: Danish Breast Cancer Cooperative Group (DBCG) clinical Breast Cancer Database
Register of Causes of Death
Register-Based Labour Force Statistics (RAS)
Income Statistics Register
DREAM weekly transfer register
Population Register (BEF)
Education Register
variables: Treatment: receipt of radiotherapy
Instrument: January 1995 DBCG guideline change expanding radiotherapy eligibility (diagnosed after 1995 x eligible group)
Outcome: all-cause and breast cancer mortality
Outcome: employment, annual labour earnings, gross income
Outcome: sickness and disability benefit receipt
sample_size: 2,823 observations (women)
sample: High-risk pre-menopausal women under 55 diagnosed with breast cancer in Denmark 1990–1998 and enrolled in the DBCG89 clinical trial.

definitions.definition: Indicator for receiving adjuvant radiation therapy, from the DBCG clinical Breast Cancer Database, which records treatments administered and dates of diagnosis and major interventions.

Instrument is the interaction between an indicator for belonging to the T95 group and an indicator for diagnosis in or after 1995. The comparison group consists of 'always eligible' and 'never eligible' women (eligible or not eligible for radiotherapy regardless of year of diagnosis); full analysis sample N = 2,823. Robustness drops women diagnosed in 1994, women residing in areas with pilot universal screening programs, or women with breast-conserving surgery.
definitions.source_location: Notes to Appendix Tables A4, A9 and Figures A4-A5

definitions.definition: Female breast cancer patients diagnosed 1990-1998 (26,900), restricted to DBCG89 trial enrollees who are pre-menopausal and high-risk, excluding always-eligible patients whose radiotherapy intensity changed, patients missing radiotherapy, tumour size or micro-radical removal information, and women aged 55+ at diagnosis (final N = 2,823).

Indicators for death from any cause and from breast cancer, using the exact date and ICD-coded cause of death in the Register of Causes of Death, measured for each year from the date of diagnosis up to 10 years after.

definitions.variable: Employed / unemployed / out of labour force
definitions.definition: Indicators of labour market status as of November from the Register-Based Labour Force Statistics, for each calendar year from diagnosis up to 10 years later. Non-survivors are assigned one for out of the labour force and zero for all other labour market outcomes.

Monetary outcomes are expressed in thousands of 2015 DKK; labour-market outcomes are averaged over 1-5 and 6-10 years after diagnosis; pre-diagnosis characteristics (employment status, labour earnings, gross personal income) are averaged over 2-4 years before diagnosis.
definitions.source_location: Notes to Appendix Table A1 and Figures A4-A5

definitions.definition: Transfer outcomes (any government transfer/any welfare, sickness benefits, disability pension) are indicators measured cumulatively within 5 (or 10) years after diagnosis, not as annual averages.
definitions.source_location: Appendix Table A3; Figure A4-A5 notes

definitions.definition: All possible interactions among indicators for: mastectomy, age <45 at diagnosis, number of positive nodes (0, 1-3, 4+), tumor larger than 50mm, and tumor removed micro-radically; plus separate indicators for age at diagnosis in full years, tumor size in cm, number of positive nodes (0, 1-3, 4+), micro-radical removal, type of surgery (lumpectomy, mastectomy, or lumpectomy followed by mastectomy), and chemotherapy type (DBCG89 trial arm: CMF, CEF, OA, tamoxifen regimens, pamidronate arms); and year-of-diagnosis fixed effects. Standard errors clustered by hospital.
definitions.source_location: Notes to Appendix Tables A2-A4, A9

definitions.definition: DBCG89 protocol (age eligibility <75 years). Low risk (as printed in the appendix protocol table): tumor <=5cm and positive nodes and grade I (if premenopausal); high risk: tumor >5cm or positive nodes or (premenopausal and ductal grade II-III). Radiotherapy indicated after lumpectomy, when the carcinoma was not removed microradically, and additionally for: age <=45 with >=4 positive nodes (until January 1995); premenopausal with positive nodes or tumor >5cm (from January 1995). Positive nodes = cancer spread to at least one lymph node.
registers: Danish Breast Cancer Cooperative Group (DBCG) clinical database

definitions.definition: Cumulative number of inpatient and outpatient hospital contacts from diagnosis until each year after diagnosis (separate outcomes).

authors: Tobias Renkin and Gabriel Züllig
title: Credit Supply Shocks and Prices: Evidence from Danish Firms
summary: Combines loan-level data on Danish firm–bank relationships with survey producer prices and export unit values. Firms whose banks were exposed to the global financial crisis saw loans fall and rates rise, and they raised output prices by 3 to 5 percent to generate cash, with smaller increases where demand is more elastic.
data: Bank account-level loan and deposit reports to the Danish Tax Authority (firm part)
Bank balance sheets from the Danish FSA (Finanstilsynet) and Danmarks Nationalbank monetary and financial statistics
Producer Price Index survey microdata
Customs export data for export unit values
Firm register
Accounting statistics (regnskabsstatistik) and VAT sales data
variables: Treatment: firm exposure to banks with high pre-crisis loan-to-deposit ratios
Outcome: producer prices (PPI) and export unit values
Intermediate outcome: firm bank loans and average interest rate
Heterogeneity: product demand elasticity
sample_size: 1,753 firms (213 linked to the PPI survey, 1,176 to export data)
sample: Danish manufacturing firms active 2005–2010 with at least ten employees and an active bank lending relationship in 2007.

definitions.definition: Share of wholesale-funded banks in the firm's 2007 loan portfolio. Descriptive bins: no exposure (<0.02), low (0.02-0.5), high (0.5-0.98), full (>0.98).
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Figure A.4 and Table A.2 notes

definitions.definition: Account balance as of December 31 summed over all of a firm's bank loan relationships reported by banks to the Danish Tax Authority, including regular and syndicated loans, credit card debt and variable-utilisation accounts (revolving loans, overdrafts). Mortgages are not included because they are provided by specialised mortgage institutions outside the banking system.

definitions.variable: Average interest rate on bank loans
definitions.definition: Because contractual rates are often missing in the loan micro data, the average interest rate is computed as interest paid divided by the average of current and lagged end-of-year loan balances (Equation 1); regression of it on the contractual rate gives a coefficient of 0.91 for rates below 0.1.
registers: Bank account-level loan reports to the tax authority

definitions.definition: Monthly transaction prices (DKK, incl. temporary sales and discounts) reported by firms in the PPI survey for products classified by eight-digit HS codes; baseline uses domestic prices only. Prices are quality-adjusted, monthly price changes winsorized at +/-1 log points, and the data converted to quarterly frequency by keeping the price in the first month of each quarter.
registers: Producer Price Index survey microdata (Statistics Denmark)

definitions.definition: Annual firm-level unit values for 8-digit Combined Nomenclature (CN) goods = export revenue / export quantity. CN revisions handled by identifying one-to-one, many-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many concordance sets between consecutive years; log changes computed over mapped sets (physical weight used if units differ); aggregated to firm-level 2-digit CN geometric mean indices weighted by year y-1 sales.

Starting from the complete 2007 Danish firm register, cumulative restrictions: active manufacturing firms (7,281); more than 10 employees (3,322); at least one bank connection (3,295); survival 2005-2010 (2,703); bank loans >100,000 DKK in 2006 and 2007 and 2007 loan-to-sales ratio >0.01 (1,753 firms; 213 matched to PPI, 1,176 to export unit values). Positive outstanding loans in 2006 and 2007 are required to compute the 2007 average interest rate control.
registers: Bank loan reports to the tax authority
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Table A.1 and Figure A.1 notes

definitions.definition: Broda and Weinstein (2006) CES demand elasticities. Baseline: 4-digit SITC Rev. 3 estimates matched to HS 6-digit codes (94% of PPI products; 98.9% after filling with 4-digit averages); for unit values, the volume-weighted mean elasticity within the firm's 2-digit CN cell (98.5% matched). Alternative: 10-digit HS estimates (86.4% of PPI, 96% of unit value sample matched).

Product-category-specific exchange-rate pass-through into domestic-currency export prices, estimated on 1995-2007 customs data at the firm x CN8 product x destination x year level, with firm-year, product-year and product-destination fixed effects and destination controls (real GDP, export, import growth, change in unemployment rate); 45 destination countries covering 89% of export value.

(sales - labour cost - purchases)/sales; alternative version additionally subtracts interest payments to banks from the loan data. Accounting profits are after interest, taxes and depreciation; total inventories include raw/intermediate inputs and pre-payments, final goods inventories only produced goods.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix table notes for firm outcomes by exposure

definitions.definition: Regressions include 4-digit NACE x year (or half-year) fixed effects; robustness with 2-digit NACE x year. Consumer packaged goods approximated by non-durable consumer goods industries classified by Eurostat Prodcom codes.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Tables A.4-A.5 notes; Appendix C.2

authors: Hale Utar
title: Workers beneath the Floodgates: Low-Wage Import Competition and Workers' Adjustment
summary: Follows Danish textile and clothing workers for a decade after the removal of quotas on Chinese imports, using within-industry and within-occupation differences in exposure. Earnings and employment fall persistently, job instability in services is the main adjustment friction, and workers with manufacturing-specific education rebuild human capital through further schooling.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA): person, establishment and job files
Firm-Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (FIDA) employer-employee link
Domestic manufacturing production database (VARES), CN 8-digit products
EU SIGL database of MFA import quotas (European Commission)
variables: Treatment: 1999 employment at a firm producing goods subject to MFA quota removal for China
Outcome: cumulative 2002–2010 wage earnings normalized by pre-shock earnings
Outcome: cumulative hours, hourly wage, employment and unemployment
Controls: 1999 age, gender, immigrant status, occupation, education, union and UI membership
sample_size: 10,521 workers
sample: All workers with primary employment in the Danish textile and clothing sector in 1999, born 1943–1982 (aged 20–67 over 2002–2010).

definitions.definition: Worker is treated if his/her 1999 primary employer domestically produced in 1999 (at the 8-digit CN level, per VARES) any good subject to the MFA quota removal for China; SIGL quota categories are mapped to CN 8-digit products (CN 1999) and firm ids are linked to workers through FIDA. Called CompExp^D in the paper.
definitions.source_location: ReadMe File.docx (variable definitions); working paper Section 'Data' (FREIT995) for construction

definitions.definition: Revenue share of domestically produced MFA-quota goods in the 1999 employer's revenue (CompExp^C / CAffW), used as an alternative continuous treatment.

All workers with primary employment in the textile and clothing (T&C) sector in 1999 (IDA November job) who were aged 20-67 throughout 2002-2010 (cumulative analysis: born 1943-1982). T&C in code (last-job NACE) is 6-digit NACE 170000-189999 before 2008 and 130000-149999 from 2008.
definitions.source_location: DataPrep.do (latc definition); working paper Section 'Data' and 'Cumulative Effects'

definitions.definition: Sum over 2002-2010 of annual primary-job (November) earnings deflated by CPI (2010=1), divided by the worker's pre-shock average earnings (normsal9699, the 1996-1999 average in the code; the 2015 working paper says the 1999-2000 average). Cumulative hours, total wages and personal income are built the same way.
definitions.codes: rsalary (joblon, primary November job earnings); rtotwag (slon, total wages from all jobs); rpersonindk (personal income); CInc=sum(rsalary*Dum0210)/normsal
definitions.source_location: DataPrep.do ('Preparation of Cumulative variables'); ReadMe File.docx

definitions.definition: Sum over 2002-2010 of annual hours worked in the primary job, normalized by pre-shock average hours (normHrs9699).
Number of years 2002-2010 with positive primary (November) salary; a worker with an end-of-November employment with positive salary is regarded as employed that year regardless of job length.

Fraction of working time spent unemployed within a year, in per mille (arledgr); cumulative unemployment sums arledgr/1000 over 2002-2010 (in months: *12/1000). The pre-1999 control is the cumulative sum since 1980 (sumgrad/1000).
definitions.codes: arledgr (per mille); sumgrad; unemp50: arledgr>=500; unemp10: arledgr>=100

definitions.definition: Built from the IDA primary labour market position pstill: self-employed, unemployed in November, retired/early retired, in education, outside the labour force.
Industry of the primary job from 6-digit NACE: manufacturing and service defined with different ranges before and after the 2008 NACE revision.

Annual benefit amounts deflated by CPI: unemployment insurance (arblhu), municipal sickness/maternity benefits (adagp), employer-paid sickness benefits (adagpagn), education allowance for unemployed (quddydl), other UI-fund benefits (andakas); UI benefit total = UI + education allowance + other benefits. Cumulated over 2002-2010 and normalized by pre-shock personal income.
registers: income register files (indk_unemptc.dta, indk_bentc.dta in code)

definitions.definition: Indicators based on the 4-digit highest attained education code in 1999 (dhf99), with explicit lists of codes classified as manufacturing-specific (MVoc) or service-related (SVoc) vocational education.
Job type of the primary job from the job-length category: full-time (incl. unemployment breaks), part-time and side jobs, unknown.
definitions.codes: joblength (jobkat): D_FT if 1 or 5; D_PST if 2,3,6,7; D_PT if 2 or 6; D_CFT if 1; unknown if 0 or 9

authors: Claus Thustrup Kreiner, Daniel Reck and Peer Ebbesen Skov
title: Do Lower Minimum Wages for Young Workers Raise Their Employment? Evidence from a Danish Discontinuity
summary: Danish minimum wages jump by 40 percent at age 18. Monthly payroll records for the whole population show employment falling by 33 percent and hours by 45 percent at the discontinuity, leaving total wage payments almost unchanged, with an implied employment elasticity between 0.6 and 1.1.
data: Monthly payroll records from the tax agency SKAT (BFL/eIndkomst) with wages and hours
Population register data at Statistics Denmark (age/birth date, parental background)
School performance and job information from Statistics Denmark registers
variables: Running variable: age relative to 18th birthday
Outcome: monthly employment
Outcome: hours worked and hourly wage (earnings divided by hours)
Outcome: monthly earnings
sample_size: 577,795 individuals and around 14 million person-month observations
sample: All individuals in Denmark aged 16–19 in a given month, Jan 2012–Dec 2015, excluding apprentices in main analyses.

definitions.definition: Monthly earnings from SKAT payroll records (eIndkomst) 2012-2015: records cancelled by corrections are dropped (korkod/ibertvirkidkod/referidkod logic), payments summed by person, firm and month (from the reporting period angivpernr) and then by person-month; non-positive values set to missing and values winsorized at the 1st/99th percentiles within event month (tline) and income year.
Reported hours summed by person-month from the payroll records; values <=0 or >1000 set to missing and winsorized at the 1st/99th percentiles within event month and income year.
Employed in a month if trimmed monthly payroll earnings are positive (non-missing).
Monthly earnings divided by monthly hours (felt_200/timeantF12), winsorized at the 1st/99th percentiles within event month and income year (an untrimmed version is also kept).

Cohorts born 1992-1999 present in BEF 2008-2015; event time tline = calendar month minus the month of the 18th birthday (month18=(yr18-2008)*12+birth month); estimation window keeps tline in [-24, 24].

When a person has payments from several firms in a month, the firm id, ownership form and main industry code are taken from the firm with the highest payment that month; firm information merged from the firm register file ES2015.
Monthly indicator equal to 1 between the start and end month of an apprenticeship agreement from Ministry of Education data (overlapping and nested agreements merged/dropped).
Mean 9th-grade exam grade from standard exams in normal classes, standardized within exam year (2007-2015) and split into deciles.
Completed (hffsp) and ongoing (igfsp) education codes from the education register for the year of the observation closest to the 18th birthday.
Average of father's and mother's wage earnings (loenmv) over the years the child is aged 12-14 (parents identified via far_id/mor_id in BEF at age 13), ranked into cohort-specific deciles.

authors: Gordon B. Dahl, Claus Thustrup Kreiner, Torben Heien Nielsen and Benjamin Ly Serena
title: Understanding the Rise in Life Expectancy Inequality
summary: Decomposes widening life expectancy gaps between rich and poor into changes in age-specific mortality and differences in survivability to each age. Lower survivability of the poor explains the entire rise in Danish life expectancy inequality; cardiovascular gains helped everyone, but lifestyle-related survivability diverged.
data: Population registers (BEF, FAIN): sex and age
Income register (IND): household income net of universal transfers
Death registers (DODAARS, DODAASG) with cause of death
US mortality by income from Chetty et al. (2016), IRS tax data
variables: Outcome: period life expectancy by income group
Income rank: household income measured two years before mortality
Decomposition: mortality changes vs. survivability
Cause of death: cardiovascular, cancer, lifestyle-related, other
sample: Universe of Danish residents 2001–2014, compared with US tax-return-based mortality data.

definitions.variable: Household income (net of transfers tied to age/pension)
definitions.definition: Individual income = total personal income PERINDKIALT minus public pensions (QPENSNY), cash assistance (KONTHJ/KONT_GL) and other transfers (ANDOVERFORSEL), with negative business income, negative capital income (after removing surplus from owner-occupied housing OVSKEJD02_NY/OVSKEJD07) and negative wage components added back; household income is the mean of own and spouse/cohabiting partner income (rowmean of inc and partner inc).
definitions.codes: PERINDKIALT, QPENSNY, KONTHJ/KONT_GL, ANDOVERFORSEL, NETOVSKUD_GL, FORMUEINDK_NY, OVSKEJD02_NY, OVSKEJD07, LOENMV, ERHVERVSINDK_GL, OVERFORSINDK, RESUINK_GL; partner via EFALLE (from 1986) / C_FAELLE_ID (before 1986)
definitions.source_location: Replication files/DKRepCode/CollectData.sas (income block) and CreateData_DK.do lines ~13-69

definitions.definition: Percentile rank (1-100, ties broken randomly) of household income measured two years earlier (t-2), computed within gender x birth cohort x year cells; mortality sample ages 40-100, years 2001-2014, collapsed to income tertiles for trends.
definitions.codes: laginc = hhinc[t-2]; incrank by gender birthyear year

definitions.definition: Underlying cause of death (ICD-10) from the cause-of-death registers: cardiovascular = I00-I78; cancer = C00-C97 and D00-D09; lifestyle-related = alcohol (K70, K74, K86.0, F10), smoking (COPD J40-J44) and obesity (E66, diabetes E10-E14); other = all remaining deaths. A Case-Deaton 'behavioural' grouping (diabetes E10-E14, suicide X60-X84/Y87.0, poisoning X40-X45/Y10-Y15/Y45/Y47/Y49, chronic liver K70/K73/K74, lung cancer C34) is also built.
definitions.codes: C_DODTILGRUNDL_ACME (DODSAASG), C_DOD1 (DODSAARS); ICD-10 I00-I78; C00-C97, D00-D09; K70,K74,K860,F10; J40-J44; E66,E10-E14

definitions.definition: Population from BEF (1986+) and FAIN (before 1986), years 1998-2014, ages 37+ (mortality analyses ages 40-100, 2001-2014); person-years after the death year are dropped (unresolved estates). Age-specific mortality by income tertile and gender is linearly trended across 2001-2014 to predict 2001 and 2014 rates.
Highest completed education HFAUDD lagged one year, mapped to ISCED: low = ISCED 0-2, mid = 3-4, high = 5-6.

authors: Mette Foged, Linea Hasager, Giovanni Peri, Jacob Nielsen Arendt and Iben Bolvig
title: Language Training and Refugees' Integration
summary: A 1999 reform improved language training for newly recognised refugees. A regression discontinuity around the cut-off date shows a permanent, positive effect on earnings that emerges after classes are completed, together with more schooling and a higher probability of working in complex jobs.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Income register (IND)
Education enrollment and completion registers
Crime register: charges and convictions
Population register (BEF)
Admission/residence permit register (OPHG)
Migration register (VNDS) and internal mobility register (FLYT)
Register for Labour Market Policy Measures (AMFORA)
Danish language training database (Danskuddannelsesdatabasen)
O*NET task intensities
variables: Running variable: date refugee status granted relative to January 1, 1999
Treatment: 1999 reform expanding Danish language training
Outcome: annual earnings and employment
Outcome: education, occupation task complexity, crime
Outcome (children): lower secondary completion and crime
sample_size: 8,558 individuals; children sample of 9,730
sample: Refugees and reunified family members aged 18–49 granted asylum in Denmark between January 1, 1997 and December 31, 2000.

definitions.definition: Number of days between the date the residence permit (refugee status) was granted (tilladelsesdato) and 1 January 1999; RD with triangular kernel, local linear, cutoff 0. Sample: refugees and family-reunified to refugees admitted from 1997, aged 18-64, restricted to age < 50 so they can be followed 18 years post-reform; Somalis excluded in main sample.
definitions.codes: day_nr = dofd(tilladelsesdato) - date('01011999'); keep if age < 50; keep if somalia == 0

definitions.definition: Annual first difference in cumulative labour market experience (ERHVER/1000 + ERHVER79) from IDAP, bounded to [0,1] and set to 0 if missing; first observed year uses the level. Separately, 'employed in November' = has a workplace ID (LBNR) in IDA.
definitions.codes: ERHVER, ERHVER79; emp = exper - exper_lag, truncated to 0-1; employment_nov = (LBNR ne ' ')

definitions.definition: Gross earnings = LOENMV_13 from the income register; welfare benefits = sum of cash assistance (KONTHJ), refugee introduction allowance (KHFLYGT), other assistance (ANDBISTANDYD) and integration allowance (INTGRAYD); all deflated by the CPI (PRIS112 from Statistikbanken) and converted to 1000 USD at 6.6 DKK/USD.
definitions.codes: LOENMV_13; UA_sum = KONTHJ + KHFLYGT + ANDBISTANDYD + INTGRAYD; DISPON_13

definitions.definition: Employed in an occupation with 4-digit ISCO-88 (time-consistent IDAN/AKM crosswalk) major group 1-5 is a complex job; employed (ISCO observed or employed in November) in other groups is a non-complex job; outcomes are cumulative years in each divided by years since migration.

Charges from KRSI and court rulings from KRAF restricted to Criminal Code offences (GER7 code starting with 1, or with 32 or 34); rulings with decision types 0, 413, 414, 514, 519, 550, 551, 555, 556 (non-convictions) dropped; shoplifting identified as GER7 code 1332515.
definitions.codes: SIG_GER7 / AFG_GER7 first digit 1 or first two digits 32, 34; AFG_AFGTYP3 excluded: 0,413,414,514,519,550,551,555,556; property_sm = 1332515

definitions.definition: Highest education HFAUDD from UDDA, keeping only education whose source HF_KILDE is Danish (codes 1, 4, 6, 13, 15) and excluding Danish language training (HFAUDD 1301-1305); mapped to main levels via UDD_HOVED_L1L5_K format.

definitions.variable: Language training and employment services participation
definitions.definition: Participation in Danish language training from the language training database (DKDB 1999-2003) within 12-36 months of admission; AMFORA spells with FORANST 128-129 (language) or 127 (social) classed as integration services, other FORANST codes as employment services; hours = weeks in spell x TIMERPU.

authors: Olivier B. Bargain and Anders B. Jonassen
title: New Evidence on Welfare's Disincentive for the Youth Using Administrative Panel Data
summary: Maximum social assistance for childless unmarried Danes rose by 55 percent at age 25 between 2000 and 2006. Only the low-skilled respond: employment falls by 2 to 3 percent and benefit take-up rises by 10 to 14 percent, two thirds through moves from work to welfare, and crime shows no discontinuity.
data: Danish administrative panel data on welfare benefit take-up, employment, earnings and crime (registers not named in abstract)
variables: Running variable: age relative to 25th birthday
Treatment: 55% increase in maximum social assistance at age 25 for childless unmarried individuals
Outcome: employment
Outcome: welfare benefit take-up
Outcome: criminal activity
sample: Childless unmarried young people in Denmark around age 25, with effects concentrated among the low-skilled.

definitions.definition: Individuals aged 20-29 (age measured in months, weekly panel 2000-2006) who are of Danish origin, have only basic education at the start and end of the year, live alone (not in a couple), have no children and are unmarried at both start and end of year; running variable is age relative to the 25th birthday.
definitions.codes: IE_TYPE == 1; edu (AUDD2015_L1L5_K from HFAUDD) == '10'; FM_MARK == 6; d_child == 0; CIVST == 'U'

definitions.definition: Weekly indicator equal to 1 if the person's DREAM weekly benefit code is a social assistance code.
definitions.source_location: baseline.do, 'Defining weekly ordinary employment (wage), earnings (wage2), social assistance (sa)'

definitions.definition: Weekly indicator equal to 1 if the person has any employment in the corresponding month in MIA (monthly A-income employer reports, linked to CONESR/RAS jobs), set to 0 in weeks with a DREAM code for study grant, wage-subsidy programmes or death.

Annual job earnings (LONBLB from CONESR 2000-2005, LOENBLB from RAS 2006) for each person-firm spread evenly over the months with MIA employment at that firm; weekly earnings = ordinary employment indicator x monthly earnings.
definitions.codes: lon_md = lonsum_se / ans_mia_md; wage2 = wage * q

definitions.definition: Monthly hours-of-work category from RAS (HELTID_DELTID_KODE) attached to months of MIA employment at the workplace, used for heterogeneity by hours.
Charges from KRSI 2000-2006 (one per person and case number), dated by charge date SIG_GER1DTO and assigned to age in months; outcome is any/number of charges by age month.

authors: Onur Altındağ, Jane Greve and Erdal Tekin
title: Public Health Policy at Scale: Impact of a Government-Sponsored Information Campaign on Infant Mortality in Denmark
summary: A nationwide campaign against sudden infant death syndrome, delivered mainly through universal nurse home visits, cut infant mortality by 17 percent in a regression discontinuity on population birth data. Effects were 11 to 14 times larger for low-birthweight and preterm infants and concentrated among low-SES families.
data: Medical Birth Register (MFR): birth weight, gestational age, parity, maternal age, immigrant status
Register of Causes of Death (exact date and cause of death)
Education register (parental education)
variables: Running variable: birth month relative to December 1991
Treatment: birth after the 1991 change in infant sleep-position guidelines
Outcome: SIDS mortality per 10,000 births
Outcome: infant and child mortality per 10,000 births
Heterogeneity: low birth weight, preterm, maternal education
sample_size: 568,106 births (SIDS outcome, MSE-optimal bandwidth of 52 months); 632,449 births for infant mortality (58 months)
sample: All live births in Denmark within the RD bandwidth around the December 1991 guideline change.

definitions.definition: Days between the child's birth date and 31 December 1991 (main tables), with treatment = born after the cutoff; local linear specification with separate slopes, SEs clustered by birthday. The setup file also defines a birth-month distance to January 1992. Births up to 2006 retained.
definitions.codes: dif = birthday - mdy(12,31,1991); setup: dif = ym(byear,bmonth) - ym(1992,1), treat = dif >= 0
definitions.source_location: 04 Tables_days.do lines ~38-42; 01 Set up RD data.do

definitions.variable: Infant and child mortality per 10,000 births
definitions.definition: mor1 = 10,000 if the child died (death register date) before the first birthday, 0 otherwise; mor5 = 10,000 if died before the fifth birthday. Deaths taken from DOD and linked to birth-register children.
definitions.codes: mor1 = 10000 if dead==1 & deathdate < bday_1yr; mor5 analogous with bday_5yr

definitions.definition: Primary cause of death (C_DOD1 in DODSAARS up to 2001; C_DODTILGRUNDL_ACME in DODSAASG from 2002) classified with ICD-8 before 1994 and ICD-10 from 1994; SIDS = ICD-8 795.0-795.9 / ICD-10 R95; per 10,000 births when death occurs before age 5. Other groups: infectious, neoplasms, nervous system, respiratory, perinatal, congenital malformations, unknown.

definitions.variable: Low birth weight and preterm birth
definitions.definition: Birth weight from MFR (V_VAGT before 1997, VAEGT_BARN after) set to missing if 0 or >9,000 g; LBW = <2,500 g, VLBW = <1,500 g; preterm = gestational age < 37 weeks (fullterm37 = 0). Gestational age only available from 1978 and birth weight recorded in 500 g bands before 1978.

Mother's highest education HFAUDD mapped to AUDD2008_L1L5_KT: basic (<20 or >=90), vocational/high school (20-39), short (40-49), medium (50-59), long further education (60-89); high education = short+medium+long. Couple = C_STATUS 2 or 4-7; immigrant = IE_TYPE 2 or 3.

authors: Ida Lykke Kristiansen and Sophie Yanying Sheng
title: The Physician-Patient Match and Health Inequality
summary: Measures general practitioners' childhood socioeconomic status from their parents' education in the registers. Low-SES patients matched to a GP of similar background have substantially lower mortality, while high-SES patients are unaffected, cutting the SES mortality gradient by a quarter through more intensive care, better detection of chronic conditions and better adherence.
data: National Health Service Register: patient-to-GP clinic assignment
Service Provider Registry (physician IDs)
Cause of Death Register
National Health Insurance Service Registry: visits, services, reimbursements
Hospital/patient data and first-line treatments for chronic conditions
Education registers and parent links (BEF/UDDA) for patient SES and physicians' parental education
variables: Treatment: assignment to a low-SES (parental education) physician after clinic closure
Outcome: patient mortality and cause of death
Outcome: detection/treatment of chronic conditions (CVC, cancer, diabetes, COPD)
Outcome: health care utilization (visits, services per visit, reimbursements)
Patient SES: highest completed education (primary school = low SES)
sample_size: over 352,000 adult patients affected by 894 clinic closures; 1,019,005 observations in the main mortality regression
sample: Danish adults aged 40–70 whose primary care clinic closed between 1999 and 2016, observed at least four years before the closure.

definitions.variable: GP visits and services per visit
definitions.definition: From health insurance claims (SSSY/SYSI), restricted to general practitioners (SPECIALE starting '80'), insurance group 1, own patients (PATTYP 1/01) and excluding child-vaccination/child-exam claims (BARNMAK = 1); visits = number of distinct provider x service-week (HONUGE) combinations per patient-year; services = count of service lines; services per visit = services / visits.
definitions.codes: substr(SPECIALE,1,2) = '80'; SIKGRUP = '1'; PATTYP in ('1','01'); BARNMAK ne '1'

definitions.definition: Total GP fees (BRUHON) per patient-year for SPECIALE starting '80'; amounts before 2005 converted from øre to kroner (divided by 100).

Annual indicators for redeemed prescriptions: statins (ATC C10AA), ACE inhibitors/angiotensin agents (ATC C09), diabetes drugs incl. metformin (ATC A10), COPD medication (ATC R03AC, R03CC, R03BB); diabetes checkup if GP claim with SPECIALE 800106, 800107, 800108 or 804549.

Underlying cause of death (C_DODTILGRUNDL_ACME, or C_DOD1 in older register), deaths from 1995: cardiovascular = any ICD-10 I; heart = I20-I25; acute stroke = I20-I25 or I60-I69; cancer = any C (lung C34 and other subgroups); diabetes = E10-E14; COPD = J44.
Hospital admissions (LPR, from 1995) with ICD-10 diagnosis J20, J21, J40, J41, J43, J47 or J44.0, J44.1, J44.9 as ambulatory-care-sensitive COPD admissions.

A GP is low-SES if the mother's highest attained education level is 10 (primary school), or, if not, the father's is 10; missing set to 0 with a missing indicator; clinic-level max/min/mean share of low-SES GPs computed by provider number and year. GPs identified as doctors in private practice (T_YDER) with HFAUDD 7170 (master in medicine).
Patient's highest completed education level (HFAUDD mapped to level) equal to 10 (primary school); separate indicator for missing education.

Patient-to-clinic spells built from weekly GP claims following Kjaergaard's algorithm (one practice per service week, practice-time intervals, intervals < 31 days dropped); clinic closure = last service week of the provider number (YDERNR), excluding cases where the same doctors continue under a new provider number (merger) and last dates after 2017.
definitions.codes: YDERNR, HONUGE; YDTYP == 5; YDLTID not in 2-9

authors: Anne Toft Hansen, Jonas Cuzulan Hirani and Miriam Wüst
title: Depressed Peers in Early Parenthood
summary: Municipal nurses assign new mothers to postnatal peer groups essentially arbitrarily conditional on a few characteristics. Exposure to a depressed peer raises a mother's own mental health care use by 11 percent two years after birth and worsens her self-reported mental health and labour market outcomes.
data: Municipal health visitor records with mothers' group assignments and EPDS postpartum depression screening
Statistics Denmark registers: GP consultations, psychologist/psychiatrist appointments, hospital contacts for mental illness, sick leave
variables: Treatment: having a peer in the new-mother group at risk of postnatal depression (EPDS)
Outcome: mental health care uptake in the two years after birth
Outcome: hospital visits for mental illness
Outcome: sick leave / labour market outcomes
sample: First-time mothers assigned by municipal health visitors to new-mother groups in Danish municipalities.

definitions.definition: Mother's own EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) score from municipal health-visitor records (first postnatal screening); high = EPDS > 10. Treatment = at least one other mother in the assigned mothers' group has a high EPDS score (leave-self-out group mean of high > 0); untested mothers coded as not high.
definitions.codes: high = (score_e1 > 10); peer_treat = (leave-one-out mean of high in group > 0); questionnaires 'EPDS gravide','EPDS nybagt','Edinburgh' variants

definitions.definition: Health insurance claims with SPEC2 = 80 (general practice) per service week (HONUGE); fees BRUHON summed by person and week (negative set to 0, duplicates by week x SPECIALE dropped) and by year of age relative to the birth; for children, contacts in the first 182 days after birth are excluded.

definitions.variable: Psychologist/psychiatrist consultations and GP mental-health tests
definitions.definition: Mother's claims with SPEC2 = 24 or 63 (psychiatrist / psychologist) by month since birth; GP contacts with a psychological test (code comment: test for depression/mental health screening) identified by SPECIALE codes 802147, 802148, 802149, 804106, 806101.
Hospital contacts with an action diagnosis in ICD-10 chapter F (DF00-DF99), split into inpatient (C_PATTYPE = 0) and outpatient (other patient types), by month since birth (admission date D_INDDTO).

Weekly DREAM codes for each parent from the birth week up to 5 years: sick leave if code 890 or 893-899; UI/other benefits if code 111, 115, 121, 151-153, 130, 133-139, 213-219, 299, 710, 713-719, 730, 733-739, 740, 743-749 (among others); 'working/self-sufficient' if no DREAM code in the week; parental leave benefit code 881.

authors: Magnus T. Buus, Jakob R. Munch, Joel Rodrigue and Georg Schaur
title: Do Export Support Programs Affect Prices, Quality, Markups, and Marginal Costs? Evidence From a Natural Policy Experiment
summary: Uses a quasi-natural experiment in the Danish Trade Council's export support to firms. Support raises firm-level exports within destination markets but leaves prices, quality, markups and marginal costs unchanged, consistent with firms growing abroad by shifting demand rather than changing products.
data: Trade Council export promotion records: firm purchases and Trade Council approaches by destination
International Trade in Goods statistics: Intrastat and Extrastat firm exports by CN8 product and destination (UHDI)
Manufacturers' Sales of Goods (VARES/Prodcom): firm sales by product, value and quantity
Firm Statistics Register (FirmStat) and Firm Accounts Statistics (FIRE)
variables: Treatment: purchase of export promotion services for a destination in year t or t-1
Instrument: whether the Trade Council approached the firm
Outcome: firm-product-destination export sales
Outcome: export unit values (prices), quality, markups and marginal costs
sample_size: 18,181 firm-years (manufacturing exporters in Prodcom data, 77 destinations)
sample: Danish manufacturing exporters with at least 10 employees present in the production data, exporting to the 77 destinations served by the Trade Council, 2002–2015.

definitions.definition: Dummy equal to 1 if the firm purchased an export promotion service from the Danish Trade Council for a given destination (or, at firm level, any destination) in year t or year t-1; multiple purchases within a year are not distinguished (collapsed with max). Trade Council records restricted to 2002-2015 with non-missing destination.
definitions.codes: treated=1 for all promodata cases, 0 for turned-down cases (tdc.dta); treated_2 = (treated_1==1 | L.treated_1==1)

definitions.definition: Dummy equal to 1 if the firm was contacted (approached) by the Trade Council for a destination, defined over both purchased cases and turned-down cases where contact was established but no support was bought; used as of year t or t-1 like the treatment.
registers: Trade Council export promotion records (promodata.dta, tdc.dta)
definitions.codes: tdcinitiative=1 if firm contacted by the TC; tdcinitiative_2 = (tdcinitiative_1==1 | L.tdcinitiative_1==1)

definitions.definition: Export value (1000 DKK) by firm, CN8+ product, destination and year from the trade-in-goods statistics, exports only. Quantity is weight in kg unless the supplementary unit is not kg, is unique within the product, and the value of observations with non-missing amounts is at least that with non-missing weights, in which case the supplementary amount is used; observations with zero/missing value or quantity are dropped. A variant keeps only flows above 7.5 (1000 DKK).
definitions.codes: ie=="2" (exports); value vrd, weight vgt, amount mgd, unit enhedskode ("00" = kg); vrd_exp_exsmall if vrd_exp>7.5

definitions.definition: CN8 product codes are made consistent over 2002-2015 by aggregating to CN8+ categories using the Van Beveren et al. (2012) algorithm; each CN8+ code is assigned the CN6 category with the largest Prodcom sales value.

Firm-years present in the Prodcom (manufacturers' sales) data from 2002, matched to FIRM and FIRE, in manufacturing with at least 10 employees year by year (employees >= 9.5), observed in FIRM in the previous year, and with positive sales, wage bill, capital and material expenditures.

definitions.variable: Capital, materials and wage bill inputs
definitions.definition: Capital is the sum of FIRE balance-sheet asset items, deflated by the gross fixed capital formation index (NABK69) by 69-industry; material expenditures are krh (2001-2003) or krhe+kvv (2004 onward), deflated by the intermediate consumption index (NABP69); the wage bill (lgag) is deflated by the CPI (PRIS112). Firm-level inputs and sales are multiplied by the share of Prodcom sales value with non-missing quantity.
definitions.codes: capital = iaat+grby+atam+fmaa+aadi; expenditures = krh (<=2003), krhe+kvv (>=2004); wagebill = lgag; sales = FIRM gf_oms

definitions.definition: Quarterly Prodcom reports of value and quantity per 10-digit product are summed to firm-product(CN8+ x unit)-year; missing firm IDs are imputed from report ID and alternative ID within 2002-2006 and 2007+ separately; observations with missing or zero quantity are dropped; firm industry is the DB07 code with the largest sales value.
definitions.codes: jurnr, rapport_id, saflbnr, varenr, vaerdi, maengde, mgd_tekst, fag_hoved_bra_db07

definitions.definition: Firm-product markups and marginal costs from the De Loecker et al. (2016) procedure: a translog production function estimated on single-product firms by 2-digit sector, with the original tariff controls replaced by the firm- and firm-product-level export support indicators; markup = output elasticity of materials over the materials expenditure share allocated to the product.
definitions.codes: outputs lmu_x (log markup), lmc_x (log marginal cost), theta_fjt_x; tau_in1=treated_p, tau_ou1=treated

definitions.definition: Trade Council support products grouped into four types: (1) partner search/matchmaking, meeting facilitation, networks; (2) fairs, PR activities, conferences/workshops; (3) intelligence/analysis, publications, market monitoring, customs/export/import information; (4) other commercial assistance, market entry assistance, trade-policy assistance; remaining products form a fifth group.

authors: Karsten Albæk and Bent E. Sørensen
title: Worker Flows and Job Flows in Danish Manufacturing, 1980–91
summary: One of the first uses of the IDA matched employer-employee data to measure job creation, job destruction and worker flows across Danish manufacturing plants. Worker turnover far exceeds job reallocation, and both are large and persistent at the plant level.
data: Plant-level data on all Danish manufacturing plants and their workers (register not named in abstract)
variables: Outcome: worker flows (hires and separations)
Outcome: job flows (job creation and destruction)
Replacement hiring (separations from and hires into existing jobs)
Business-cycle variation
sample: All individual manufacturing plants in Denmark, 1980–91.

authors: Lars Pico Geerdsen
title: Is there a Threat Effect of Labour Market Programmes? A Study of ALMP in the Danish UI System
summary: Exploits the timing rules for compulsory activation in the Danish unemployment insurance system to test whether the prospect of being activated speeds up exit from unemployment. Exit rates rise markedly as the activation deadline approaches, which identifies a sizeable threat effect of active labour market programmes.
data: Danish UI system administrative data (not specified in abstract)
variables: Outcome: exit from unemployment to employment before programme participation
Identification: legislative changes to the length of the UI benefit period before compulsory activation
Treatment: approach of compulsory ALMP participation (threat effect)
sample: Unemployed UI recipients in Denmark subject to compulsory labour market programmes after the benefit period.

definitions.definition: Unemployment spell = at least 15 days of unemployment within a given month; a spell is broken if the individual receives no UI for more than 2 weeks in a month or regains the right to a new UI period mid-spell. Exit is any departure from UI (employment, leave, social benefits, early retirement, disability pension, education) in the thesis version. UI days per month come from SSHS, built from CRAM (unemployment fund records).
definitions.source_location: PhD thesis (SFI 2003), Paper II, Sections 5.1-5.2, pp. 113-116

definitions.definition: Days in activation per month after 1994 from the Register on Labour Market Measures (AMFORA), based on the Labour Market Agency's Labour Market Policy Register (AMPO) reports of activation start and end; before 1994 from the Job Offer Data Set (ATB), 1980-1994.
definitions.source_location: PhD thesis (SFI 2003), Paper II, Section 5.1, pp. 113-114

definitions.definition: Months of passive UI left before the compulsory activation period, constructed by replicating the 1994 departmental order that placed each unemployed person in the new UI system (entitlement depends on prior activation, UI use and employment before 1994). Passive period cut from 4 years (1994) to 3 years (July 1996) to 2 years (January 1998); three expectation models (perfect foresight, system foresight, no foresight) for how individuals perceive the remaining months.
definitions.source_location: PhD thesis (SFI 2003), Paper II, Sections 2.2, 4.1, 5.2 and Appendix A

definitions.definition: IDA gives employment status in November and the number of months employed in the year; monthly employment is located in the residual months not covered by other monthly/weekly states (leave schemes, UI, activation, early retirement, social benefits).
definitions.source_location: PhD thesis (SFI 2003), Paper II, Section 5.1, p. 114

definitions.definition: 10% sample of the Danish population aged 17-67, panel 1980-1998, topped up each year with 10% of new 17-year-olds and immigrants; leavers at age 68, emigration or death drop out. Restricted to UI spells beginning between January 1994 and January 1998.
definitions.source_location: PhD thesis (SFI 2003), Paper II, Section 5.2, pp. 114-115

authors: Eskil Heinesen
title: Estimating Class-size Effects using Within-school Variation in Subject-specific Classes
summary: Uses within-school variation over time in the size of French classes, which Danish seventh graders choose between French and German, as quasi-random variation in class size. Larger classes lower French exam marks, especially for weaker students and boys, and marks in subjects taught in the regular class serve as a check on selection.
data: Administrative registers on 9th-grade marks and exam results, school attended, merged via personal and school ID numbers
Family background registers (parents' education, income, labour market status, family structure)
variables: Outcome: French examination marks at end of 9th grade
Treatment: French class size (school/year cell)
Identification: within-school year-to-year variation in subject-specific class size
Placebo/control: marks in other subjects taught in basic classes
sample_size: 6,507 students in 782 school/year cells and 375 schools
sample: 9th-grade students in 2002–2004 studying French at schools offering both German and French from 7th grade, with at most 20 French students per grade.

definitions.definition: Number of students with marks for the year's work in French in 9th grade, measured per school/year cell; sample restricted to schools offering French from 7th grade where at most 20 students attend French (so only one French class) and where some students attend German.
registers: Administrative registers on 9th-grade marks and school attended

definitions.definition: Examination mark in French at the end of 9th grade on the Danish 13-scale (values 0-13 excluding 1, 2, 4 and 12; pass at 6); marks for the year's work are not analysed. Cohorts finishing 9th grade in 2001/02-2003/04.

definitions.variable: Marks in other subjects (placebo and ability)
definitions.definition: Examination marks in English, Danish (oral, written, spelling), math (oral, written) and science; average mark computed over each student's non-missing marks. Academic ability dummy = average marks in other subjects at least 9.

32 variables for siblings, family structure, parents' education, age, labour-market status, income, unemployment and housing conditions, all measured in the calendar year the child turned 12; parental high education = at least one parent with long further or higher education.
registers: Family background registers (parents' education, income, labour market status)

authors: Martin Browning, Mette Gørtz and Søren Leth-Petersen
title: Housing Wealth and Consumption: A Micro Panel Study
summary: Uses register-based imputed consumption and house price changes over the 1987 to 1996 boom and bust to test whether housing wealth drives spending. For most households consumption does not respond to unanticipated house price changes; the response is confined to young households, consistent with a collateral rather than a wealth effect.
data: Administrative income and wealth (tax) registers for a 10% random sample of the Danish population aged 16+
House price / housing wealth information from registers
variables: Outcome: imputed household total expenditure (disposable income minus change in net wealth)
Key regressor: unexpected changes in house prices / housing wealth
Heterogeneity: age, owners vs renters, credit constraints (1992–93 mortgage reform allowing home-equity borrowing)
Disposable household income
sample: Married or cohabiting stable couples from a 10% random sample of the Danish population aged 16+, who were either homeowners or renters throughout the period.

definitions.definition: Household disposable after-tax income minus the change in net financial wealth from t-1 to t, following Browning and Leth-Petersen (2003); deflated to 1990 prices. Possible only up to 1996 because wealth-tax register data end after the wealth tax was abolished in 1997.
registers: Income and wealth tax registers (10% sample)

definitions.definition: Gross income including interest income, housing transfers and dividends, minus taxes on income, taxes on shares, surplus on owner-occupied housing and tax-exempted interest expenses (labour, transfer and capital income net of personal taxes).
Financial assets (market value of shares, bank deposits, market value of bonds and securities) minus debt (mortgage debt, bank debt etc.).

definitions.variable: Municipal house prices and house price innovations
definitions.definition: Average sales prices of traded single-family houses by municipality (275 municipalities), 1985-2001, collected by the tax authorities. Log municipal price modelled as an AR process with municipality effects, average house size (square metres, rooms) and year effects, estimated by system GMM; the predicted change is the expected price change and the residual is the house price innovation.
registers: Tax authority house sales statistics (Statistics Denmark)
definitions.source_location: Section 4 (House prices); Section 5 (house price process); Appendix 1

definitions.definition: 10% random sample of the Danish population aged 16+, 1987-1996; married or cohabiting stable couples who were either home owners or renters throughout; split before and after the 1992-93 mortgage/collateral and tax reforms.
registers: Income and wealth tax registers (10% sample)

definitions.definition: Liquidity-constrained households have liquid funds (cash and bonds) below 1.5 months of disposable income; high-liquidity households have liquid funds above half a year's disposable income. Mortgage sensitivity measured by mortgage debt / house value.

authors: Jesper Bagger, Javier A. Birchenall, Hani Mansour and Sergio Urzúa
title: Education, Birth Order and Family Size
summary: Develops a model of parental investment with birth order preferences and human capital cost differences that delivers a generalised quantity–quality trade-off. Danish administrative data confirm its predictions: at any given parity, children in smaller families have more education, and the average child's education falls with family size even after accounting for birth order.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA), 1980–2006, with mother-child links
Precise date of birth from Statistics Denmark (to identify twin/multiple births)
variables: Outcome: years of education (measured in 2006)
Key regressors: birth order and family size
Instrument: twin birth at last birth (twins at 2nd, 3rd or 4th birth)
Controls: parental education, gender, age
sample_size: 1,256,031 children in 581,159 families (excluding single-child families)
sample: Individuals aged 25–41 in 2006 whose mother was alive and present in IDA during 1980–2006, in families with completed fertility, siblings defined by common mother.

definitions.definition: Highest completed education in 2006 from the IDA person files (8-digit HFFSP code), mapped to years of education using the first two digits per Table A.1 (e.g. 10 = primary: 7 years if born 1958 or earlier, 9 years if born 1959 or later; 20/25 = high school 12; 35 = vocational 12; 40 = short further 14; 50 = medium-length further 16; 60 = Bachelor 15; 65 = Master 18; 70 = PhD 20; 90 = unknown, missing).

Siblings are children born to the same mother (families defined by mother's identity, via the IDA pointer to mother's person ID); family size is the number of siblings born to the same mother, recorded before individual-level selection. Families with children born after 1991 (any child aged 0-14 residing at mother's address in 2006) are excluded so family size reflects completed fertility.

Order of birth of each child within the mother's family, identified using precise date of birth obtained from Statistics Denmark and merged onto IDA (69.4% of IDA individuals matched, unmatched mostly older cohorts).

Multiple births identified from precise dates of birth (24,186 twin sets, 217 triplets, 5 quadruplets); twin observations themselves are dropped, retaining an indicator for a twin birth in the family and its order. Family size is instrumented with twins at the second, third or fourth birth in respective samples, and with twins at last birth.

Individuals aged 25-41 in 2006 linked to a mother alive, aged 15-70 and present in IDA during 1980-2006. Excludes families with mother younger than 17 or older than 49 at birth, missing education for any member, non-twin siblings born less than seven months apart, unknown or different fathers, children born after 1991, and single-child families; 1,256,031 individuals in 581,159 families.
Parental income measures are trimmed by recoding observations in the 1st and 99th percentiles as missing; mother's education measured in the last year she appears in the data.

authors: Jennifer L. Baker, Lise G. Bjerregaard, Christian M. Dahl, Torben S. D. Johansen, Emil N. Sørensen and Miriam Wüst
title: Universal Investments in Toddler Health: Learning from a Large Government Trial
summary: A 1960s Copenhagen government trial of preventive health care for toddlers, documented from handwritten nurse records and linked to the registers, improved a good adult health index by five percent of a standard deviation. Gains are largest for initially disadvantaged children and girls and fade for later cohorts as the counterfactual policy environment improved.
data: Transcribed handwritten Copenhagen nurse records (Copenhagen City Archives), 1959–1967 cohorts
Central Person Register (CPR) linkage
Education registers (UDDA)
Income registers (IND)
Death register
National Patient Register (LPR)
Copenhagen Perinatal Cohort (CPC), births 1959–1961
Family links to parents, siblings, children and spouses
variables: Treatment: born on the first three days of the month (extended toddler home-visiting trial)
First stage: nurse record contains a treatment table (take-up)
Outcome: adult SES index (years of education, post-secondary education, earnings and employment ages 30–50)
Outcome: adult good-health index (hospital contacts and diagnoses), mortality
Second-generation outcomes of trial children's own children
period: Births 1959–1967 (trial covered births January 1959–April 1968); register outcomes 1977–2020
sample_size: 87,336 individuals
sample: Children born in Copenhagen 1959–1967 with transcribed nurse records linked to Statistics Denmark administrative data, excluding twins.

definitions.variable: Treatment: born on days 1-3 of the month
definitions.definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the child's day of birth (from the transcribed nurse records) is 1-3 and 0 if 4-31; this identifies eligibility for the extended toddler home-visiting trial.

definitions.variable: First stage: record contains a long (treatment) table
definitions.definition: Indicator that at least one page of the child's nurse record is a long table (the trial's table with rows such as GP referral, nutrition, vitamins, illnesses, emotional problems recorded at 15, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months).
definitions.codes: has_long_table = 1 if any page type in 4, 5, 25, 27

definitions.definition: Annual wage earnings LOENMV_13 (negative values set to 0), inflated to 2015 prices, assigned by age (year minus birth year) 18-65, winsorised at 1% in each tail by age, and averaged over available ages 30-50 (also 25-50).

definitions.variable: Employment (average ages 30-50) and out of labour force
definitions.definition: Employment indicator by age from IDAP: before 2008 PSTILL below 40 is employed; from 2008 PSOC_STATUS_KODE below 200 is employed. Out of labour force (defined only from 2008) is PSOC_STATUS_KODE 300-517. avg_emp is the mean employment indicator over ages 30-50; out of labour force is measured at age 50 (and 55).
definitions.codes: PSTILL < 40 (pre-2008); PSOC_STATUS_KODE < 200 employed, 300-517 out of labour force (2008+)

definitions.variable: Years of education and higher education
definitions.definition: Latest available highest completed education HFAUDD (UDDA 2019 back to 1981), mapped to main level and normed length (months/12 = years). Higher education = KVU, MVU, bachelor, LVU or PhD; university = bachelor, LVU or PhD; above compulsory = anything but primary school (Grundskole).
definitions.codes: HFAUDD via AUDD_HOVED_L1L5_KT (levels 10 Grundskole, 40 KVU, 50 MVU, 60 BACH, 70 LVU, 80 PhD) and AUDD_PRIA_L1LX_KT (length)

definitions.definition: Row mean of years of education, higher education, average earnings 30-50 and average employment 30-50, each standardised by the control-group (not born days 1-3) mean and SD, set to missing if any component is missing, then rescaled to control-group SD 1. A labour market index (earnings at 25, average earnings 30-50, average employment) and an education index are built the same way.
definitions.codes: ses_index from edulen, higher_edu, avg_inc_30_50, avg_emp

definitions.definition: Inpatient admissions (patient type 0) from LPR 1977-2018, with nested spells removed; nights (V_BEHDAGE) summed per year, capped at 365, and summed over age bands 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59. Ever hospitalised = any nights at ages 30-59.

definitions.variable: Chronic diagnoses (diabetes, cardiovascular, cancer, asthma, infection)
definitions.definition: Action or secondary diagnoses (diag type A or B) in LPR 1977-2018 plus causes of death, treated as absorbing with onset at first year observed; diabetes uses ICD-10 only.
definitions.codes: Diabetes ICD-10 DE11, DE13, DE14; cardiovascular DI00-DI99 / ICD-8 390-458 (heart DI20-DI25 / 410-414); cancer DC00-DC97 / ICD-8 140-209; asthma DJ45-DJ46 / ICD-8 493; infection DA00-DB99 / ICD-8 000-136

definitions.definition: Any spell in the psychiatric central register (LPSYADM2016) starting 1995-2016; also records age at first observed contact.

Row mean of sign-reversed, control-group-standardised indicators of ever diabetes, cardiovascular disease, cancer, asthma, infection, any mental health contact and ever hospitalised (30-59), plus total hospital nights ages 30-59; missing if any component missing; rescaled to control-group SD 1.

Death dates pooled from the cause-of-death registers (DODSAARS2001, DOD2013, DODSAASG2017, using the statistics date if death date missing) and the Statistics Denmark death registers DOD2018 and DOD2020 (the latter without cause of death).

authors: Sarah Sander
title: Universal Daycare and Mothers' Working Lifetime
summary: Exploits the roll-out of daycare centres across Danish municipalities to follow mothers over their working lives. Daycare availability raises participation, hours and earnings sixteen years after the first birth, with effects driven by low-educated mothers and mediated partly through fertility and separation.
data: 1970 Census (FT70) with parish of residence
Historical daycare institution yearbooks digitised (1964–1975) and daycare institutions in registers from 1976
Population register with parent-child links and fertility histories (BEF)
Earnings from tax records (income registers), 1980–2015
Supplementary Pension Fund register (ATP) contributions for hours and participation
Education registers (UDDA)
variables: Treatment: daycare availability in the mother's 1970 parish after first birth
Outcome: labour force participation by age of first child
Outcome: log annual earnings
Outcome: weekly hours and full-time employment from ATP contributions
Mediators: fertility and separation from child's father
sample_size: 370,602 mothers
sample: Non-immigrant women resident in Denmark in the 1970 census who had their first child between 1964 and 1975 and stayed in Denmark until the child turned 16.

definitions.definition: Mothers are placed in their parish of residence in the 1970 Census. vg = 1 if a daycare institution for ages 0-2 (nursery or integrated institution, from digitised institution data) existed in the parish in the year of first birth; bh = same for ages 3-6 (kindergarten); availability is also tracked for each year from child age 0 to 6 (all/some/no years).
definitions.codes: institution number NUMMER < 120000 = nursery (vuggestue), > 250000 = integrated; parish (SOGNNR) x year; vg, bh, daycare0-daycare6

definitions.variable: Mother sample and timing of first birth
definitions.definition: Native (IE_TYPE 1) women born 1920-1959 with a first child born 1964-1975, aged at least 13 at first birth, with a 1970 parish observed and surviving until the first child is 16. First-birth year is the earliest birth year among children linked through MOR_ID (supplemented by family-register child counts).

Annual ATP pension contributions (sum of orer/100 per person-year) are divided by the full-time contribution amount for the year (194.4 up to 1964, 259.2 up to 1971, 302 in 1972, 432 in 1973-1981, 1166.4 from 1982) and capped at 1. Full-time = ratio of 1; for workers the ratio is converted to weekly hours as 9 + 26 x ratio. Measured for child ages 0-35; missing set to 0 if the mother is alive.
definitions.codes: ATP field ORER; divisors 194.4/259.2/302/432/1166.4 by year; full = hours>=1
definitions.source_location: dofiles/createfirst.do, '*ATP' block and final forvalues x=0/35 loop

definitions.variable: Labour force participation by child age
definitions.definition: For child ages 0-15, participation = positive ATP contributions in the year (hours > 0); for ages 16-40, participation = positive wage earnings (non-missing log earnings), set to 0 if missing and the mother is alive.
definitions.codes: work = hours>0; xwork = learn (loglon non-missing) for ages 16-40

definitions.definition: Wage income (LONIND, replaced with corrected wage income CORLOEN in 2010-2015) converted to 2016 DKK with fixed year factors and to US dollars (6.7327), negative values set to 0, top-coded at 400,000, and logged (also inverse hyperbolic sine); measured child ages 5-40. Gross income (BRUTTO) is treated the same way for 1976 onward.

Years of education (normed months/12) completed by the year of first birth, taken from the highest, vocational or general education fields with completion dates before the first birth (or inferred from age 5 + length), with self-reported sources dropped and minimum 7 years; grouped into basic (main level 10), medium (20, 25, 35) and high.
definitions.codes: HFPRIA, EKPRIA, ALMPRIA; HFAUDD, ERHAUDD, ALMAUDD; HF_VFRA, ERH_VFRA, ALM_VFRA; drop HF_KILDE in 3, 9, 10, 17, 18; H1 10 = basic, 20/25/35 = medium

definitions.variable: Separation from the first child's father
definitions.definition: divor = 1 if the mother's partner ID (C_FAELLE_ID) in the population register when the first child is 16 differs from the first child's father ID (FAR_ID); missing if father unknown.
definitions.codes: C_FAELLE_ID at age 16 of first child vs FAR_ID

definitions.definition: Number of children (more1-more4 indicators for at least 2-5 children) and time from first to second birth (space1-space3: second birth within 1, 2, 3 years).
From IDA labour market position, early retirement pension = PSTILL 50, 55 or 56 and old-age pension = PSTILL 92, 93 or 94; first year observed used to compute pension age.

authors: Petter Lundborg, Erik Plug and Astrid Würtz Rasmussen
title: Can Women Have Children and a Career? IV Evidence from IVF Treatments
summary: Uses success in in vitro fertilisation treatment among childless Danish women as an instrument for having children, since IVF success is unrelated to labour market history. Children lower women's earnings substantially and persistently, mostly through hourly earnings rather than hours, and the effect is much larger for the first child than for later ones.
data: IVF register held by the Danish National Board of Health (all IVF treatments in public and private clinics, 1994–2005)
Linked administrative registers on education, age, marital status and number of children
Linked labour market registers: labour force status, hours worked, hourly wages, annual earnings, occupation, sector and firm
variables: Instrument: success of the first IVF treatment
Endogenous treatment: having children (fertility at the extensive margin)
Outcome: annual earnings
Outcome: hourly wages and hours worked / employment
Mechanisms: occupation, sector and firm changes
sample_size: 18,538 treated women
sample: Childless women entering their first IVF treatment with embryo implants between 1995 and 2005.
