definitions.definition: Equals 1 if the first IVF treatment with embryo implants (in a sequence of treatments) led to a childbirth, 0 otherwise; treatment outcome (birth, abortion, stillbirth, failure) and dates from the IVF register (mandatory reporting 1994-2005).
registers: IVF register (Danish National Board of Health)

definitions.definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the woman has children and 0 otherwise, measured over periods t = 0-1, 2-5 and 6-10 after the (potential) childbirth.

definitions.variable: IVF sample and potential childbirth year
definitions.definition: Treatment success is measured at the first IVF treatment with embryo implant; t=0 is the year of (potential) childbirth. All regressions control for age at first IVF treatment, year of first IVF treatment, and pre-treatment education and earnings; pre-treatment baseline means are taken over years 1-4 before the first IVF treatment. Four samples: (i) IVF-treated women without children (baseline); (ii) IVF-treated women with children; (iii) successfully treated women with at least two embryos implanted (twin strategy); (iv) representative sample of women with a first child born 1995-2005. Balanced-panel robustness sample also used.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix A, B (Table 2 notes), D, E

definitions.definition: Annual labour earnings from tax and employer-employee registers, including parental leave and sickness benefits, in 2008 DKK.

Dummies for any workplace change and any (four-digit) occupation change in the short, medium and long run; job characteristics are averages of earnings, hours and log hourly wages by workplace and four-digit occupation over the study period computed in a representative sample of Danish women, plus workplace percent female, public sector and home-work distance.
Measured as antidepressant medication use (data complete only from 1994 onward).

Sensitivity specification adds medical factors from the IVF register: number of eggs retrieved, number of embryos implanted, diagnoses, causes of infertility, type of IVF treatment, and clinic indicators. A 'healthy women' subsample consists of women not diagnosed with any fertility problem.
registers: IVF register (Danish National Board of Health)

definitions.definition: Main wage regressions condition on observing positive wages; robustness extends the sample to all women by setting missing wages to 0.

definitions.variable: Pre-treatment sickness benefits and positive earnings
definitions.definition: Pre-treatment balance covariates measured the year before IVF treatment: years of schooling, annual earnings (100,000 DKK), sickness benefit receipt, marriage, indicator for positive earnings, and partner's schooling and earnings.

authors: Steffen Andersen, Cristian Badarinza, Lu Liu, Julie Marx and Tarun Ramadorai
title: Reference Dependence in the Housing Market
summary: Combines Danish housing listings and transactions with register data on owners to estimate a structural model of listing and sale decisions with loss aversion and financial constraints. Households derive utility from gains over the original purchase price and weigh losses about 2.5 times more than gains, which helps explain the co-movement of house prices and turnover.
data: Property ownership and transaction register from SKAT and the Building and Housing Register (BBR), 1992–2016
Tax-assessed property values (SKAT)
Property listings data from RealView, 2008–2016
Loan-level mortgage data from Danmarks Nationalbank, 2009–2016
Civil Registration System (CPR/BEF) for demographics and household links
Income and wealth records from SKAT (IND/formue)
variables: Outcome: listing decision and listing premium relative to hedonic value
Main regressor: potential gain or loss relative to original purchase price (reference point)
Potential home equity relative to down-payment constraint
Expected house value from hedonic pricing model
Structural parameter: loss aversion
sample_size: 214,103 listings (191,507 unique households, 178,933 unique properties); housing stock of 5,538,052 observations of 807,345 properties
sample: Listings of Danish owner-occupied housing between 2009 and 2016, both sold and retracted, matched to mortgages and household finances.

definitions.definition: ln(P_it) regressed on time x municipality effects, apartment indicator, and property characteristics: ln(lot size), ln(interior size), number of rooms, bathrooms, showers, unoccupied-at-sale dummy, ln(building age), rural dummy, historic-building dummy, ln(distance to nearest major city), all interacted with the apartment indicator, plus a third-order polynomial of the previous-year (biennial) SKAT tax-assessed value. R2 = 0.88 on sold listings (N = 114,303). Variants add repeat-sales residuals and lagged renovation deductions.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix C.1; Figure L.4 notes; E

definitions.definition: l = ln(L) - predicted ln(P), where L is the initial listing price and predicted ln(P) is from the hedonic model.
G = predicted ln(P) - ln(R), where R is the nominal original purchase price of the property; measurable only for properties bought in 1992 or later.

H = predicted ln(P) - ln(M), where M is the outstanding mortgage balance reported by the household's mortgage bank that year (multiple mortgages on a property summed; LTV and rate weighted); sellers with H < 20% are classed as potentially facing a binding down-payment constraint.

From 615,040 RealView listings of owner-occupied housing (excluding cooperative housing): drop unmatched in registers (-107,679), no reference price i.e. purchased before 1992 (-144,962), owner ID not uniquely determined (-71,876), non-household buyer i.e. government/company/organization (-10,382), foreclosures (-6,416), extreme prices (<100,000 DKK or >20,000,000 DKK in 2015 prices, or flagged extreme by Statistics Denmark; -5,499), owner ID not found, missing lot size or hedonic characteristics, listing date before previous purchase date, intra-family/special-circumstance sales, missing listing price; then drop summer houses (-24,098) and professional investors owning more than 3 properties (-18,312). Final: 214,103 listings 2009-2016 (172,225 with mortgage, 41,878 without), 191,507 households, 178,933 properties; 70.4% sold, 29.6% retracted. Extensive-margin stock sample: 5,538,052 observations of 807,345 properties.
definitions.codes: price bounds 100,000-20,000,000 DKK (2015 prices); >3 properties = investor
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix C.5 and Table L.1

definitions.definition: Households consist of one or two adults and any children below age 25 living at the same address, linked via the CPR family identification number; individual income and wealth are aggregated to the household. Household education = average years of education across all adults in the household; household age = average age in the household. The seller is the owner (CPR) at the beginning of the year of the transaction.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix C.1, C.4 (fn 5), Figure L.29 notes

definitions.definition: Danmarks Nationalbank loan-level mortgage data (via Finance Denmark), annual 2009-2016, covering all mortgage banks: principal, outstanding balance, LTV and interest rate, with borrower CPR and property number. Multiple mortgages on a property are summed, with balance-weighted average interest rate and LTV.

Proxy for maintenance/renovation: claimed BoligJob ('Boligjobordningen') tax deductions for labour costs of service work in the home, available from 2011, aggregated by household and linked to the seller; maximum 15,000 DKK per adult 2011-2015, then 12,000 DKK for maintenance/renovation and 6,000 DKK for other services (2016-2018). Used as 1-year lag (2012-2016) and 3- and 5-year cumulative lags.

Liquid financial assets = cash, stocks and bonds; net financial assets = liquid financial assets minus short-term non-mortgage liabilities (mainly unsecured debt). Used as household controls with age and education length.

definitions.variable: Share of apartments and row houses (IV)
definitions.definition: Instrument: share of apartments and row houses (as defined in the BBR) listed in a given sub-market (municipality), capturing homogeneity of the housing stock.

authors: Mathias Fjællegaard Jensen and Ning Zhang
title: Effects of Parental Death on Labor Market Outcomes
summary: Uses sudden first parental deaths and matched controls in Danish administrative data. Earnings fall by about 2 percent for men and 3 percent for women, mental health worsens for both, and women with young children lose the most, around 4 percent, consistent with the loss of informal childcare from grandparents.
data: Cause of death registers (DODSAARS/DODSAARG)
Population register with parent-child links (BEF)
Income and labour market registers (IND, AKM, IDAS/IDAN/IDAP), ATP-based hours proxy
Health Insurance Register for GP/psychologist/psychiatrist visits (SYSI/SSSY)
National Patient Register (LPR_ADM/LPR_DIAG)
Psychiatric Central Research Register (PSYK_ADM/PSYK_DIAG)
Prescription register (LMDB)
Childcare registers (DAGI/BOERNFB)
variables: Treatment: first sudden parental death (heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, acute respiratory infection, accidents)
Outcome: annual earnings (indexed to pre-death gender mean)
Outcome: employment and hours proxy
Outcome: mental health care use and prescriptions
Control group: matched not-yet-treated individuals
sample_size: Treated: 21919 daughters and 24354 sons whose mother died first; 74991 daughters and 85022 sons whose father died first (plus matched controls)
sample: Danish adults aged 25–50 with two known parents who experienced a sudden first parental death between 1985 and 2014, with matched controls.

definitions.definition: Sudden deaths = deaths from heart diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, and traffic or other (external) accidents; non-sudden = all remaining causes. Sample: first parental deaths 1985-2014 for children aged 25-50 in the year of the first parental death with two known parents.
definitions.codes: cause categories only (no ICD list given in appendix); child age 25-50; deaths 1985-2014
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Figure B.2 and B.5 notes

definitions.definition: Alternative control group following Fadlon and Nielsen (2021): individuals treated 6 years later serve as controls. Spillover analysis on in-laws restricts to married/cohabiting individuals matched to married/cohabiting controls who lose no parent-in-law in the window, also matching on whether own parents are alive. SEs clustered at individual-by-match ID.
Earnings from employment and self-employment, inflated to 2020 levels and indexed by the average earnings of men (women) one year before the parental death.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Figure B.5 and B.9 notes

definitions.definition: Participation = strictly positive ATP pension contributions; intensive margin = amount of ATP contributions (paid proportionally to hours worked), following Kleven, Landais and Sogaard (2019).
Psychologist visit data available 1990-2019; GP visits also used as an outcome.
Any prescription classified as mental-health related: ATC codes N05*, N06A*, N06B*, N06C*. Prescription data available from 1995; effects measured within 5 years after first parental death.
Opioid painkillers: ATC N02A*; prescriptions for treatment of alcohol addiction: ATC N07BB. Prescription data from 1995.

In- and outpatient visits at non-psychiatric hospital wards (data 1994-2018). Split into self-screening visits, defined by ICD-10 Z00 (general examination and investigation of persons without complaint and reported diagnosis) and Z01 (other special examinations and investigations of persons without complaint or reported diagnosis), including subcategories, versus non-screening diagnoses. Surviving parent's health status is based on their hospital visits in the 5 years before the first parental death.
definitions.source_location: Supplemental Appendix Figures B.10, B.11, B.15 notes

definitions.definition: Uptake of formal childcare for children under age 5 and above age 5; only 2005-2019 used due to low coverage before 2005.
Four categories: same municipality (99 municipalities); same NUTS3 region but not municipality (11 NUTS3 regions); same NUTS2 region but not NUTS3 (5 NUTS2 regions); greater distance.

authors: Kenneth Gillingham, Fedor Iskhakov, Anders Munk-Nielsen, John Rust and Bertel Schjerning
title: Equilibrium Trade in Automobiles
summary: Develops and estimates a dynamic equilibrium model of the market for new and used cars with heterogeneous households on the universe of Danish car ownership records, which record every vehicle's owner, age and scrappage. The model is used to evaluate Denmark's very high registration taxes and fuel taxes, showing how tax changes propagate through used-car prices and the age distribution of the fleet.
data: Car ownership register covering all privately owned cars (Statistics Denmark extract)
Odometer readings from mandatory vehicle inspections (driving)
Demographic and income registers for all Danish households
Tax deduction for commuting distance (work distance)
Fuel prices from eof.dk
variables: Outcome: car ownership transitions (keep, trade, buy new, scrap)
Car types: four classes by weight and fuel efficiency, 25 age groups
Household types: couple/single, high/low income, high/low work distance
Outcome: kilometres driven
Policy variable: new car registration tax and fuel tax
sample_size: nearly 39 million observations on car ownership transitions
sample: All Danish households and all cars owned by private individuals, 1996–2008.

definitions.definition: Cars are split by whether weight is above or below the median for the car's vintage cohort, then within each half by whether fuel efficiency is above (green) or below (brown) the median, giving four types; attributes are averaged within type. Cars are grouped into 25 age groups from new to 24+ years (cars over 22 years dropped from estimation).
Eight household types from couple vs single, high vs low work distance, and high vs low income, where the income split is at the median income within the demographic cell.

Based on the Danish tax deduction for travel distance to work, which applies only to full-time workers living more than 12 km (each way) from their workplace; households with the deduction are classed as high work distance (slightly under half of Danes).
Driving measured from odometer readings recorded at mandatory vehicle inspections, which occur biannually from car age 4 (ages 4, 6, 8, 10, ...).

Scrappage is not observed directly: a vehicle is defined as scrapped if an ownership spell ends and no other ownership spell ever begins afterwards (ownership register extract from September 2011, last sample year 2008, so at least about 3 years without an owner). Accidents are not observed.
T(P) = 1.25 x [tau1 x min(P, K) + tau2 x max(P - K, 0)], with 25% VAT on the price including tax; in 2008 K = DKK 81,000, tau1 = 105% and tau2 = 180%. Fuel prices are country averages from eof.dk.
Universe of Danish households and all privately owned cars, 1996-2008 (estimation on holdings 1997-2008, about 39 million household-year observations of car ownership transitions).

authors: Giacomo De Giorgi, Anders Frederiksen and Luigi Pistaferri
title: Consumption Network Effects
summary: Measures household consumption from Danish tax records on income and assets and defines peer groups by workplace using matched employer-employee data. Instrumenting peers' consumption with shocks to their own non-overlapping networks and firms, the paper finds sizeable consumption spillovers that can generate macro multipliers, operating through both intertemporal and intratemporal channels.
data: Administrative income and wealth tax records (tax registry incl. wealth tax data)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA) for plant IDs and coworker networks
Danish Expenditure Survey (DES) 1994–1996
variables: Outcome: household consumption imputed from income and change in assets
Endogenous regressor: average consumption of coworkers' households (peer consumption)
Instruments: firm-level shocks to distance-3 (non-overlapping) network members
Network definition: coworkers in the same plant
Mechanisms: budget shares of visible goods (DES)
sample_size: 757,439 households
sample: Danish households with head aged 18–65 where both spouses are working employees, linked to spouses' coworkers.

definitions.definition: Annual household consumption (spending) imputed from the budget constraint as C = Y - T - dA, where Y = gross income from all sources (labour and capital) + housing support + child support - implicit tax on the consumption value of owned housing, T = total taxes paid, and dA = change in assets (cash, bank deposits, stocks and shares, property value, cars and other vehicles, minus liabilities). Values in 2000 DKr.
registers: Tax records (income and wealth tax data)

definitions.definition: Co-workers are individuals working in the same plant (for public employees, the physical address of the workplace) from IDA. Baseline weights favour similar workers: with five education groups and three occupation groups (blue collar, white collar, manager), degree of separation d = |E_i - E_j| + |O_i - O_j| and weight (d+1)^-2; peers' consumption is the weighted average of co-workers' household log consumption.

Starting from households where both spouses work, distance-1 peers are co-workers, distance-2 peers are the working spouses of co-workers, and distance-3 peers are the co-workers of the spouses of co-workers. Couples working in the same plant are excluded and feedback cases (where own household would serve as instrument for the peer) are discarded.

Weighted averages over distance-3 peers of their firm's size, firm-specific change in employment, firm type dummies (publicly traded, limited liability, other) and a public-sector dummy, all expressed in first differences. A separate set uses distance-3 peers' demographics (age, age squared, years of schooling, share women, occupation shares, kids 0-6 and 7-13).

Households 1980-1996 whose head is aged 18-65 and where both spouses work as employees (not self-employed); households are dropped from the year one or both members stop working or become self-employed. Peers' consumption is computed using all workers, including singles and one-earner households.
definitions.source_location: Section 2.1; Online Appendix Table A1 (selection steps)

definitions.definition: Spending in the Danish Expenditure Survey is split using the Heffetz (2011) visibility index: visible = tobacco and alcohol, food away from home, clothing, furniture and home goods, electrics/appliances, vehicles, entertainment, books, education, personal care; neutral = food at home; everything else (insurance, rent, etc.) non-visible.

authors: Wolfgang Keller and Hale Utar
title: Globalization, Gender, and the Family
summary: Men and women hit by the same import shock from China adjust differently. Women in their late thirties who are displaced respond by having a child, especially high earners and those who would need to retrain, so a gender-neutral trade shock produces a long-run gender gap through the biological clock.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Central Population Register (CPR/BEF) for births, marriages, divorces and cohabitation
Domestic production database by 10-digit product (Industrial commodity statistics, VARS) to identify firms making quota goods
Industry-level imports from China and other advanced countries (instrument)
Parental leave records
variables: Outcome: new births, marriage, divorce, parental leave
Outcome: earnings, hours, unemployment
Treatment: 1999 employer produces goods subject to MFA quota removal for China after WTO entry
Treatment (economy-wide): industry import penetration from China, instrumented with other countries' imports
Heterogeneity: gender and age (biological clock)
sample_size: about 1,600,000 workers; about 10,000 textile and clothing workers
sample: The 1999 cohort of full-time Danish private-sector workers aged 18–56, followed through 2007.

definitions.definition: A firm is exposed (treated) if as of 1999 it had domestic production in any 8-digit CN good for which China would no longer face a quota upon WTO entry; quota categories are matched to 8-digit CN goods and firms producing quota goods are identified from the domestic production database reporting establishment sales by 10-digit product. Workers are exposed if employed by such a firm in 1999.
definitions.codes: Stata variable affwd (1=Exposed, 0=Non-exposed); clustering on cvrnr99 (1999 firm id)

definitions.definition: Cohort of workers who in 1999 were full-time employed in Denmark's private sector, had positive wages and were aged 18-56; part-time workers are excluded. IDA covers persons aged 15-70, establishments with at least one employee and jobs active in the last week of November. The textile sample is the roughly 10,000 such workers employed in the textile and clothing industry in 1999; the economy-wide sample excludes public administration, education and health.

Indicator for whether a worker fathers or mothers a newborn baby in a given year (for the IV specification: parent of a new child over 2000-2007). Child births come from Statistics Denmark's Fertility Database, which links parents' personal IDs to every child born in Denmark.

Indicators for whether a worker marries or divorces in a given year, taken from the Central Population Register and linked by personal identifier. The divorce analysis uses workers married as of 1999; marriage analysis uses workers unmarried in 1999 (1999 dropped from marriage-rate plots). Cohabiting partners are distinguished from married spouses.
Indicator for taking childcare/parental leave in a year, from childcare leave spells in Statistics Denmark's social benefits statistics, part of the income statistics registers.

Fertile-age sample is women below 37 and men below 46 years as of 1999 (fertile age limit taken as 36 for women and 45 for men). The published-version code instead uses an age 18-39 indicator (age1839) for fertility heterogeneity.

Unemployment is the percentage of annual time in unemployment. UI benefits are the sum of unemployment insurance, education allowance for the unemployed and other UI benefits, deflated by CPI and expressed relative to the worker's average 1996-1999 monthly earnings.
definitions.codes: arblhu (unemployment insurance), quddydl (education allowance for unemployed), andakas (other UI benefits); normalised by normsal9699
definitions.source_location: Analysis1.do lines 684-705 (Table A5); WP Table 8 notes

definitions.definition: Annual labour earnings (salary) and personal income, the latter including unemployment insurance and government transfers; in the cumulative textile-worker regressions both are expressed as multiples of the worker's own 1999 value. Earnings at the 1999 firm are also analysed separately.
definitions.codes: Stata variables anrsalary, anrsal99, anrperinc, anrperinc99

definitions.definition: 1999 occupation grouped from DISCO-88 major groups: 1 Managers; 2-3 Professionals and technicians; 4-5 Clerks and service workers; 7 Craft workers; 8 Operators; 9 Labourers; set missing if 2-digit code is 99. Machine operator is DISCO 2-digit group 82.
definitions.codes: DISCO-88 1-digit (disc1_99) groups {1},{2,3},{4,5},{7},{8},{9}; disc2_99==82 machine operator; disc2_99==99 missing

definitions.definition: Change in Chinese import penetration at the six-digit industry level, instrumented with Chinese imports in other advanced countries (Australia, Finland, Germany, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, USA), log average distance of Denmark's import partners in 1996, and the share of retail trading firms; two-digit industry fixed effects included.
definitions.codes: Stata IP_9909 instrumented by iv8del6, lntdistw

definitions.definition: Percentage of the workplace's 1998 employees who are not employed in the workplace in 1999.

authors: Petter Lundborg, Erik Plug and Astrid Würtz Rasmussen
title: On the Family Origins of Human Capital Formation: Evidence from Donor Children
summary: Uses Danish children conceived through sperm and egg donation to separate nurture from genetic transmission, since donors are not selected on parental traits. Only mothers' education matters once genes are removed: fathers' schooling has no effect on children's test scores, while mothers' schooling raises reading scores as much as among non-donor children.
data: Danish IVF register (Danish Health Data Authority)
Danish Education Register (UDDA)
National test scores in reading and math (from 2010)
Administrative registers on demographics and labour market (birth year, gender, marital status, children, earnings)
variables: Outcome: child average standardized national test score (reading and math)
Explanatory: mother's and father's years of schooling
Variation: donor sperm / donor egg conception (genetically unrelated parent)
Controls: month of first donor treatment and clinic fixed effects (waiting-list assignment)
period: IVF treatments 1994–2007; demographics 1991–2016; labour market 1991–2012; tests from 2010
sample_size: 19,509 non-donor IVF children, 820 sperm donor children and 157 egg donor children (97 matched to egg donors)
sample: Children conceived through IVF treatments in Denmark 1994–2007 with at least one national test score, compared with 30% random samples of non-adopted (650,930) and adopted (2,674) children.

definitions.definition: Scores from nationwide math and reading tests in primary and lower secondary school (2010-2020), each standardized to mean 0 and SD 1 within cohort; for each child the average over all available standardized reading and math scores. Math covers numbers and algebra, geometry and applied mathematics; reading covers language comprehension, decoding and reading comprehension. Grade-specific scores: reading grades 2, 4, 6, 8; math grades 3, 6.
definitions.codes: overall_grade; lang2 lang4 lang6 lang8 math3 math6

definitions.variable: Parental years of schooling and college
definitions.definition: Years of schooling of highest completed education of mother and father (and of egg donor, imputed when missing). College indicator equals 1 if more than 14 years of completed education.

Children conceived by IVF are split into a non-donor IVF sample, an egg-donor sample and a sperm-donor sample; treatment timing is captured by the calendar month of first IVF treatment and clinic dummies.
definitions.codes: one_de_ds (non-donor), de (egg donor), ds (sperm donor); first_year_month_linear; clinic

definitions.definition: Average annual labour income (in 10,000 DKK) of mother/father (or egg donor) over the 4 years preceding the child's birth year; post-minus-pre log income change uses average labour income over the 5 years following the birth year.
Total days of leave taken by mother/father within two (leavedays) or five (leavedays05) years after the child's year of birth.
Equals 1 if the couple divorced within the first five years of the child's life.
Indicator that mother/father/egg donor is a first- or second-generation immigrant.
Low birth weight is below 2500 grams; prematurity is pregnancy length below 37 weeks; indicator for Apgar score below 10.

authors: Hanno Foerster
title: Untying the Knot: How Child Support and Alimony Affect Couples' Dynamic Decisions and Welfare
summary: Estimates a dynamic model of family labour supply, home production, saving and divorce on Danish register and survey data to study post-marital maintenance payments. Alimony carries larger labour supply disincentives and insures consumption less efficiently than child support, so welfare rises when child support is increased and alimony reduced.
data: Danish register data on income, labour force status and hours worked
Marital histories and birth register (BEF/family links)
Maintenance (child support and alimony) payment records and child residence after divorce
Danish Time Use Survey 2001 (DTUS)
variables: Outcome: labour supply (employer-recorded hours bins) and annual labour income
Outcome: divorce
Policy: child support and alimony (maintenance) payments
Survey: housework hours and relative consumption in couples (DTUS)
sample_size: 322,732 couples (645,464 individuals) and 4,312,826 couple-year observations; DTUS 2,105 households
sample: Danish couples in their first marriage, both spouses aged 25–58, at least one working, excluding couples with children from previous relationships.

definitions.definition: Marriage event when marital status is unmarried in year t and married in t+1; divorce event when married in t and divorced in t+1. Marital status from CIVST (G=1 married, U=0 unmarried, F=2 divorced, D=3, E=4, L=5, O=6, P=7), with CIV_VFRA giving the date since status.
definitions.codes: CIVST in {G,U,F,D,E,L,O,P}; marriage: CIVST U->G; divorce: G->F; CIV_VFRA
definitions.source_location: code/assembledat_untying.sas (marital status recode and event definitions)

definitions.definition: Divorce year is the minimum of the formal divorce year and the first year, within 6 years before formal divorce, in which a married, never-divorced person's partner ID (FAELLE_NR) changes to a new partner or no partner.
definitions.codes: FAELLE_NR (parid); divyear=min(fdivyear, firstparswitch_year), parswitch window t_ref_fdiv in [-6,0]

definitions.definition: Individuals observed from the start of their first marriage (first observed marriage event with missing prior marital-status date and no prior divorce), years 1980-2013, ages 28-58; individuals or partners with children from previous relationships are dropped.

IDA job attachment code TILKNYT recoded into weekly hours per the Statistics Denmark key: codes 0/10/20/30 -> 0, 5/15/25/35 -> 5, 4/14/24/34 -> 15, 3/13/23/33 -> 25, 2/12/22/32 -> 34, 1/11/21/31 -> 38 hours. Set to 0 for those out of the labour force with missing hours.
Weekly hours (from TILKNYT bins) times 49 weeks times hourly wage TIMELON; zero if hours are zero. Register labour income LONIND is also assembled (earnings), with negative values truncated to 0.
definitions.codes: TIMELON (hourly wage), TILKNYT; LONIND (earnings); labor_income = work_hours*49*wage

definitions.definition: Out of the labour force if IDA labour force status PSTILL is in 40, 41, 50, 52, 90, 92, 93 or 95; labour force participation is the complement.
definitions.codes: PSTILL in 40,41,50,52,90,92,93,95 = out of labour force
definitions.source_location: code/datprep_untying.do (Define out of the labor force)

definitions.definition: Post-marital maintenance paid (child support and alimony) from the income register variable UNDERHOL, deflated to 2004 prices; an indicator for any positive payment is also used.

Custody counts children under 19 living in the same family ID after a divorce. Child support imputed from 2004 rules: 10,608 DKK per child times an earnings-dependent multiplier (thresholds 320k/340k/370k/500k/900k for one child, higher for 2-3 children) for children in the ex-partner's custody; alimony = 20% of (payer earnings minus child support minus max(ex-partner earnings, 90,000)), capped, only if ex-partner not remarried; total maintenance capped at one third of earnings. Earnings base = labour income + UI benefits (ARBLHU, KONTHJ, KONT_GL) in 2004 prices.

Individual and household assets from the income register wealth variables: FORM before 1997 and FORMREST_NY05 after 1997; household assets are the sum of own and partner's post-1997 assets in DKK 1000s.

Children linked to fathers and mothers via the fertility database (PNRF, PNRM, PNRB) with birth year from FOED_DAG; first, second and third child IDs are assigned sequentially; birth event = child born in that year. Number of children and persons in the family from the family register.
definitions.codes: PNRF, PNRM, PNRB, FOED_DAG; C_ANTBOERNF, C_ANTPERSF

authors: Ufuk Akcigit, Jeremy Pearce and Marta Prato
title: Tapping into Talent: Coupling Education and Innovation Policies for Economic Growth
summary: Builds an endogenous growth model with heterogeneous talent, financial resources and career choice, and links it to Danish micro data on who obtains a PhD and who becomes an inventor. R&D subsidies work better when combined with higher education subsidies that let talented but poor youth pursue research, and education policy matters most in unequal societies.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Firm-linked IDA (FIDA)
PhD enrolment register (PHD)
Military conscription IQ test (Boerge Prien Proeve)
European Patent Office patents linked to IDA
R&D funding data (Innovation Danmark) and Ministry of Education PhD policy data
variables: Outcome: PhD enrolment/attainment
Outcome: patent filing (inventor status)
Talent proxy: military IQ test score
Background: parental income
Policy: 2002 expansion of PhD slots and R&D subsidies
sample_size: approximately 32 million employer-employee observations, 10,000 inventors and 37,000 unique PhDs; approximately 500,000 males with IQ data
sample: Danish population in IDA linked to PhD, IQ test and patent data.

definitions.definition: Score on the Danish military conscription test Boerge Prien's Proeve, taken mostly at age 18; data go back to 1995 and cover most males entering the workforce or college after 1995 (about 500,000 males).
Enrolment in a PhD programme from the PHD dataset, which records subject, enrolment date, graduation date and funding source of PhD students.
Individual with at least one European Patent Office patent; Danish inventors matched to IDA using a DST disambiguation algorithm (about 75% matched).
definitions.source_location: Section 2.2; Section 2.3 (Determinants of Being an Inventor)

definitions.definition: Child's father's income percentile, used as the measure of parental income (correlation with child IQ of 0.18).

Background data available 1980-2013, but the intersection of the IDA, FIDA, PHD, IQ, R&D funding and patent datasets covers 2001-2013, which is the analysis window (about 32 million employer-employee observations, 10,000 inventors, 37,000 PhDs).

R&D project funding following the expansion of government R&D support from 2002, including funding through the Innovation Danmark programme and specific R&D subsidies (the programme also records funding to education).

authors: Steffen Altmann, Anita M. Glenny, Robert Mahlstedt and Alexander Sebald
title: The Direct and Indirect Effects of Online Job Search Advice
summary: A large two-stage randomised experiment on the Danish public employment service's online platform gave job seekers vacancy information and occupational recommendations, with treatment intensity varying by region. Advice raises employment and earnings when few job seekers receive it, but the gains vanish at high intensity because treated job seekers crowd into the same occupations.
data: Field experiment on jobnet.dk (Danish public employment service platform): treatment assignment and dashboard exposure
Jobnet job search profiles, vacancy information and registered job applications (with occupation codes)
Statistics Denmark register data on employment, hours and earnings (12 months after start)
Population registers and benefit payment records (UI recipients)
Register data on the universe of unemployment-to-job occupational transitions (to build recommendations)
variables: Treatment: occupational recommendations, vacancy information, or both (individual randomization)
Treatment intensity: municipality cluster share of treated job seekers (two-stage randomization)
Outcome: working hours and earnings in the year after intervention
Outcome: job applications by occupation (search strategy)
period: Intervention from March 17, 2019; outcomes over the following 12 months (before March 2020)
sample_size: 92,098 individuals
sample: All individuals registered as unemployed and receiving UI benefits in Denmark on March 17, 2019.

definitions.definition: Full stock of individuals registered as unemployed and receiving UI benefits in Denmark at the start of the experiment on March 15, 2019 (92,098 individuals); welfare recipients and later entrants excluded. Outcomes measured over windows after entrydate.
Sum of paid hours (AJO_LOENTIMER) over all BFL monthly job records whose AJO_JOB_START_DATO falls after entrydate and within q x 30.42 days (q=6, 12); zero if no records.
definitions.codes: AJO_LOENTIMER summed for AJO_JOB_START_DATO in (entrydate, entrydate+q*30.4167]

definitions.definition: Sum of AJO_SMALT_LOENBELOEB over BFL records with job start date in the window after entrydate, zero if none.
emp_q = 1 if cumulative BFL hours increase between month q-1 and q after entry (emp1 = any hours in month 1); employment rate over 6 or 12 months is the mean of these monthly indicators.

Hours, earnings and monthly employment in BFL jobs whose DISCO code (VMO_DISCO_KODE truncated to 4 digits) matches one of up to five recommended occupations (Alternative_DISCO mapping of the job seeker's profile occupations) or an occupation stored in the job search profile (jsjs CVFAGID), within 183 and 365 days of entry.

definitions.variable: Share of applications to recommended occupations
definitions.definition: Among applications logged in Joblog within 1 or 12 months (30.25-day months) after entry, the share whose DISCO-AMS occupation equals a recommended occupation (or one stored in the profile).
Vacancies divided by job seekers per municipality x occupation in the experiment's starting week (week 1442), averaged over the occupations in the individual's search profile.

Baseline: municipality regime (10 super-control, 44 medium with 60% treated, 44 high with 90% treated). Alternatives: share treated in own plus bordering municipalities; commuting-weighted shares using the fraction of workers residing in j who commuted to m in the three prior years; and an individual measure over zip-code x 3-digit-occupation markets applied to in the two prior years.

From BFL records with period start before entry: mean monthly wage (lon) and employment degree (grad) in each of the three years before entry (year t-1 excludes the last 30 days), set to zero if absent; last pre-intervention occupation is the 1-digit DISCO of the most recent BFL spell.

authors: Andrey Stoyanov and Nikolay Zubanov
title: Productivity Spillovers Across Firms through Worker Mobility
summary: Tracks firm-to-firm worker moves in Danish manufacturing. Firms that hire workers from more productive firms see productivity gains of about 0.35 percent a year for an average firm, rising with the education, tenure and skill of the new hires and persisting for several years, consistent with knowledge spillovers carried by workers.
data: Matched employer-employee data from Statistics Denmark (worker records from 1983, ages 15–65)
Manufacturing firm-level accounts data with sales, value added, materials, capital and investment, 1995–2007
variables: Outcome: receiving firm's log value added per worker normalised by 4-digit industry-year mean
Treatment: productivity gap between sending and receiving firms of newly hired workers, weighted by hires' employment share
Positive and negative productivity gaps (hires from more vs. less productive firms)
Worker characteristics: education, occupation/skill level, experience, wage
Firm characteristics: size, industry
sample_size: 173,929 firm-year observations (about 5.8 million worker-year observations, 668,034 job changers); benchmark regressions use 74,507 and 61,112 firm-year observations
sample: All Danish manufacturing firms and their employees with positive annual salary, 1995–2007.

definitions.definition: Natural log of firm value added per worker normalized by the 4-digit NACE industry-year average; manufacturing firms 1995-2007, with firm accounts from annual surveys (all firms with 50+ workers) and interpolated values for less frequently surveyed small firms.

Split into four groups by sending firm: from more productive firms in the same 2-digit industry (gap_p_same), more productive firms in a different industry (gap_p_diff), less productive same industry (gap_n_same), less productive different industry (gap_n_diff). Regressions include five lags of value added per worker (autocorrelation insignificant at the sixth lag), industry-year fixed effects and average size of the sending firm; period 1995-2007; firm-specific trend robustness restricted to firms with 50+ workers.

Worker observed at a different firm than in the previous year; employment record is as of end of calendar year, so only the year of the move is observed. Sample restricted to manufacturing firms and employees aged 15-65 with positive annual salary; multiple jobs treated as different.
Occupation grouped into four categories: low-skilled, mid-skilled, high-skilled workers and managers.
Highest completed education measured in three levels: high school, college and university.
Work experience recorded in thousands of hours in the individual-level data.

Firm average of worker wage net of the AKM firm effect, h = (1/N) sum (w - lambda - psi_j), from a wage equation with person and firm fixed effects (Abowd, Kramarz and Margolis 1999); new workers' human capital measured in t-1, their last full year in the previous firm.

Nine 2-digit NACE manufacturing industry groups used for industry-specific estimates and industry-year fixed effects: Food, beverages, tobacco; Textiles, clothing, footwear; Wood, paper and products thereof; Publishing, printing, recording; Fuel, chemical and other non-metallic mineral products; Metals and products thereof (excluding machinery); Machinery and equipment; Electrical and optical equipment; Manufacturing n.e.c.

authors: Steffen Andersen, Elin Colmsjö, Gianpaolo Parise and Kim Peijnenburg
title: Breaking Bad: How Health Shocks Prompt Crime
summary: Uses plausibly exogenous timing of cancer diagnoses in Danish registers to show that a health shock raises the probability of committing a crime, both first offences and re-offences, persistently. Patients replace lost legal income with illegal income and face a lower expected cost of punishment because of reduced survival, and welfare programmes that cushion the income loss dampen the effect.
data: Danish administrative registers on cancer diagnoses (timing of diagnosis)
Crime registers (first crimes and re-offenses)
Income and welfare program registers
variables: Treatment: timing of a cancer diagnosis (health shock)
Outcome: probability of committing a crime (first crimes and re-offenses)
Mechanism: loss of legal income
Mechanism: survival probability (expected cost of punishment)
Heterogeneity: welfare program coverage
sample: Danish individuals diagnosed with cancer, using variation in the timing of diagnosis.

definitions.variable: Crime (conviction for offence committed in year t)
definitions.definition: Indicator equal to one if the individual is convicted of a crime committed in year t, dated by offence year and scaled to 100 in event-study figures. Offence types are classified as economic/non-economic and as property/sexual/violent (the latter following Statistics Denmark's system), covering 4,732,529 crimes 1980-2018.
definitions.codes: Offence classification in Online Appendix Table I.I
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix H eq. (15)-(16); Table I.I; Figure I.6 notes

definitions.definition: Log of one plus the days between when a crime is committed and when the perpetrator is apprehended, using the median time if the person commits multiple crimes in a year; only observations in the offence year are used.

definitions.variable: Decline in 5-year survival probability due to cancer
definitions.definition: Logit of dying within 5 years, estimated on people aged 18-62 in 1980-2013 (diagnosed plus up to ten exactly matched controls per case) with cancer-type indicators (14 types plus multiple), age polynomial interactions, post-cancer, gender and marriage controls, separately for 1980-1992, 1993-2003 and 2004-2013. The decline is predicted probability minus the counterfactual with no diagnosis. Low survival means an above-median decline within gender (also split by quintile).

For each diagnosed individual, controls who in the year before diagnosis share age, marital status and gender and are in the same income ventile and years-of-education quintile. Up to ten controls with the smallest difference in total income are kept; unmatched observations are dropped.

Alternative design comparing individuals diagnosed in a given year with those diagnosed Delta years later (Delta from 3 to 8), with person, year-by-age, in-prison and cancer-recurrence fixed effects. The baseline sample keeps only the 10 years before cancer for pre-diagnosis observations.

definitions.variable: Change in municipal welfare generosity (2007 reform)
definitions.definition: Percentage change in labour income plus transfers in post-diagnosis years relative to the five-year pre-diagnosis average, regressed on municipality fixed effects, age fixed effects, a cubic in pre-diagnosis income rank and year effects, separately pre-reform (1987-2006) and post-reform (2007-2018). People diagnosed 2004-2006 are excluded. The generosity change is the difference between post- and pre-reform municipality effects.
Indicator for having received treatment by a psychologist or psychiatrist following the cancer diagnosis, from data on medical visits.
registers: Health insurance / medical visits data (name not given)

authors: Edmund Crawley and Andreas Kuchler
title: Consumption Heterogeneity: Micro Drivers and Macro Implications
summary: Estimates marginal propensities to consume across Danish households with a method that corrects biases in earlier register-based estimates. Liquid wealth is the dominant predictor of MPCs, and the estimated heterogeneity is used to quantify monetary policy transmission in Denmark and the United States.
data: Tax-authority income records (household after-tax and transfer income)
Tax-reported wealth data: bank deposits, loans, bond and stock holdings, mortgages (year-end balances)
Private pension contribution records
Civil Registration System (CPR) family/household links
Mortgage reset data (amount resetting over the following year)
variables: Outcome: imputed household expenditure (income minus pension contributions minus change in non-housing net worth)
Shock: unexpected (residual) change in after-tax household income of the head
Heterogeneity: liquid wealth (bank deposits) quintiles
Heterogeneity: Unhedged Interest Rate Exposure (URE) and Net Nominal Position (NNP)
sample_size: 7.7 million observations from 2004 to 2015
sample: Danish households headed by an individual aged 30–55 in 2008, excluding business owners, households with housing transactions, and top/bottom 1% of income and income changes.

definitions.definition: Households have one or two adults; two cohabiting adults are one household if (i) married or in a registered partnership, (ii) have at least one common child in the Civil Registration System, or (iii) are of opposite sex, age difference of 15 years or less, not closely related and with no other adults present. Children under 25, never married and childless belong to the parents' family. The head is the highest earner over the 13-year sample period.

C = Y - P - dNW: after-tax income (all labor and capital income, excluding capital gains) minus contributions to privately administered pension schemes minus the change in non-pension, non-housing net worth between 31 December of t-1 and t. Households in housing-transaction years and with more than trivial business income are excluded; equity holders are assumed to hold a diversified stock index; household-years with negative imputed expenditure (about 3 percent) are discarded.

After dropping the top and bottom 1 percent of household after-tax-and-transfer income, income is normalized by average household income over the period and regressed on dummies for age, year, highest education, marital status, homeowner status and number of children plus age interactions with education, marital and homeowner status; the year-to-year change in the residual is the unexpected income change, trimming the top and bottom 1 percent. Expenditure residuals are constructed the same way.

Households whose head is aged 30-55 in 2008 (to exclude young/old whose income growth is likely anticipated and whose income variance is non-constant). Out-of-sample exposures allocated to seven bins: young (<30) heads, old (>55) heads, pension funds (incl. children's savings accounts), government, non-financial corporates, financials, rest of the world.

Households are assigned to quantiles by their mean level of liquid wealth (or income, etc.) over the sample period (long-term quintiles); liquid wealth is the end-of-year balance, averaged in real terms over 2009-2015 in descriptive comparisons.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix E.1 and Table F.1 notes

definitions.definition: Household URE = annual savings (after-tax income minus imputed expenditure) plus maturing assets minus maturing liabilities. Maturing assets: all bank deposits (assumed floating) plus 20% of securities (5-year maturity assumed). Maturing liabilities: all bank debt (assumed floating), mortgage debt contractually due to reset its interest rate in the coming 12 months (counted at half weight since the new rate applies half the year; voluntary refinancing excluded), and other liabilities with an assumed 5-year maturity. Non-household sectors' maturity calibrated to 3.65 years so economy-wide URE sums to zero.

Household NNP = financial assets minus liabilities, averaged over 2009-2015 and deflated by CPI. Assets: bank deposits plus market value of securities excluding shares. Liabilities: all debt to financial institutions (including credit card debt), publicly administered student debt, tax debt and other debt to government bodies, as reported to the tax authorities by financial institutions. Other sectors from national financial accounts: net assets in currency and deposits, securities other than shares, loans, and trade credits/other accounts receivable-payable.
Imputed expenditure adjusted using registry data on household car purchases to proxy nondurable consumption (details in online appendix G, not in this file).

authors: Jakob Munch and Georg Schaur
title: The Effect of Export Promotion on Firm-Level Performance
summary: Evaluates the Danish Trade Council's export promotion services, separating firms that sought help from firms the council approached on observables. Promotion raises sales, value added, employment and value added per worker, and for small firms the gain in value added is roughly three times the direct cost.
data: Danish Trade Council data on export promotion services (self-selected vs. Council-approached firms)
Danish firm-level performance data (sales, value added, employment); specific registers not stated in abstract
variables: Treatment: firm receives export promotion services from the Danish Trade Council
Comparison: firms that self-selected into services vs. firms approached by the Trade Council
Outcome: sales, value added, employment, value added per worker
Controls: extensive set of firm characteristics (selection on observables)
sample: Danish firms, comparing users of Trade Council export promotion services with comparable non-users.

authors: Andreas Bjerre-Nielsen and Mikkel Høst Gandil
title: Attendance Boundary Policies and the Limits to Combating School Segregation
summary: Uses address-level data on the universe of Danish children and changes in school attendance boundaries over time. Households defy reassignment to schools with lower socioeconomic status, resourceful households most of all, so redrawing boundaries toward highly disadvantaged schools barely changes those schools' composition.
data: Register data on the universe of Danish children (Statistics Denmark)
School attendance boundary data with boundary changes over time
variables: Treatment: reassignment of a residential area to a different school by an attendance boundary change
Outcome: enrolment in (or defiance of) the assigned school
Heterogeneity: household socioeconomic resources
Socioeconomic composition of the new school's students
sample: Danish children (universe) whose residential areas were affected by changes in school attendance boundaries.

definitions.definition: Population rank (uniform on the unit interval) of the first principal component of four household variables: INC = highest market-income rank among adults in the household; LCE = any adult has completed a long-cycle education; NE = any adult has no education beyond primary school or no registered education; EMP = any adult is employed. With z-scored inputs, SES = 0.62 INC + 0.38 LCE - 0.44 NE + 0.53 EMP (47 percent of variance explained).
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix A (Construction of SES index), equation (1)

definitions.definition: Mean of the household SES index among seven-year-old children enrolled in a school in a given school-year.
Share of non-Western children in the school, used as an alternative school characteristic; it is interacted with a household non-Western dummy. The appendix does not state the exact origin coding.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Tables B.6-B.7 notes, Figure B.2

definitions.definition: Binary indicator equal to one if the child is enrolled at age 7 in the district (attendance-zone) school that corresponds to the child's address at age 5. Control units are artificially assigned to nearby recipient schools. An alternative version uses enrolment in the assigned school at age 7 (see main text Section 5.4).
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix Tables B.2-B.4 notes, Figure B.4 notes

definitions.definition: Three binary outcomes measured at age 7 relative to the address at age 5: enrolled in another public school, enrolled in a private school, or moved out of the district between ages 5 and 7. Aggregate non-compliance is their sum.
Low density: less than 1,000 per sq. km; medium: 1,000-5,000 per sq. km; high: more than 5,000 per sq. km. Used to describe enrolment for all children aged 7 in 2008-2015.

authors: Jonas Fluchtmann, Anita M. Glenny, Nikolaj A. Harmon and Jonas Maibom
title: The Gender Application Gap: Do Men and Women Apply for the Same Jobs?
summary: Uses administrative records of the job applications made by every Danish unemployment insurance recipient. Men and women apply to very different job types even when observationally similar, and these differences in applications account for more than 70 percent of the residual gender wage gap.
data: Joblog job application records from the public employment service platform (Jobnet)
Unemployment insurance payment records / DREAM event-history data
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Employment Statistics for Employees, monthly earnings and hours (BFL)
variables: Outcome: characteristics of applied-for jobs (occupation, industry, AKM firm wage premium, commute, hours)
Group: gender
Outcome: hourly wage in new job one month after hire
Predicted 'typical wage' of applied-for jobs
sample_size: 105,879 individuals, 114,375 UI spells, 2,911,585 job applications
sample: Danish UI recipients entering new spells from September 2015 to September 2017 lasting at least 8 weeks, with at least 4 registered applications and finding a job within one year.

definitions.variable: New UI spell and analysis sample
definitions.definition: UI recipients of Danish nationality entering new UI spells September 2015 to September 2017. A new UI spell starts when a person who received no UI benefits in the previous 4 weeks is observed with at least 4 consecutive weeks of UI payouts. Restrictions: spell lasts at least 8 weeks; at least 4 Joblog applications registered during the spell (counted after dropping the last 4 weeks); exits UI to employment within 52 weeks; applications from the last 4 weeks before the new job starts are dropped (median transition time 6 weeks minus an assumed 2 weeks from application to offer). Observations with an estimated propensity score above 0.99 or below 0.01 are trimmed.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix A.1 and A.6, Table A.1, fn. 39

definitions.definition: Applications self-reported in the Joblog section of Jobnet during the UI spell. Only applications actually sent are kept, using the first saved version of each entry. Other Joblog events (vacancies saved for later, interviews, rejections) are excluded. Mandatory fields include job title, part-time or full-time status, and firm name, zip code and city.

Self-reported job titles were cleaned and mapped to DISCO (the Danish version of ISCO) in three steps: (1) unique 1:1 occurrences of DISCO occupation names in the title (43.4% of applications); (2) manual mapping of acronyms and common titles, e.g. 'sosu-hjælper' (+27.2%); (3) fuzzy matching with SAS compget, speedist and soundex plus substring matches, keeping only consistently high-ranked matches (+10.9%). In total 81.5% of applications are matched. Occupations are used at the 1-, 2- and 3-digit levels (9, 55 and 153 groups).

The reported firm name, zip code and city are matched to the CVR firm register and then to BFL. Steps: exact 1:1 match on firm name and zip code (66.3%); substring matches closest to the reported address (+13.9%); fuzzy matching on the 50 closest Stata matchit candidates, ranked by 5 scores (bigram similscore, token, tokensound, SAS compget and speedist), keeping the best average rank (+6.2%). Overall firm match rate is 86.4%. Industry comes from BFL using NACE Rev. 2 groupings of 10, 21 or 38 industries. Industry is missing when the firm is too new or small to have an industry recorded in BFL.

AKM model on log hourly wages (BFL monthly earnings divided by monthly paid hours) with worker, firm and calendar-month fixed effects. The panel uses March and September of each year from 2008 to 2017, giving 265,425 connected firms (about 95% of firms). Firm effects are standardised within industry by subtracting the industry mean and dividing by the industry SD. Decile bins are employment-weighted by firm employment in August 2015. Gender-specific AKM effects are used as a robustness check.

BFL monthly earnings divided by recorded monthly paid hours in the first full month of employment in the new job. Results are similar using a 4-month average or excluding observations whose hours were imputed by Statistics Denmark.

Predicted log wage from a Post-LASSO OLS model estimated on new jobs in the analysis sample. Candidate regressors are 1-, 2- and 3-digit industry and occupation dummies, the within-industry standardised AKM firm effect (set to 0 when missing, plus a missing dummy) and all pairwise interactions, 10,407 variables in total. Rigorous LASSO (Belloni et al. 2016, LASSOPACK, clustered by individual) selects 233 variables, of which 117 remain after collinearity. Out-of-sample R2 is 0.201. Alternative models without firm information or without occupation information fill in values for unlinked applications. The model uses no worker characteristics.
Mandatory Joblog field: full-time is 37 hours per week; part-time is less than full-time.
Commuting distance or time from the applicant's municipality of residence to the job's postal code, computed with the Google Maps API (following Harmon 2015).

Firm-level average days of parental leave per birth among employees. Built from childbirth-related payouts after 2011 in the sickness/maternity benefit register (SGDP), covering both employer reimbursements and direct payments, for workers who later return to the same pre-birth employer. Births are inferred from a new leave spell or a gap of more than half a year between payments. Leave length is censored at 14 months and demeaned by gender before averaging at the firm. Firms with no births form a separate 'no birth' category.
definitions.source_location: Online Appendix A.8.1, fn. 55-57, Figure A.4

definitions.definition: The double-LASSO of Belloni et al. 2014 (PDSLASSO) selects 332 variables from 4,196 candidates, of which 302 remain after collinearity; they enter a logit propensity score for being male, and women are reweighted by p/(1-p). Candidates: years of education, field of study, age, total work experience and experience over the last 5 years, sector/industry/occupation of the previous job, industry- and occupation-specific experience over the last 5 years at 1/2/3-digit levels, and time on UI, social assistance and other transfers over the last 5 years, with interactions and squares of age, education and experience.

authors: Marianne Simonsen and Lars Skipper
title: Healthy at Work? Evidence from a Social Experimental Evaluation of a Firm-Based Wellness Program
summary: A large social experiment across worksites, followed for up to twelve years in the registers, evaluates an employer-sponsored health programme. Employees at treated worksites see fewer GP visits and buy fewer prescription drugs for up to seven years, with no change in hospitalisations, absence or turnover and some spillovers within the family.
data: Healthy-at-Work randomised experiment records (work-unit assignment, September 2008)
Primary care physician consultation records (Statistics Denmark registers)
Prescription drug purchase records
Hospital contact / hospitalisation records
Employment, sickness absence and turnover registers
Socio-economic background registers
variables: Treatment: work-unit randomised to the Healthy-at-Work wellness program
Outcome: primary care physician visits
Outcome: prescription drug purchases (any, months supply)
Outcome: hospitalisations (somatic, psychiatric)
Outcome: sickness absence and turnover
Spillover outcome: spouses' health care use
period: Randomisation 2008; follow-up to 2020 (PCP visits and work outcomes), 2019 (prescriptions), 2018 (hospitalisations)
sample_size: 7,541 workers (3,735 treatment, 3,806 control) in 314 work-units
sample: Elderly-care health workers in 314 work-units of 110 employers across 11 Danish municipalities enrolled in the Healthy-at-Work experiment.

definitions.definition: Work units (314 units of eldercare workers across 110 employers in 11 municipalities) were randomised in September 2008, with 144 units (46%) assigned to Healthy-at-Work. The population is individuals employed at participating work units in the month just before randomisation (7,541 of 7,660 linked to registers). Treatment status is fixed at the initial randomisation month, so post-randomisation moves are ignored and estimates are intention-to-treat.
Individuals with an above-median number of primary care physician consultations in the six months before randomisation; the low-risk group is at or below the median.
registers: Primary care physician consultation records (Statistics Denmark)

definitions.definition: Number of consultations (and any consultation) with the primary care physician, from register data on fee-for-service payments to primary care physicians; follow-up to 2020. The paper does not give the register name or speciality codes.
registers: Primary care physician fee-for-service records (Statistics Denmark)

definitions.definition: Any prescription drug purchase and months' supply per year (through 2019), covering drugs for hypertension, cholesterol, diabetes, severe pain relief and depression.
definitions.codes: ATC C9 (hypertension, as printed), C10, A10, N2, N05A, N05B, N05C, N06A

definitions.definition: Any hospital contact and number of days admitted to hospital, separately for contacts with a psychiatric diagnosis and with a somatic diagnosis; follow-up to 2018. Diagnosis code lists are not given.
Any absence and yearly absence rate (share of scheduled hours missed), conditional on hours > 0. Absence data cover about 95% of the sample.
registers: Absence register (Statistics Denmark; name not given)

definitions.definition: Any hours worked, hours worked per year, continued employment with the same employer (turnover measure), and earnings per year.
registers: Employment registers (Statistics Denmark; names not given)

definitions.definition: Individuals married to or cohabiting with individuals employed at participating work units in the month just prior to randomisation.

authors: William W. Olney and Dario Pozzoli
title: The Impact of Immigration on Firm-Level Offshoring
summary: Uses the Danish refugee dispersal policy as a natural experiment and matched data on all firms and workers from 1995 to 2011. An exogenous inflow of immigrants into a municipality reduces firm-level offshoring on both margins, while immigrants' ties to their origin countries raise offshoring to those particular countries.
data: Firm Statistics Register (FirmStat)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Firm-Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (FIDA)
Foreign Trade Statistics Register: Intrastat and Extrastat firm-level imports (UHDI)
Central Business Register (foreign ownership)
variables: Outcome: extensive margin of offshoring (firm imports in same HS4 as own production)
Outcome: log volume of narrow offshoring
Treatment: non-EU immigrant share of municipality workforce
Instrument: refugee placement under the 1986–1998 Spatial Dispersal Policy (shift-share)
sample_size: approximately 35,000 firms and 1 million workers
sample: Unbalanced panel of Danish private-sector firms with more than one employee in 97 municipalities, 1995–2011.

definitions.definition: Sum of a firm's imports (Foreign Trade Statistics, Intrastat/Extrastat, 1995-2011) in the same product category as the firm's production (paper: same HS4 category; code: import product code equals the firm's export product code or domestic-production product code). Extensive margin = 1 if narrow offshoring > 0; intensive margin = log of narrow offshoring volume. Broad offshoring = all imports.
definitions.codes: uhdi ie=='1' imports, ie=='2' exports; product vare (8-digit CN) -> HS4_imp=int(vare/100), HS4_exp=int(vare/100); vars varenr -> HS4_dom_1=int(varenr/10000); narrow=(HS6_imp==HS6_exp | HS6_imp==HS6_dom_1); ext_narrow_off=(narrow_off>0); int_narrow_off=ln(narrow_off)
definitions.source_location: Trade_data.sas; offshoring_project_will_dario.do (narrow offshoring block); working paper Section 3 and fn. 23

definitions.variable: Non-EU immigrant share of municipality workforce
definitions.definition: Share of workers in a municipality-year (IDA, workplace municipality akom) who are not natives, where natives are ie_type=='1' (Danish origin) or born in an EU15 country; lagged one year in regressions. 97 municipalities (Copenhagen and Frederiksberg combined; pre-2007 municipalities recoded to post-reform codes).
definitions.codes: ie_type=='1' native; opr_land (ieland) EU15 codes 5126,5130,5180,5134,5142,5150,5108,5140,5156,5164,5170,5182,5104,5120 treated as natives; foreigner_nonEU=(natives!=1)

definitions.definition: For each origin country d, the national number of immigrants in year t is allocated to municipalities using the municipality's 1990 share of immigrants from d, summed over non-EU origins and normalized by municipality total employment in 1990.

definitions.variable: Skill groups and years of education
definitions.definition: From the first two digits of the highest completed education code (HFFSP): skill1 (medium) if 15, 20, 25, 35 or 40; skill2 (high) if 50, 60, 65 or 70; otherwise low (incl. missing). Years of education: 10->6, 15/35->10, 20/25/39->12, 40->14, 50/60->15, 65->17, 70->20, missing->6.

definitions.variable: Managers, middle managers and blue-collar workers
definitions.definition: Sample restricted to wage earners with IDA occupational position PSTILL 31-37; manager if PSTILL=31, middle level if 32-34, blue collar otherwise.

Labour productivity = ln(sales / employees); capital intensity = ln(capital / employees) with capital from FirmStat GF_EGUL (1999+) or GF_E_GUL (before 1999); size dummies 1-19, 20-49, 50+ employees (fansh). Firms with fewer than 2 employees, missing productivity/capital, or in group bra==2 (NACE 35) dropped; sample 1995-2011.
definitions.source_location: offshoring_project_will_dario.do (firm-level controls block); Program_to_create_stata_data.sas; WP fn. 15

definitions.definition: Firm is foreign-owned if its Central Business Register ownership-form code takes one of the listed values (lagged one year in regressions).
Firm industry from FirmStat GF_BRANCHE_07 (NACE rev.2, first two digits) grouped into 8 sectors.

authors: Benjamin U. Friedrich
title: Trade Shocks, Firm Hierarchies, and Wage Inequality
summary: Shows that trade shocks change within-firm wage inequality by changing firm hierarchies, using both firm-level foreign demand shocks and the Muslim boycott of Danish exports after the 2006 cartoon crisis. Adding a hierarchy layer widens pay gaps throughout the firm, and delayering after the boycott compresses wages through cuts, demotions and turnover.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA) with DISCO occupation codes
Firm-Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (FIDA)
Danish Business Register / firm statistics (GF): sales, value added, industry
Foreign Trade Statistics Register: firm-level exports by CN8 product and destination (UHDI)
UN Comtrade bilateral trade flows (HS6)
U.S. Imports of Merchandise, Penn World Tables distances, Brent oil prices (transport cost estimation)
variables: Outcome: within-firm wage inequality (std. dev. of log wages, 90-10 gap)
Treatment: number of hierarchy layers based on occupations
Instrument: firm-specific world import demand and transport-cost shocks
Natural experiment: 2006 Muslim boycott of Danish exports (Cartoon crisis)
sample_size: 68,090 firm-year observations on 12,470 firms (within-firm inequality regressions)
sample: Universe of pre-existing private-sector exporting firms in Denmark, 1999–2008.

definitions.definition: Workers' DISCO occupation code (DISCOALLE_INDK) harmonised to 3 digits and mapped to four hierarchical layers following Caliendo et al. via a DISCO3-to-PCS layer correspondence; missing layers imputed from the same worker-firm's adjacent years (up to 2 years), then from the layer whose average hourly wage is closest; firm-years with more than 20% of hours requiring imputation are set to missing.
definitions.codes: DISCOALLE_INDK; military code 0110/011000 recoded to 900; file correspondence_DISCO3_pcslayer

definitions.definition: Number of distinct occupational layers present in the firm-year (layers renumbered consecutively from the lowest present), missing if more than 20% of firm hours had imputed layers; alternative 3-layer versions collapse layers 1-2 or use DISCO 3-digit <200 for layer 3.
definitions.codes: layers = max(layerN); managers: first DISCO digit = 1

definitions.variable: Hourly wage and within-firm wage inequality
definitions.definition: Hourly wage TIMELON (job earnings JOBLON / hours) for active November jobs (JOBLON and TIMELON > 0), CPI-deflated to 2000; observations below the 0.25th or above the 99.75th percentile of the yearly hourly wage distribution dropped; firm-year inequality is the s.d. of log hourly wages and percentile gaps 90-10, 75-25, 90-50, 50-10.
Worker-level data restricted to IDA sector code 2 (private sector) before building firm outcomes.

Sales (GF_OMS), value added (GF_BAV) and full-time equivalent employment (GF_AARSV) from firm statistics, CPI-deflated; industry from DB93/DB03 9-, 27- and 53-group aggregations, 2007 industry carried forward to 2008 if missing; firm age = year - start year + 1.
definitions.codes: GF_OMS, GF_BAV, GF_AARSV, GF_gr009_DB93/DB03, GF_gr027_DB93/DB03, GF_gr053_DB93/DB03

definitions.definition: Firm-level Bartik shock: sum over HS6 product-destination pairs of the firm's pre-sample (first year exported, from 1998) export share times log world import demand, where world import demand is the destination country's total HS6 imports from the world excluding Denmark (Comtrade 1999-2008), aggregated to HS4/HS2 when HS6 unavailable.
definitions.codes: UHDI ie == 2 (exports); vrd (value), vgt (weight); HS1988/92 concordance

definitions.definition: Predicted transport costs per product-destination from US Imports of Merchandise estimates, combining HS2 group coefficients, log Brent oil price, log distance, their interaction and (for one version) new-EU-member accession after 2003, weighted by the firm's pre-sample export shares.

Treated firms exported to Muslim-majority countries (>50% Muslim population) in 2003-2005 and had more than 0.5% of 2005 exports going to those countries; control firms had no such exports in 2003-2005.
definitions.codes: treatment = 1 if Arabpre == 1 & Arabshare > 0.005; 0 if Arabpre == 0; country list by ISO2 (AE, AF, AL, AZ, BD, ...)

definitions.definition: Firm imports (ie == 1) a product at HS4 or HS6 level that it also exports in the same year.

authors: Henrik Yde Andersen, Stine Ludvig Bech and Alessia De Stefani
title: Spending Response to a Predictable Increase in Mortgage Repayments: Evidence from Expiring Interest-Only Loans
summary: Matches the universe of Danish mortgages to borrower registers and studies the fully anticipated start of amortisation on interest-only loans. When instalments rise by 9 percent of income, consumption falls by 3 percent of income and stays down, with the failure to smooth concentrated among highly leveraged borrowers likely to be refused a new interest-only loan.
data: Mortgage registry: loan-level data on the universe of Danish mortgages reported by mortgage institutions to Danmarks Nationalbank (from 2009)
Income and wealth registers (IND/FORMUE): household income, bank deposits, stocks, bonds, pensions, debts
Population/household registers (BEF): family composition, residence
Imputed household consumption from income and wealth registers
variables: Treatment: expiry of the interest-only period (start of amortisation)
Outcome: imputed household consumption relative to income
Installment increase relative to income
Heterogeneity: loan-to-value ratio and liquid savings
period: Mortgage registry 2009–2018; IO loans originated 2003–2007 expiring 2013–2017
sample_size: 46,025 household-year observations (baseline regressions); 8,813 households beginning amortization
sample: Danish households with an interest-only mortgage originated 2003–2007 whose IO period expires in 2013–2017 and who keep the original loan, excluding self-employed and house buyers/sellers.

definitions.variable: Expiring interest-only loan sample / treatment year
definitions.definition: Households with a mortgage loan taken in year t-10 that started with an interest-only (IO) period lasting at least 9 years (IO length = years between IO start and end dates in REAL) and that survives from t-1 to t; treatment year is when the IO period expires; event time = year - treatment year. Households with any self-employed member, non-tax-liable members, or a property purchase/sale/ownership change in event years -1 to 1 are dropped.
definitions.codes: y_laanoptag = t-10 & l_afdragsfrihed_aar >= 9; drop if selvst, ikkeskattepligtig, or koebt/solgt/ejerskift in t_count -1..1

definitions.definition: Family disposable income (excluding imputed rent of own home) plus one-off pension payouts (ATP, SP, LD, withdrawn pensions) net of their tax, minus savings in bank deposits, minus stock savings corrected for price changes (change in stock holdings less lagged holdings x stock index return), minus foreign asset savings, minus repayments (afdrag) on mortgage, bank, mortgage-deed and foreign debt, minus private pension contributions. From 2010 the mortgage repayment uses loan-level REAL repayments (version 3).
definitions.codes: famforbrug1a / famforbrug3 = famdispindk + (famatp_engang+famsp_pension+famld_udbetal+famhaevpen) - taxes on these - op_famindestpi - (op_famkursakt - famkursakt_lag*makro_aktie/100) - op_famudlakt - af_famoblgaeld (or af_famrealgaeld) - af_fambankgaeld - af_fampantgaeld - af_famudprigael - fampripensindbetal

definitions.variable: Outcomes scaled by lagged disposable income
definitions.definition: Annual changes in household consumption, bank deposits, financial assets, bank debt and mortgage debt, and levels of installments and interest payments, divided by previous-year family disposable income (DISPON_13); all censored at the 1st and 99th percentile by year.
definitions.codes: rdiffconsump = (famforbrug - L.famforbrug) / L.famdispon_13; rfamafdrag_for = famafdrag_for / L.famdispon_13

definitions.definition: Liquid assets = bank deposits + bonds + stocks (market value); total assets add housing value; liabilities = bank debt + mortgage outstanding; debt-to-income = total liabilities (QPASSIVN) / gross income (PERINDKIALT_13); total mortgage payment (ydelse) = installments + interest paid + administration fee (bidrag).
definitions.codes: liq_assets = fambankakt + famoblakt + famkursakt; dti = famqpassivn/famperindkialt_13; ydelse = famafdrag_for + famrente_bet_nu + fambidrag

definitions.definition: At the expiry year: loan stays (survives, no new loan in t-1, t, t+1); new IO loan taken in t-1, t or t+1; new amortising loan (no IO); or pays out the loan (none of the above).

authors: Gustaf Bruze, Alexander Kjær Hilsløv and Jonas Maibom
title: The Long-Run Effects of Individual Debt Relief
summary: Links court records on the Danish debt relief programme to the registers and uses quasi-random assignment of applicants to court trustees with different admission rates. Debt relief raises earned income, employment, assets, home ownership and wealth for more than 25 years, with the move into employment accounting for two thirds of the income gain.
data: Hand-collected debt relief announcements from the official gazette Statstidende (court records), 1984–2005
Central Person Register (CPR) for linkage
Income Tax Register: earned income, taxable assets and debt, real estate ownership
Labour market status registers (employment status in November)
Hourly wage measure from Statistics Denmark
variables: Treatment: being granted court-ordered debt relief
Instrument: court trustee admission rate (judge/trustee leniency design)
Outcome: earned income and employment
Outcome: taxable assets, secured and unsecured debt, home ownership, wealth
sample_size: 46,571 individuals (final sample); 32,794 observations in the IV sample with 515 trustee identifiers
sample: All applicants for debt relief in Danish City Courts from 1984 to 2003, linked to national registers.

definitions.definition: Applicants identified from Statstidende announcements (decision types P = proklama, K = kendelse/ruling, T = tilbagekaldelse/revocation, I); granted = the person's sequence of announcements contains a Kendelse (court ruling granting debt relief); alternative definition requires no subsequent revocation.
definitions.codes: granted = 1 if any decision 'K'; granted_not_revoked = granted & no 'T' after 'K'
definitions.source_location: 01classify_rep.sas, section 'Classify individuals into those who receive debt relief and those who don't'

definitions.definition: Leave-one-out mean grant rate of the applicant's court-appointed trustee (lawyer ID unique within court), net of the leave-one-out court grant rate; sample restricted to trustees with at least 20 cases; regressions include court x year fixed effects, SEs clustered by trustee.
definitions.codes: iv_lawyer2 = (mean_lawyer_leniency*n_lawyer - granted)/(n_lawyer-1) - (iv_court*obs_court - granted)/(obs_court-1); keep if n_lawyer >= 20
