definitions.definition: Through 2012: employed if IDA occupational status PSTILL < 38 or in 71-77; unemployed if PSTILL = 40; out of labour force if PSTILL 41-57 or 90-98. From 2013: employed if JOB_P_SOCIO_KODE 110, 120, 131-136; unemployed if 200; out of labour force if 311-517. Alternative: employed if wage income LOENMV_13 > 0.
Earned income ERHVERVSINDK_13 from the income register and hourly wage TIMELON from IDA, CPI-deflated and winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles by year.

definitions.variable: Assets, debt, wealth, secured debt, home ownership
definitions.definition: Assets = QAKTIVF (before 1997) / QAKTIVF_NY05 (from 1997); debt = QPASSIV / QPASSIVN; wealth = assets - debt; secured (mortgage) debt = PRIGALD before 1995 and OBLGAELD from 1995; home owner if property value KOEJD > 0. Bank debt BANKGAELD and mortgage deed debt PANTGAELD also used.
definitions.codes: QAKTIVF, QAKTIVF_NY05, QPASSIV, QPASSIVN, PRIGALD, OBLGAELD, KOEJD, BANKGAELD, PANTGAELD, GALDIO

definitions.definition: Disability insurance if TILBTOT > 0; social assistance if cash assistance (KONT_GL, KONTANTHJ_13 from 1994) > 0; unemployment benefits if ARBLHUMV > 0 or ANDAKAS > 0.

authors: David Hummels, Jakob R. Munch and Chong Xiang
title: No Pain, No Gain: Work Demand, Work Effort, and Worker Health
summary: Links Danish worker-firm data to hospital and prescription records to study how rising workload affects health. Increases in firm sales lead workers to log longer hours and raise the probability of stress, depression, heart disease and stroke, most for older and already strained workers; the welfare loss from sickness offsets nearly a quarter of the earnings gain.
data: Firm Statistics Register (FIRM)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA)
Firm-worker link (FIDA)
Accounts Statistics (Regnskabsstatistik)
Prodcom firm sales by product (VARS)
Health care registers: prescription drug purchases, doctor visits and hospitalizations (National Patient Register)
Monthly payroll records with earnings and hours (eIndkomst/BFL)
Monthly firm VAT sales and material purchases (FIKS)
variables: Treatment: log firm sales (Prodcom), with a Bartik/shift-share instrument in robustness checks
Outcome: monthly hours worked and earnings
Outcome: stress/depression indicators (anti-depressant use, psychiatrist visits, burnout hospitalizations)
Outcome: heart disease drugs, heart attack/stroke and alcoholism hospitalizations
Fixed effects: job-spell fixed effects
sample_size: 3,336,244 annual worker-year observations; 8,834,846 monthly observations
sample: Full-time workers aged 20–60 in private-sector Danish firms in the Prodcom sales data with at least 50 employees and positive imports and exports, excluding single-year employment relationships.

definitions.definition: Annual sum of prescription drug expenditure on antidepressants per person, from the prescription register 1995-2016; set to 0 for person-years with no purchases.
definitions.codes: ATC3 = N06A; eksp_anti = sum of eksp where atc3='N06A'

definitions.definition: Annual sum of prescription drug expenditure per person on cardiac therapy drugs (heart) and antithrombotic agents (stroke), 1995-2016; 0 if none. Sleep medication defined analogously.
definitions.codes: heart: ATC2 = C01; stroke: ATC2 = B01; sleep: ATC3 = N05C; depression: ATC3 = N06A (eksp summed)

definitions.definition: Person-year indicators for hospital contacts with an action (primary) diagnosis in the listed ICD-10 groups: severe stress, depression, mild depression, work problems, burnout; broad burnout = burnout + work problems excluding unemployment/job change/job loss; narrow burnout = burnout + stressful work + mental strain.
definitions.codes: ADIAG: severe stress DF43; depression DF32; mild depression DF320, DF321, DF329; work problems DZ56 (excl. DZ560 unemployment, DZ561 job change, DZ562 job loss for workproblems2); stressful work DZ563; mental strain DZ566; burnout DZ730-DZ733

definitions.variable: Heart attack, stroke and circulatory hospitalizations
definitions.definition: Person-year indicators for hospital contacts with action diagnoses for heart attack, hemorrhage, cerebral infarction, hypertension (bloodpressure) and a broad circulatory group.
definitions.codes: ADIAG: heart attack DI21; hemorrhage DI61; infarction DI63; bloodpressure DI10-DI13, DI15; circulatory DI20-DI25, DI44-DI50, DI512, DI513, DR001

definitions.variable: Alcohol, digestive, accident and suicide hospitalizations
definitions.definition: Person-year indicators for alcohol-related and stress-related digestive diagnoses following Browning and Heinesen (2006), plus accidents and suicide attempts identified from the contact-cause field.
definitions.codes: alcohol: DF100, DF102, DF104, DF105, DI85, DK70, DK860, DT500, DT510; digestive: DK20, DK222, DK223, DK25-DK31, DK902; accident: KONTAARS=2; suicide: KONTAARS=4; self-harm DX7*, DX8*; poisoning DT36-DT39, DT4*, DT50

definitions.variable: Annual hours, overtime and sick hours (job-spell analysis)
definitions.definition: Hours paid, overtime hours and absence hours from the wage statistics register 1997-2012, merged to the worker-firm link by person, firm and year; for 2011-2012 earnings components are per-hour rates multiplied by hours.
definitions.codes: 1997-2010 lon: timprae (total hours), timover (overtime), timfra (absence), sftj (gross earnings), smftj (net), bfra (sick pay); 2011-2012 lonn: timprae, timover, timfra, fortj_prae*timprae etc.

definitions.definition: Monthly paid hours and narrow/broad wage amounts per person and firm summed from monthly employer payroll reports.

For each firm, HS4 product shares of Prodcom sales in a pre-sample year (first year the firm is in both Prodcom and the estimation sample, or its designated pre-sample year), multiplied by aggregate Danish Prodcom sales of each HS4 product in later years and summed to the firm-year; used in logs after deflating by the GDP deflator.
definitions.codes: bartik = sum_hs4 share_presample * aggvrd(hs4, year), years after presample year only

definitions.definition: Worker-firm-years in firms with positive imports and exports, workers aged 20-60, full-time employees, non-missing output, capital-labour ratio, skill share and the import-price instrument; firms kept from the first year with at least 10 employees onward; singleton job spells (person-firm) dropped.
definitions.codes: heltid==1 (full-time, HDTID2 codes 1-4 per code comment); age 20-60; empl>=10

definitions.definition: 4-digit DISCO/ISCO-88 codes harmonised across years, missing codes filled within job spells (constant code, then forward/backward fill); hierarchical layers counted per firm-year from ISCO88 class (2-5), set missing if more than 25% of the firm-year's workers lack a class. CEO/manager dummy = ISCO major group 1.
definitions.codes: ceo = disco 1000-1999; disco set missing if 0, 99, 110, 999, 9999; layers = sum of class 2-5 present

authors: Alex Xi He and Daniel le Maire
title: Managing Inequality: Manager-Specific Wage Premiums and Selection in the Managerial Labor Market
summary: Builds a manager-firm-worker matched dataset for the whole Danish population to estimate manager effects on wages. Manager-specific premiums are almost as important as firm premiums for between-firm wage inequality, are unrelated to productivity, and high-paying managers are more likely to be replaced after acquisitions.
data: Matched employer-employee data covering all Danish workers and firms (IDA)
Occupation codes used to identify managers
Firm balance sheet data for private-sector firms (FIRE)
Mergers and acquisitions identified from firm and establishment identifiers
variables: Outcome: worker log wages
Key estimate: manager-specific wage premiums (manager fixed effects identified from worker and manager mobility)
Comparison: firm-specific wage premiums
Event: firm acquisition and manager replacement
Heterogeneity: industry concentration (HHI)
sample: Manager-firm-worker matched panel covering the entire Danish population; acquisitions sample of about 3,700 private-sector acquisitions in the 2019 working-paper version.

definitions.definition: A worker is a manager if their ISCO-88 occupation is 1200-1399 or their job position code is top management (pstill 31); a manager status is carried forward within an establishment in years where it has no identified manager. If no manager is found, the top earner (or anyone in the top 5% of earners) is flagged when not in a non-managerial ISCO>=2000 occupation, earns at least 1.6 times the average of co-workers, or earns more than 1.5 times the second-highest earner; further fallbacks assign the top earner with a unique occupation/position earning >1.3 times the second highest.
definitions.codes: isco 1200-1399; PSTILL==31 (top manager), PSTILL 32 exception; ratio = lonind*(n-1)/(wagebill-lonind) >= 1.6; lonind/second-highest > 1.5

definitions.definition: Among identified managers, one manager per establishment-year is kept by successively preferring ISCO 1210 (CEOs), then pstill 31, managers with longer tenure in the establishment, and higher within-establishment earnings rank; only managers observed in at least two firms are retained (mobility needed for identification), establishments that were acquisition targets are excluded, and at the firm (CVR) level the manager of the largest establishment is used.

Log of the IDA hourly wage, deflated to constant prices; when the hourly wage is zero it is replaced by annual labour income divided by 1800. Observations with missing firm ID, labour income <=1, missing education or experience, or unemployment degree above 500 are dropped; firms whose maximum employment is 5 or fewer are excluded.
definitions.codes: timelon; lonind; replace timelon=lonind/1800 if timelon==0; arledgr (unemployment degree) >500 dropped; maxemp<=5 dropped

definitions.definition: M&As are identified from establishment (workplace) IDs changing firm (CVR) IDs: a firm-year is a merger if its establishments were owned by more than one distinct firm in the previous year (ignoring spurious ownership changes where an establishment's firm ID reverts); the acquirer is the establishment whose firm ID is unchanged, and targets are establishments whose previous-year firm ID differs when the firm also has an acquirer.
definitions.codes: lbnr (establishment), cvrnr (firm); merger = nvals(cvrnr_prevyear)>1 within cvrnr-year; acquirer: cvrnr==cvrnr_prevyear; target: cvrnr!=cvrnr_prevyear & nacquirer>0

definitions.definition: Share of a firm's workers in establishments that move to a different firm ID next year (spinout) or disappear next year before 2011 (exit).
definitions.codes: spinout = cvrnr_nextyear!=cvrnr; exit = cvrnr_nextyear missing & year<2011

definitions.definition: Four education groups from the first two digits of the highest completed education code: basic (<=25), vocational (35), short/medium higher (40-50), long higher (>=60).

Establishment industry is the modal worker industry code if held by more than 50% of workers; firm industry (127- and 36-group) is assigned only if at least 70% of the firm's workers share it, otherwise missing.
definitions.codes: persbrc mapped to pb07, ind127, ind36; thresholds 0.5 (establishment) and 0.7 (firm)

definitions.definition: Hiring rate = workers whose firm ID differs from the previous year divided by lagged firm employment; firing rate = workers whose firm ID differs next year divided by current employment.

authors: Benjamin Ly Serena
title: The Causal Effect of Scaling up Access to Psychotherapy
summary: A 2008 reform introduced 60 percent coverage of private psychotherapy for patients aged 18 to 37 with depression or anxiety. Using registers from 1995 to 2019, coverage reduces psychiatric hospital contacts, physical health care use and suicide attempts, leaves employment unchanged, and saves more in other health spending than it costs.
data: National Patient Register (LPR), psychiatric and somatic hospital contacts
National Health Insurance Service Register (Sygesikringsregistret), primary care and psychologist services
Prescription drug purchases (psychiatric drugs)
DREAM register (employment, sick leave, disability pension)
Yearly socioeconomic registers (population, income, education)
variables: Treatment: eligibility for 60% psychotherapy coverage introduced in 2008 for depression/anxiety patients aged 18–37
Running variable: age relative to the age-38 eligibility cutoff (RD design)
Comparison: ages 18–37 vs 38–50 before/after the reform (difference-in-differences)
Outcome: psychiatric hospital contacts and other mental health services
Outcome: physical health care use and suicide attempts
Outcome: employment, sick leave and disability pension receipt
period: 1995–2019 (published abstract; the 2021 CEBI working paper uses 2000–2016)
sample: All Danish residents, comparing those just below and above the age-38 eligibility cutoff and ages 18–37 versus 38–50 around the 2008 reform.

definitions.definition: Monthly counts of services (YDLANT) in the health insurance register 1995-2014: GP consultations (speciale 800101), private practising psychiatrists (speciale beginning 240-245 or 260-265), and psychologists (provider type YDTYP 93 or 94); costs from fee field BRUHON.
definitions.codes: GP visit: SPECIALE=800101; psychiatry: substr(SPECIALE,1,3) in 240-245, 260-265; psychologist: YDTYP in 93, 94; quantity YDLANT; fee BRUHON; doctor GP if first two SPECIALE digits = 80, psychiatrist if 24 or 26

definitions.variable: Psychometric test and GP talk therapy (event)
definitions.definition: GP-administered psychometric tests (identified by specific health insurance service codes) define the event used for treatment timing; GP talk therapy/mental health consultations are identified by a second set of service codes. Up to four first-test events per person are used in the event-study data.
definitions.codes: psychometric test: SPECIALE in 802147, 802148, 802149; therapy: SPECIALE in 804106, 806101, 804003, 804063

definitions.definition: Monthly psychiatric hospital contacts with an F-chapter action diagnosis from the psychiatric central register: inpatient admissions (patient type 0/1) with bed days, emergency room visits (patient type 3 before 2014; same-day type-2 contacts with discharge mode 0 in 2014), and outpatient visits; anxiety/depression contacts are those whose derived diagnosis group equals 3 or 4 (the recoding of C_ADIAG into these groups is done in a do-file not read).
definitions.codes: C_ADIAG starting 'DF'; C_PATTYPE 0/1 inpatient, 3 ER (2014: 2 with D_HENDTO=D_INDDTO and C_HENM=0); V_SENGDAGE bed days; bamb_AnxDep/erp_AnxDep/PHosp_AnxDep use diagnosis group in (3,4)
definitions.source_location: CollectData_Psyc_AllAges.sas (Psychiatric Hospital, Ambulatory visits sections); PsykTestLongRunRD.do

definitions.definition: Suicide attempts are somatic hospital contacts with contact reason 'suicide attempt' (duplicates on the same day removed); poisonings by selected drug groups are tracked separately; completed suicides from the cause-of-death register (49-group list code 48). Attempts are priced using average costs by patient type and diagnosis.
definitions.codes: C_KONTAARS=4 (attempt); poisoning C_ADIAG DT39, DT42, DT43 (DT39 painkillers); suicide C_LISTE49='48'; somatic contacts exclude C_SPEC 50, 52

definitions.definition: Monthly prescription purchases of psychiatric drugs (ATC N05 and N06, excluding bupropion N06AX12 used for smoking cessation): antidepressants, SSRIs, anxiolytics, hypnotics/sedatives, psychostimulants and antipsychotics; cost = IBGP minus PTP (floored at 0); prescriber classified as GP or psychiatrist via the health insurance register provider number.
definitions.codes: ATC: antidepressants N06A; SSRI N06AB; anxiety N05B; sleep N05C; psychostimulants N06B; antipsychotics N05A; excludes N06AX12

definitions.variable: Somatic hospital contacts with mental diagnosis
definitions.definition: Indicator for a somatic hospital contact (excluding psychiatric departments) with an F-chapter action diagnosis other than dementia (F0).
definitions.codes: C_ADIAG starting 'DF' and not 'DF0'; C_SPEC not 50, 52
definitions.source_location: CollectData_Psyc_AllAges.sas (Somatic hospital visits with mental health diag)

definitions.definition: Employed in a month if the DREAM employment degree (GRAD, scaled to hours by 160.33) exceeds 80 hours, available from 2008 (missing GRAD set to 0); employment before 2008 is predicted with a machine-learning imputation.

Monthly indicators from weekly DREAM benefit codes (codes 997-999 excluded): sickness benefits, disability pension, UI benefits, cash/social assistance, student grants, flex-job, early retirement and parental leave; grouped into any cash assistance, any disability-type, any UI, and any non-parental-leave transfer.
definitions.codes: fyd=floor(yd/10): sick 89; parental leave 88; UI 11 (unemployed), 21 (activation); cash 13, 71, 73, 15, 70/16, 72/14; SU 65; flexjob 77; early retirement 75 (forre), 76; 74, 81, 87; disability pension yd=783; yd=781

definitions.definition: Monthly indicator for being in a sickness-absence spell from the sickness benefit register, counting spells of at least 21 days (before 2012) or 30 days (2012 onward), using the latest registration year for each spell start.
definitions.codes: FRAVDAGE>=21 if year<2012; FRAVDAGE>=30 if year>=2012; FOERFRAV start date

definitions.variable: Monthly hours worked and absence hours
definitions.definition: Paid hours and absence hours from the wage statistics register, spread evenly over the months of each reference period.
definitions.codes: workh = TIMPRAE / months in REF_FRADATO-REF_TILDATO; absh = TIMFRA / months

authors: Andrew E. Clark, Nicolai Kristensen and Niels Westergård-Nielsen
title: Job Satisfaction and Co-worker Wages: Status or Signal?
summary: Links survey measures of job satisfaction to register wages of all co-workers at the same establishment. Satisfaction is higher when co-workers earn more, the opposite of the usual income comparison result, which the authors interpret as co-worker pay signalling one's own future earnings; the effect is stronger for men and in the private sector.
data: Danish sample of the European Community Household Panel (ECHP), eight waves
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA), matched via CPR number
variables: Outcome: overall job satisfaction (1–6 scale)
Key regressor: co-workers' wages within the same establishment
Own wage (gross annual income from IDA)
Wage deficit relative to establishment wage distribution
sample_size: about 16,000 observations on around 4,100 individuals
sample: Employees in the Danish ECHP 1994–2001 matched to IDA, in establishments with at least 5 colleagues.

definitions.definition: ECHP question 'How satisfied are you with your work or other main activity?', ordered scale from 1 (not at all satisfied) to 6 (fully satisfied); Danish ECHP waves 1994-2001, employees only.

Individual's gross annual income from IDA, matched to ECHP respondents via CPR number; entered as ln(own wage) together with a Mundlak term (individual mean wage over waves); summary statistics in 1994 DKK real terms.

Average wage of all other employees at the same establishment (IDA establishment identifier); alternatives are the 75th (and 90th) percentile of the establishment wage distribution and mean wage by three occupation categories (managers, middle-ranking, lower-level). Sample restricted to establishments with at least 5 colleagues (robustness 4 and 6).

Following Ferrer-i-Carbonell (2005): if own wage > establishment average wage, wage surplus = ln(own) - ln(average) and deficit = 0; if own < average, wage deficit = ln(average) - ln(own) and surplus = 0; both zero if equal.

authors: Mette Ejrnæs and Stefan Hochguertel
title: Is Business Failure Due to Lack of Effort? Empirical Evidence from a Large Administrative Sample
summary: Danish self-employed can voluntarily buy unemployment insurance, which creates a moral hazard test. Using a large administrative panel, insured entrepreneurs are more likely to close their businesses and enter unemployment, with effects that strengthen as the eligibility date approaches, consistent with reduced effort rather than selection alone.
data: CAM 10% Sample: 10% random sample of the Danish population aged 16+ (linked administrative registers incl. tax and benefit records)
Unemployment insurance fund membership records
variables: Outcome: transition from self-employment to unemployment (registered unemployed >10% of year)
Treatment: UI fund membership (insurance status)
Instrument: eligibility for early retirement scheme (VERP) available only to UI members
Estimator: bivariate random effects probit
sample_size: 13,434 individuals and 86,092 observations (estimation sample)
sample: Denmark-born male Danish citizens aged 25–59 who were self-employed in their first three observed years, excluding agriculture, from the CAM 10% sample.

definitions.definition: 10% random sample of the Danish population aged 16 and above from the Danish National Register, followed annually from 1981; waves up to and including 1998 are used. Unbalanced: new residents turning 16 or immigrating enter, people leave through death or emigration.

Labour market status is recorded in calendar week 48 (late November) of each year; individuals are classified as self-employed according to their main economic activity in that week. Persons originally classified as 'on leave' (possible for UI fund members from 1994) are re-classified to their state of origin.

Indicator equal to one if the individual was registered unemployed in excess of 10% of the year according to the annual 'unemployment degree' (fraction of the year UI benefits are received), zero otherwise. 'Unemployed' means registered as such with the job centre, which also covers non-UI-members on social assistance; an alternative measure is the week-48 unemployment stock.

Membership in an unemployment insurance fund, as recorded in the administrative data; 'insured' and UI fund member are used interchangeably. Treatment enters the unemployment equation lagged one year (status in t-1).

Institutional-rule indicator of eligibility for the UI-fund-linked early retirement (ER) scheme (retirement from age 60). Before 1992 members qualified with 10 years of UI membership before age 60 ('10-year rule'); the 1992 reform required at least 20 years ('20-year rule', latest joining age 40), with those aged 40-50 in 1992 required to join in 1992 and stay until 60. Identification comes from changes over year and cohort in this rule.

Denmark-born males with Danish citizenship aged 25-59; excludes students, retirees, persons out of the labour force in every year, persons receiving public pensions, and anyone who worked as wage earner or self-employed in agriculture 1981-1998; requires at least one employment spell. Estimation sample: persons self-employed in their first three observed years and not unemployed (>10% measure) in any of those years (13,434 individuals, 86,092 obs).
Receipt of sickness benefits is used as the health or illness measure because of data limitations.

Income from self-employment (surplus or profit of business), entered linearly with a dummy for negative values; income and wealth measured in constant 1981 million DKK. Controls also include receipt of start-up allowance (for entrants from unemployment via active labour market programmes) and regional unemployment calculated from the micro data.

authors: Paul Bingley, Lorenzo Cappellari and Niels Westergård-Nielsen
title: Unemployment Insurance, Wage Dynamics and Inequality Over the Life Cycle
summary: Models permanent and transitory wage dynamics over the life cycle for Danish men, allowing dynamics to differ by unemployment insurance membership. Insurance is associated with lower wage inequality and less persistence of shocks, and the paper quantifies how much of life-cycle wage inequality UI members avoid relative to non-members.
data: Administrative register data on the Danish labour force (Statistics Denmark): annual labour earnings and hours-derived hourly wages
UI fund membership contributions reported to tax authorities
Mandatory pension contributions (ATP) for year of labour market entry
variables: Outcome: log gross hourly wage (permanent and transitory components)
Key regressor: UI fund membership
Potential labour market experience
Birth cohort (1943–1973, 31 cohorts)
sample_size: roughly 810,000 individuals, about 12.5 million person-year observations
sample: Danish men aged 21–55, full-time private-sector employees, born 1943–1973, with at least five consecutive valid wage observations.

definitions.definition: Calculated by Statistics Denmark as annual labour earnings (reported by employers to the tax authorities) divided by hours worked, where hours are an annual average derived by Statistics Denmark from mandatory pension (ATP) contributions adjusted for contribution rates by sector and collective agreement. Zero wages dropped, bottom and top 0.5% trimmed per year, observations below minimum wage dropped.
Annual dummy for UI fund membership, observed from tax-deductible UI fund membership contributions reported annually by the funds to the tax authorities.
Years since entering the labour market, where year of entry is observed from the first mandatory pension (ATP) contribution; ATP was introduced in 1964, so entry is censored at 1964.

Men aged 21-55, full-time private-sector employees, 1980-2003, birth cohorts 1943-1973 (31 single-year cohorts; each observed at least ten years). Individuals must have valid wage observations for at least five consecutive years.

authors: Juanna Schrøter Joensen and Helena Skyt Nielsen
title: Mathematics and Gender: Heterogeneity in Causes and Consequences
summary: A pilot scheme in Danish high schools that let students combine advanced mathematics with chemistry increased advanced maths take-up, especially among girls. The induced maths qualification raised later earnings, with the gains concentrated among students who would otherwise have taken less maths and operating through higher education choices.
data: Education registers: detailed educational histories, high school branch choice and GPA (Statistics Denmark)
Labour market registers: earnings, occupation, industry, self-employment, part-time work
variables: Outcome: log earnings (measured 18 years after high school graduation)
Outcomes: college graduation, field of major, occupation/top corporate jobs, sector
Treatment: choice of advanced high school math
Instrument: unexpected introduction of high school pilot scheme allowing math–chemistry combination
period: High school entrants 1984–1986, followed into the labour market
sample_size: about 25,658 females and 19,406 males from about 140 high schools
sample: Danish high school entrants of 1984–86 who graduated in three years and have at least one year of employment.

definitions.definition: Indicator MathA for choosing the advanced math course in the branch-based high school; because the instrument works through the option to combine advanced math with advanced chemistry, the treatment is effectively the combined advanced math and advanced chemistry package.

PilotIntro equals one if the individual enrolled in a high school which afterwards decided to introduce the experimental (math-chemistry) curriculum for the first time, i.e. unexpectedly exposed before choosing math level; zero otherwise. Pilot school status (PilotSchool) is always controlled for.

Log earnings (2000 DKK) measured 9-18 years after high school graduation (table labels describe it as average income 9-18 years after starting high school); at least one year of employment required to have an earnings observation.
Weighted average of final exam grades for each high school course.

definitions.variable: College graduation and field of major
definitions.definition: Graduation from 2- or 4-year college, Master's education, and PhD measured 8-18 years after leaving high school, excluding those who already graduated at a higher level; field of major (e.g. Humanities, Health Sciences, Technical Sciences) from detailed education codes.

CEO = high-level managers as defined by raw occupation codes (7% of males, 2% of females); Top CEO = top-level managers in public and private enterprises regardless of number of employees using the Danish version of ISCO (D-ISCO) (1% of males, 0.2% of females); also Manager, Managerial Employee, Vice-Director, Middle Manager categories. Measured 18 years after graduation.
Indicator for being employed in the private sector 18 years after high school graduation; also nine industry indicators (e.g. transportation, mail and communication).

Population of high school entrants 1984-86 who graduated in three years and have at least one year of employment (25,658 females, 19,406 males from about 140 high schools). Controls: county, entry cohort, high school controls, parental highest education and parental income at end of year before high school start.

authors: Anders Frederiksen and Takao Kato
title: Human Capital and Career Success: Evidence from Linked Employer-Employee Data
summary: Uses complete Danish career histories to study who reaches top management, through internal promotion or external recruitment. Formal schooling and breadth of experience across occupations both help, they are complementary, and breadth acquired within the firm matters more than breadth acquired outside it, consistent with human capital theories of corporate leadership.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA) with DISCO occupation codes
Education registers
variables: Outcome: appointment to top management (DISCO 12/13) in firm with 100+ employees
Key regressor: breadth of occupational experience over prior 8 years (TOCC)
Formal schooling
Tenure, general work experience, age, gender
sample_size: 773,094 observations (3,813 appointed to top management)
sample: Private-sector employees in Denmark with complete 8-year occupational histories forming the contestant pool for top management positions.

definitions.definition: APPOINTMENT = 1 if the worker is appointed to a top management position, defined as DISCO 12 (Corporate Managers) or DISCO 13 (General Managers), in a firm with 100 or more employees between year t and t+1 (appointments in 2000 and 2001); robust to a 50-employee cut-off. CEO-only definitions were not used because 4-digit codes are inconsistently assigned.
Number of distinct 2-digit DISCO occupations held prior to the current occupation over years t-8 to t-1; alternatives are dummies OCC1-OCC7 for number of prior occupations differing from current one.

definitions.variable: Internal vs total occupational experience (INT_OCC, INT_EXT_OCC)
definitions.definition: INT_OCC = number of occupations experienced within the present firm excluding the current one; INT_EXT_OCC = total number of all occupations experienced excluding the present one, counting the same occupation in two different firms as two occupations. Internal promotion vs external recruitment distinguished by whether the appointment occurs without switching firm.

Private-sector employees in year t with complete occupational histories (DISCO codes) for t-8 to t-1 whose primary occupation in t-1 is one of the 2-digit DISCO occupations from which any top manager appointed in year t came in t-1. DISCO data used for 1992-2002 (before the 2003 switch from 4-digit to 6-digit DISCO).

definitions.variable: Firm tenure and general work experience
definitions.definition: Constructed by matching the linked employer-employee data with pension contribution data dating back to 1964.
Five levels of highest educational attainment: less than high school (reference), regular high-school diploma, vocational, college degree (3-year Bachelor), graduate (Master's and PhD combined).

authors: Sandra E. Black, Sanni Breining, David N. Figlio, Jonathan Guryan, Krzysztof Karbownik, Helena Skyt Nielsen, Jeffrey Roth and Marianne Simonsen
title: Sibling Spillovers
summary: Identifies spillovers within the family from having a disabled younger sibling using administrative data from both Denmark and Florida. Comparing first- and second-born children in families with three or more children, the second child, who spends more early childhood with the younger sibling, is differentially affected when the third child is disabled.
data: Medical Birth Register (MFR)
National Patient Register (LPR) for disability diagnoses
9th grade exit exam grades (school/education registers)
Parental education, labour market, earnings and leave registers
Florida birth records linked to Florida public school records (FCAT)
variables: Outcome: cohort-standardised 9th grade exit exam GPA (Denmark); FCAT test scores (Florida)
Treatment: third-born sibling has a disability (diagnosed in medical registers) observed by age five
Comparison: second-born vs first-born child (difference-in-differences)
Controls: parental age, education, labour market status, earnings, immigrant status
sample_size: Denmark: 134,277 families with first two children observed, 28,581 families with first three children (4,430 with a disabled third child by age five); Florida: 80,879 and 9,987 families
sample: Families in Denmark (births 1990–2001) and Florida (births 1994–2002) with at least three children where the first two children have the same father.

definitions.definition: Indicator D = 1 if the third-born child is observed disabled, in Denmark from disabilities recorded in the medical (patient) registries, with the main treatment being disability first observed by age five (alternatively between ages five and ten). Most common Danish by-age-five disabilities: asthma (41%), congenital malformations of the musculoskeletal system (20%), congenital malformations of the circulatory system (10%); diagnosis code lists are not given.
Cohort-standardised 9th grade exit exam grades (GPA), based on assessments by the student's teacher and an external reviewer, normalised to mean zero and standard deviation one.

definitions.variable: Birth order / exposure (second vs first born)
definitions.definition: M = 1 if the child is second born ('more exposed'), 0 if first born; birth order measured from exact dates of birth in the Birth Register with parent-child links. Sample restricted to families with at least three children where the first two children have the same father; Danish births 1990-2001.
Disabilities grouped into physical, cognitive and behavioral; severity checked using hospitalisation records (inpatient, outpatient and emergency room admissions).

Parental age, educational attainment, labour market status, earnings, leave taking and immigrant status from administrative registers linked via the unique identification number; regression covariates include year and month of birth and child gender with family fixed effects.

authors: Paul Bingley, Lorenzo Cappellari and Konstantinos Tatsiramos
title: Family, Community and Long-Term Socio-Economic Inequality: Evidence from Siblings and Youth Peers
summary: Decomposes sibling correlations in permanent earnings, education and unemployment for the Danish population into family and community components, allowing for life-cycle dynamics. Family is the dominant factor; community background shapes earnings and unemployment correlations early in working life but fades quickly.
data: Civil registration system / population register with parent links (BEF)
Central person register address histories (parish of residence)
Education register / national pupil database (school at age 15)
Annual earnings from tax-based income registers
variables: Outcome: pre-tax annual labour earnings (residual log earnings), 1984–2011
Grouping: brothers (family), schoolmates at age 15, parish neighbours at age 15
Parameters: sibling, school-peer and neighbour correlations over the life cycle
sample_size: 695,960 men; 10,930,859 earnings observations (122,652 brother pairs, 380,948 singletons)
sample: Danish men born 1960–1983 (first and second sons sharing both legal parents, plus singletons and same-age peers), linked to schoolmates and parish neighbours at age 15.

definitions.definition: Pre-tax annual labour earnings 1984-2011 in 2005 prices; zero-earnings observations excluded, a quarter of a percentile trimmed from each tail of the annual distribution, and at least three consecutive earnings observations required. Residuals from regressing log real gross annual earnings on year dummies and a quadratic age trend by two-year birth cohort group.

First and second sons (born 1960-1983) of sampled fathers who share both legal parents from registration at birth and are not adopted; son birth order determined irrespective of daughters. Excludes sons also observed as fathers and brothers born less than 12 months or more than 12 years apart (122,652 pairs); singletons kept.

Males born in the same calendar year enrolled in the same school on 31 October of the calendar year they turn 15 (normally 9th grade), from the national pupil database (covers grade 8 and above from August 1973). Pupils at schools exclusively for special educational needs are excluded.

Neighbourhood defined as parish of residence (available from 1973) from the central person register address data on 31 October of the calendar year the male turns 15; neighbours are males born in the same year living in the same parish (2,123 parishes).
Data grouped into two-year birth cohorts (1960-61 to 1982-83) with age imputed from the first year of birth; each cohort observed from age 24 for at least 6 years and up to 28 years.

authors: Steffen Andersen, Julie Marx, Kasper Meisner Nielsen and Lise Vesterlund
title: Gender Differences in Negotiation: Evidence from Real Estate Transactions
summary: Men appear to secure better prices than women in Danish real estate transactions, but the gap shrinks with better controls for property value and disappears in repeat-sales and inherited-property samples. The price differences reflect men and women demanding different properties, not differences in negotiation.
data: Property transactions from the Danish Tax and Customs Administration (SKAT)
Housing register (BBR)
Civil Registration System (CPR)
Income and tax-assessed property values from SKAT
Education registers (Ministry of Education)
Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA) employment status
Cause-of-Death Register (Danish National Board of Health)
variables: Outcome: realised transaction price of house or apartment
Key regressor: gender of single buyer/seller
Controls: tax-assessed property value, BBR property characteristics, property fixed effects (repeated sales)
Death sales: properties inherited by an only child from a deceased parent
sample_size: 337,685 real estate transactions (97,216 in repeated-sales sample; 13,953 inherited houses and apartments in death-sales sample)
sample: Arm's-length transactions of Danish houses and apartments involving single female or single male buyers and sellers, 1994–2013.

definitions.definition: Buyers are the owners of the property (per BBR owner records) on January 1 in the year after the transaction; sellers are the owners on January 1 in the year of the transaction. If the sales agreement is signed in year t but ownership is transferred in t+1, buyers are the owners on January 1 of t+2, conditional on no registered trades during t+1.

All property transactions 1994-2013 restricted to single-family houses and apartments bought and sold by individuals; drops transactions flagged by Statistics Denmark as involving price clauses or extreme prices, rented-out properties, properties traded more than once within a year, transactions within a household or between parents and children, households buying or selling more than three properties in a year, and agents outside ages 18-65. Cottages, farms and cooperative housing are excluded.
definitions.source_location: Appendix A, Sample selection; paper Section 2

definitions.variable: Stable household / single man / single woman
definitions.definition: Households use the Statistics Denmark household ID: one or two adults plus children under 25 living with them; three types are couples (married, registered and cohabiting partners), single women and single men. A household must be stable: constant number of adults in the transaction year and the year after, no divorce from two years before to one year after the transaction, and no adult member lost to death within one year before or after.
definitions.source_location: Appendix A, Sample selection and Variable definition

definitions.definition: Log of the realised transaction price in thousand year-2015 DKK, from property transactions announced in the Danish Gazette (Statstidende) as received by SKAT.

SKAT's assessment of the property's value if sold (basis for property value tax and municipal land tax), carried out every other year and regulated by local house price growth in non-assessment years; the paper uses the assessed value in the year prior to the transaction, entered as log of thousand year-2015 DKK.
definitions.source_location: Appendix A, Data sources and Variable definition; paper Section 2

definitions.definition: IDA status classified at end of November each year: employed if the majority of personal income is from paid employment, self-employed if the majority is from self-employment, retired if outside the labour market with the majority of income from private or public pensions, and unemployed otherwise. Household variables are shares of adult members (0, 0.5 or 1), measured in November of the year before the transaction.
definitions.source_location: Section 2 (data source 6); Appendix A Variable definition

definitions.definition: Household totals of total income and net wealth (third-party reported to SKAT) in million year-2015 DKK, measured December 31 of the year before the transaction and winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles.
definitions.source_location: Table 1 note; Appendix A Variable definition

definitions.definition: First-time buyer: no member of the buyer household has previously owned real estate. Out-of-town buyer: the household buys property in a municipality it did not previously live in.

Household terminations (death of the only member of a one-person household: single, widowed or divorced) of individuals owning real estate at death, identified by linking the Cause-of-Death Register to CPR; restricted to decedents with exactly one child (the beneficiary, linked via CPR) and to sales of the property within 1.5 years of the death, applying all full-sample selection criteria (13,953 death sales).
definitions.source_location: Appendix A, Death data; paper Section 4

definitions.definition: Indicator for having children aged 5 to 15 (not necessarily living in the household), interacted with the transaction quarter following Harding, Rosenthal and Sirmans (2003).

authors: Christian Dustmann, Mikkel Mertz and Anna Okatenko
title: Neighbourhood Gangs, Crime Spillovers and Teenage Motherhood
summary: Uses the random assignment of refugees to municipalities between 1986 and 1998. Gang crime in the assignment neighbourhood raises boys' probability of offending before 19 and girls' probability of teenage motherhood, with lasting consequences: more inactivity for men and lower earnings and more benefit claims for women at ages 19 to 28.
data: Immigration register
Annual population registers (BEF)
Central Police Register (criminal charges and convictions)
Education registers (including survey-based register of immigrants' education)
Income registers and register-based labour force statistics (RAS)
National Patient Register (abortions)
variables: Outcome: teenage motherhood (child born while aged 15–18); youth crime convictions for boys
Treatment: municipal group (gang) crime conviction rate of males 15–25 in assignment year
Identification: quasi-random assignment of refugees to municipalities under the 1986–1998 dispersal policy
Long-run outcomes: earnings, employment, education
sample_size: 8,172 assigned refugee children; 3,792 girls in teenage motherhood estimation sample
sample: Refugee children from eight refugee-sending countries assigned to Danish municipalities at age 0–14 between 1986 and 1998, observed every year until age 19.

definitions.definition: Judicial decisions 1980-2018 from the conviction register; for each person-case (journr) the final decision is kept (appeals), and a case counts as guilty unless the decision type is acquittal or dismissal. Offences are classified by 7-digit offence code into violent/sexual, property, drug, other and traffic, and traffic offences are dropped; the date of the offence comes from the charge register.

A conviction for a gang-type offence in a case where more than one person is convicted (gang_crime_3 requires at least three). Gang-type offences are non-sexual violence, arson/robbery-type property offences, drug offences and weapons offences; a case is gang-type if anyone in the case is convicted of a gang-type offence.
definitions.codes: gang type: 2-digit AFG_GER7 (floor(ger7/100000)) == 12; 4-digit (floor(ger7/1000)) in 1312, 1339, 1380, 1390, 1435, 1440, 3410; 7-digit in 1366505, 1445750, 1445777-1445782, 3210510; gang_crime = N convicted in journr > 1 & gang type

definitions.definition: Per municipality and year: number of male residents aged 15-25 (calendar year minus birth year between 15 and 26) with at least one conviction (resp. gang-crime conviction) for an offence committed that year at age above 14 and below 27, divided by the number of such male residents, times 100. Offences from 2017 onward or before 1980 are dropped.
definitions.codes: sh_g (gang), sh_nc (overall); KOEN==1 for men; KOM municipality

definitions.definition: Immigrants arriving 1986-1998 from refugee-sending countries (Balkan origins excluded as covered by a different placement policy), with some countries restricted by arrival year; the household head at immigration is identified via father, mother (if under 18) or spouse links, and individuals arriving more than a year after the household head, or with a gap of more than one year between immigration and first appearance in the registers, are dropped.
definitions.codes: IELAND: Iraq 5436; Iran 5438 (arrival>=1980); Vietnam 5468, 5488; Sri Lanka 5418 (>=1984); stateless Lebanon 5103, 5456, 5473; Ethiopia 5214 (<1991); Afghanistan 5404; Somalia 5289 (>=1989); keep refugee_ieland<=8

definitions.definition: The first municipality (KOM) in which the household head at assignment is observed in the population registers after immigration; children assigned to a different municipality than their household head are dropped, and Copenhagen assignment is KOM 101.

Date of first birth is the earliest birth date among children linked to the woman through the mother ID (PNRM) in the population registers; teenage motherhood (mother_1518) equals 1 if the first birth occurs at age at least 14 and below 19 (commented 'had a child by age 19'). For girls aged 15-20 at assignment, motherhood within 4 years of assignment is used, dropping those whose first birth is within 280 days of immigration.
Indicator for an abortion diagnosis in the National Patient Register 1980-2014 (medical, other, unspecified and failed attempted abortion), attached to refugee girls.
definitions.codes: ICD-10 (DIAG first 4 chars) DO04, DO05, DO06, DO07

definitions.variable: Labour market status (employed / unemployed / not in labour force)
definitions.definition: Primary labour market status in the last week of November from RAS, with code schemes varying by year.
definitions.codes: 1981-1993 ARBSTIL: employed 11-39, unemployed 40, NILF 50-92 (1990+ keep NOVPRIO==1); 1994-1995 NYARB: employed 11-39, unemployed 40, NILF 41-400; 1996-2007 SOCSTIL_KODE: employed 115-199, unemployed 200, NILF 201-400; 2008-2015 SOC_STATUS_KODE (PRIMAER_STATUS_KODE==1): employed 110-138, 611, 612, unemployed 200, NILF 311-517

definitions.definition: For assigned refugee children 1987-2018, income outcomes are taken from the income register over the full year and education from the education registers (measured in October of the year prior), with employment taken from RAS for November of the previous year.
definitions.codes: IND: PERINDKIALT_13, LOENMV_13, ERHVERVSINDK_13, STIP, OFF_OVERFORSEL_13, NETOVSKUD_13; UDDA: HFAUDD; RAS ARBSTIL 11-37 employed, 40 unemployed (pre-1994)

authors: Mikkel Aagaard Houmark, Victor Ronda, Esben Agerbo, Preben Bo Mortensen and Michael Rosholm
title: Genetic and Socioeconomic Achievement Gaps in Elementary School
summary: Shows that the achievement gap by polygenic score for educational attainment is as large as the gap by socioeconomic status and widens during elementary school, but only among low-SES children. Selection into neighbourhoods and schools explains part of the SES gap but none of the genetic gap, which instead relates to conscientiousness and the learning environment.
data: iPSYCH2015 case-cohort genotype sample (neonatal blood spots from the Danish National Biobank)
Danish national tests (reading and mathematics, grades 2–8)
Population registers with parent-child links (BEF)
Parental income registers (IND)
Parental education registers (UDDA)
Psychiatric diagnoses of parents (patient registers)
School and neighbourhood identifiers
variables: Outcome: standardised national reading test scores (grades 2, 4, 6, 8); mathematics tests (grades 3, 6, 8)
Key regressor: polygenic score for educational attainment (EA PGS)
Key regressor: SES index from parental income and education
Sibling fixed effects: within-family variation in the PGS
Mediators: neighbourhood and school sorting
sample_size: 40,136 individuals with 87,917 reading test outcomes (24,062 psychiatric cases, 16,074 random controls); sibling sample 2,705 individuals
sample: Genotyped iPSYCH children of European descent born 1994–2008 who completed at least one national test between 2nd and 8th grade.

definitions.definition: Danish national (adaptive, Rasch-scored) reading tests in grades 2, 4, 6 and 8: each of the three profile areas (text comprehension, language comprehension, decoding) is standardised by school year, averaged, and the average re-standardised to mean 0, SD 1. Repeated tests of the same subject-grade are dropped (first test kept by test time).
definitions.codes: FAGID 0102, 0104, 0106, 0108 = reading grades 2, 4, 6, 8; outcome variable ztheta

definitions.definition: Mathematics national tests in grades 3 and 6 and, from 2018, grade 8, constructed in a similar fashion to the reading score.
Mother's and father's highest education category converted to years of schooling.

definitions.variable: Family disposable income in early childhood
definitions.definition: Mother's and father's disposable income deflated by CPI (2015=100), averaged over child ages 1-7, summed across parents and logged (set to 0 if negative).

Families are ranked in percentiles (one observation per child) on the sum of parents' years of education and on log family disposable income; the two percentile ranks are summed and re-ranked into percentiles scaled to 0-0.99 (ses_rank), and the SES index is this rank standardised to mean 0, SD 1 within the sample.
definitions.codes: xtile famedu_rank, faminc_rank nq(100); famses_rank; ses_std = std(ses_rank)

definitions.definition: Indicators for the mother and father ever having received a psychiatric diagnosis (based on the date of the parent's first psychiatric diagnosis in the parental psychiatry file); an additional indicator flags a diagnosis by the child's birth year.
definitions.codes: mpsych_date, fpsych_date -> mmh_ever, fmh_ever, mmh_age0, fmh_age0

definitions.definition: Sum of four risk indicators: both parents with 10 years of education; family disposable income in the bottom birth-cohort quintile; either parent ever with a psychiatric diagnosis; family not intact. ses2 groups risk 0-1 vs 2-4.
definitions.codes: risk1..risk4; fdinc2 = xtile(famdinc18, n(5)) by yearborn

definitions.definition: Families defined by the mother-father ID pair (full siblings); the sibling sample includes children with at least one full sibling observed on the same test.

Keeps children of European genetic ancestry (non_european==0) or, if missing, those whose own and both parents' region of birth is Denmark or Europe; required because the EA GWAS uses European-descent samples.
definitions.codes: non_european; region_birth, region_birth_m, region_birth_f in {Denmark, Europe}

definitions.definition: Following Gensowski et al. (2020), teachers are linked to schools; school-by-year averages of teacher high-school GPA, age, experience, tenure, sick-leave share and share of the previous ten years unemployed are used to predict school national test scores, and the predictions are used to rank schools by teacher quality.
Total fraction of school days absent, including all absence regardless of reason, from the absence registries.

authors: Bent Jesper Christensen, Rasmus Lentz, Dale T. Mortensen, George R. Neumann and Axel Werwatz
title: On-the-Job Search and the Wage Distribution
summary: Estimates an on-the-job search model on the Danish Integrated Database for Labour Market Research, splitting each firm's separation rate into an exogenous part and a job-to-job part that falls with the firm's wage. Workers search less intensely the higher their wage, and the estimated model accounts for the gap between the distribution of wages earned and the distribution of wage offers.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA), matched employer-employee data
variables: Outcome: job separations (stayers one year later) by establishment
Establishment average hourly wage (Statistics Denmark hourly wage estimate)
Wage offer distribution weighted by hires from non-employment
Wage earned distribution weighted by establishment employment
Sub-samples by occupation: skilled, unskilled, managers, salaried
sample_size: 113,332 private-sector establishments
sample: All establishments in the Danish private sector, with workers aged 18–65, split by occupational category.

definitions.definition: For each establishment, the number of employees in November 1994 and the number of 'stayers', defined as workers who were employees both initially (November 1994) and in the following November (1995); separations are modelled as stayers out of initial employment.

For each private-sector establishment and occupational sub-sample, the average of the Statistics Denmark estimate of the hourly wage of each worker of that occupational type employed during November 1994 to November 1995, in 1994 DKK; only workers aged 18-65 included, and wage rates below 69 DKK per hour (taken as the effective legal minimum wage) and in the top 1 percent are excluded from the average (but such workers are kept in employment and stayer counts).

Distribution of establishment average hourly wages, each weighted by the fraction of all non-employed workers hired by the establishment during the year (only hires from non-employment are used, to avoid selection among job-to-job movers).
Distribution of the same establishment average hourly wages weighted by the establishment's relative employment size in November 1994.

Pooled private-sector establishment sample partitioned by worker occupation into skilled and unskilled workers ('blue collar') and managers and salaried workers ('white collar'); distributions and counts are built separately per sub-sample.
All establishments in the Danish private sector are included (overall 'private sector sample', 113,332 establishments).

authors: Anna Piil Damm
title: Ethnic Enclaves and Immigrant Labor Market Outcomes: Quasi-Experimental Evidence
summary: Uses the quasi-random dispersal of refugees across Danish municipalities between 1986 and 1998 to separate the effect of living in an ethnic enclave from self-selection. Larger enclaves raise refugee men's annual earnings without changing their employment rates, and the gains are larger where more co-nationals are employed, pointing to job information networks.
data: Longitudinal administrative registers on the immigrant population (Statistics Denmark), 1984–2000
Population register (BEF) incl. country of origin, year of immigration and municipality
Survey-based register on immigrants' pre-immigration education and integrated pupil register
Municipality statistics: unemployment register, election statistics, register-based labour force statistics, housing statistics
Danish Refugee Council administrative statistics on temporary housing (to identify assignment municipality)
variables: Outcome: employment probability
Outcome: real annual labour earnings
Key regressor: ethnic enclave (co-national group) size in municipality
Instrument / identification: initial assignment municipality under the 1986–1998 spatial dispersal policy
Controls: gender, age, marital status, children, education, country of origin, year of immigration
sample_size: 13,927 individuals (balanced panel observed annually for seven years after immigration)
sample: Adult refugees from 11 main refugee-sending countries assigned to Danish municipalities under the dispersal policy, observed annually from receipt of residence permit to seven years after.

definitions.definition: Based on labour market status in November of each year: employed if main occupation is wage-employment with at least 9 hours of weekly work, or self-employment (includes part-time of at least 9 weekly hours and full-time). Outcome measured seven years after immigration.

Sum of wage earnings, profits from own company and sickness benefits, deflated by the consumer price index (base year 1980); analysed for refugees with positive earnings seven years after immigration.
Number of first- and second-generation immigrants (immigrants and descendants) from individual i's source country living in i's municipality of residence; ethnicity proxied by country of origin.
registers: BEF (100 per cent sample of immigrants)
definitions.source_location: Section III.B (p. 13); Table A.I Part B

definitions.definition: Individuals from 11 main refugee-sending countries extracted by an algorithm based on country of origin and first year of residence permit (built from official asylum permit counts), immigrating under the 1986-1998 dispersal policy, aged 18-59, observed annually up to seven years after immigration (balanced panel of 13,927). Excludes those married at immigration to a Dane, an immigrant from a non-refugee-sending country, or an immigrant from a refugee-sending country who immigrated at least one year earlier (family reunification).

The first municipality of residence observed in the registers is classified as temporary housing if the person relocates to another municipality within the same county within one year after receipt of the first residence permit; otherwise the first municipality is the municipality of assignment (algorithm based on the Danish Refugee Council's statistics on temporary housing).

Number of immigrants from the individual's source country placed by the authorities in the individual's municipality of assignment in year t, for t = -7, ..., 0 (0 = year of immigration), i.e. initial and past inflows of placed co-nationals.
registers: BEF (100 per cent sample of immigrants)

definitions.definition: Dummies from the education code of highest degree attained: no degree = 0-9 years, high school = 10-12 years, professional = 13+ years, plus unknown education.
registers: Survey-based register on immigrants' pre-immigration education

definitions.definition: Unemployment rate within a radius of DKK 60 (approx. USD 10) of transport cost around the largest post office in the municipality, constructed by Local Government Studies.

definitions.variable: Municipality characteristics (right-wing votes, county jobs, social housing)
definitions.definition: % right-wing votes: Liberal plus Conservative votes as a share of Liberal, Conservative, Social Democratic and Socialist People's Party votes at the latest municipal election; % county jobs: persons employed in the municipality as a share of county employment; % social housing: social housing dwellings for all-year residence as a share of all such dwellings.

authors: Christian M. Dahl, Daniel le Maire and Jakob R. Munch
title: Wage Dispersion and Decentralization of Wage Bargaining
summary: Exploits the shift in Denmark during the 1990s from centralised to firm-level wage bargaining. Workers covered by firm-level bargaining earn a wage premium, returns to skills are higher, and wage dispersion is greater than under sector-level bargaining.
data: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research (IDA), matched employer-employee data
Income register (tax files)
Supplementary Pension Fund (ATP) contributions for hours worked
DA/LO bargaining-segment classification by NACE industry and DISCO occupation (Confederation of Danish Employers)
variables: Outcome: log hourly wage (labour income plus mandatory pension payments over hours)
Treatment: wage-setting system (standard-rate, minimum-wage, minimum-pay, firm-level bargaining)
Outcome: wage dispersion (quantile regressions) and returns to skills
Controls: gender, children, marriage, immigrant status, education, experience, plant size, industry-by-year dummies
Worker fixed effects; changes in wage-setting system over time
sample_size: about 1.14 million worker-year observations (1,137,367)
sample: 30% random sample of full-time private-sector workers aged 25–65 in 36 DA/LO bargaining segments, in plants with at least five employees.

definitions.definition: Sum of total labour income (from tax files in the Income Register) and mandatory pension fund payments, divided by the total number of hours worked in the year (ATP-imputed); observations with unobserved wage, wage flagged by Statistics Denmark as low precision, or in the top or bottom half percentile are discarded.

Imputed from the worker's ATP contribution group: no payment for 0-9 weekly hours, 1/3 of full-time payment for 9-18, 2/3 for 18-27, and full payment for 27+; workers paying full-time ATP are assigned hours corresponding to the standard 37-hour week. Overtime not captured.

Workers are allocated to 36 DA/LO bargaining segments using six-digit NACE industry and four-digit DISCO (ISCO-88) occupation codes, as DA and LO do (about 85% of DA/LO employment); each segment's yearly system is classified as standard-rate (normallønssystemet), minimum-wage (minimallønssystemet), minimum-pay (mindstebetalingssystemet) or firm-level bargaining (uden lønsats).
definitions.codes: NACE 6-digit x DISCO 4-digit (segment list not given)

definitions.definition: Full-time workers aged 25-65 employed in one of the DA/LO bargaining segments, 1992-2001, excluding scholarship recipients in ordinary education, plants with fewer than five employees, and observations with unreliable/extreme wages; a 30% random sample is drawn (about 1.14 million worker-years).

Unskilled (high school or equivalent or less), vocational education (final stage of secondary education preparing for direct labour market entry), short-term higher education and long-term higher education, from the Danish education code corresponding to ISCED (higher education = ISCED 5 and 6).
Actual labour market experience accumulated since 1964.
Plant size defined as the number of employees, plus variables measuring the labour force composition at plant level; regressions also include 25 industry dummies interacted with year dummies.

authors: Gustaf Bruze, Michael Svarer and Yoram Weiss
title: The Dynamics of Marriage and Divorce
summary: Estimates a dynamic model of marriage, divorce and remarriage with learning about match quality on long register histories of Danish cohorts. Spousal education is complementary in generating marital surplus, education stabilises marriages, education raises men's share of the surplus, and divorce costs are high both early and late in a marriage.
data: Population register with marital and cohabitation histories (BEF)
Education registers (UDDA), completed education at age 46
variables: Outcome: transitions into and out of marriage, divorce and remarriage
Key variable: completed education group at 46 (high school or less, vocational, college)
Assortative matching by education of spouses
Structural model parameters: match quality, gains from marriage, divorce costs
sample_size: 61,780 individuals (31,835 men and 29,945 women)
sample: All men and women born in Denmark in 1960 with complete residence records 1980–2006 and not married at age 20.

definitions.definition: All men and women born in 1960 followed annually 1980-2006 (ages 20-46); individuals must have a Danish address in every year (complete marital history), and those already married at age 20 are excluded, leaving 61,780 individuals.
Three groups based on completed education at age 46: high school or less, vocational education, and college (some college or more).

Classified as cohabiting if sharing an address with an opposite-sex person who is not family-related and is no more than 15 years older or younger. The paper uses two alternative partnership definitions: legal marriage only, and partnerships including legal marriage and cohabitation.

Yearly states: single never married, single previously married, or married (characterised by own and spouse's marital history, spouse's education and type, and marriage duration). Divorced persons are assumed single for at least one year before remarrying; direct marriage-to-marriage moves (2.3%) have the first year of the new marriage recoded as singlehood.
Fixed cost of divorce parameterised with ten dummies for marital duration of 1, 2, ..., 9 and 10 or more years.

authors: Paul Bingley and Alessandro Martinello
title: Measurement Error in Income and Schooling and the Bias of Linear Estimators
summary: Links survey reports of income and schooling for Danish respondents to the same variables in the registers. Measurement errors in survey income and schooling are correlated and non-classical, so standard corrections fail, and the paper quantifies the resulting bias in linear estimators such as returns to schooling.
data: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), Danish respondents
Danish administrative income registers
Danish administrative education registers
variables: Variable validated: survey-reported annual income vs register income
Variable validated: survey-reported schooling vs register schooling
Estimand: measurement error bias in OLS and IV estimators of returns to schooling
sample: Danish SHARE respondents linked to administrative registers to validate survey income and schooling.

authors: Pieter Gautier, Paul Muller, Bas van der Klaauw, Michael Rosholm and Michael Svarer
title: Estimating Equilibrium Effects of Job Search Assistance
summary: A randomised activation experiment in two Danish counties helped treated job seekers find work faster, but untreated job seekers in the same counties found work more slowly than in comparison counties. An equilibrium search model fitted to the data shows that these displacement effects make a large-scale rollout far less beneficial than the partial estimates suggest.
data: National Labour Market Board administrative data on unemployment benefit spells (all Danish counties)
Randomised activation experiment assignment (Storstrøm and South Jutland, birth date 1st–15th of month)
Income transfer data (exit destinations)
National Labour Market Board monthly stock of open vacancies by county (from local job centres)
variables: Outcome: unemployment duration / exit rate from benefits (weeks)
Treatment: assignment to intensive activation programme (born 1st–15th of month)
Spillover comparison: non-participants in experiment counties vs comparison counties (difference-in-differences)
Outcome: log stock of open vacancies by county and month
Structural equilibrium search model parameters
period: Benefit inflows November 2004–February 2005 (pre-experiment) and November 2005–February 2006 (experiment), followed up to two years; vacancies January 2004–November 2007
sample_size: 40,403 benefit claimants in experiment period (3,751 experiment participants: 1,814 treated, 1,937 controls); 49,063 in pre-experiment sample
sample: All individuals in Denmark who started collecting regular unemployment benefits between November 2005 and February 2006, plus a pre-experiment inflow cohort one year earlier.

definitions.definition: Duration (in weeks) of collecting regular unemployment benefits from the week benefits start, followed for at most two years; exits treated as exits from unemployment (linked income-transfer data show almost all exits in the first two years are to employment); durations censored otherwise.
registers: National Labour Market Board benefit spell data

definitions.definition: All individuals starting to collect unemployment benefits November 2005-February 2006 in Storstrom and South Jutland counties took part; those born on the 1st-15th of the month were assigned to the intensive activation programme (letter after ~1.5 weeks, 2-week JSA course after 5-6 weeks, weekly/biweekly caseworker meetings, new programme after 4 months); those born 16th-31st are controls.
registers: National Labour Market Board benefit spell data

definitions.definition: All 41,801 individuals applying for regular benefits November 2005-February 2006 in all Danish counties, minus 1,398 with inconsistent county of residence; non-experiment counties form the comparison group; a pre-experiment sample of 49,063 individuals starting benefits November 2004-February 2005 controls for county differences (difference-in-differences in a stratified proportional hazard model).
registers: National Labour Market Board benefit spell data

definitions.definition: Monthly average number of open vacancies per day by county, January 2004-November 2007, collected by the National Labour Market Board from local job centres; used in logs.
registers: National Labour Market Board vacancy data

definitions.definition: Weeks of benefit receipt in the previous year and in the past two years, plus gender, nationality and an indicator for entering unemployment in November or December.
registers: National Labour Market Board benefit spell data

authors: Sanni Breining, Joseph Doyle, David N. Figlio, Krzysztof Karbownik and Jeffrey Roth
title: Birth Order and Delinquency: Evidence from Denmark and Florida
summary: In both Denmark and Florida, second-born boys are substantially more likely than their first-born brothers to be disciplined in school and to enter the criminal justice system. The evidence points to reduced parental time investment for later-born children, rather than differences in health at birth or neighbourhood, as the mechanism.
data: Medical Birth Register (MFR)
Population register with parent and sibling links (BEF)
Central Crime Register (convictions, sentences, incarceration)
School registers (9th grade exit exam grades)
Register of Daycare Institutions
National Patient Register (LPR) and Psychiatric Central Register
Parental education, employment, earnings and maternity leave registers
Florida birth records linked to school and juvenile justice records
variables: Outcome: criminal conviction by age 16 and 21; sentenced to prison; incarcerated
Treatment: being second-born vs first-born boy (sibling fixed effects)
Outcome: 9th grade exit exam grades in reading and math
Mechanisms: maternal leave and employment, daycare enrolment ages 1–3, school starting age, psychiatric diagnoses by age 10
Controls: parental age, education, employment, family income, immigrant status
sample_size: Denmark: 121,100 children in 60,550 families (first- and second-born boys); 448,979 singleton births 1981–1990 in the full Danish population
sample: Danish families with two or more children with the same father, comparing first-born and second-born boys born 1981–1990 (plus Florida comparison samples).

definitions.definition: Indicator (x100) for having any criminal conviction by age 16, and by age 21, from the Criminal Registers; convictions observable from age 15 (age of criminal responsibility). Traffic offences are excluded; crime outcomes cover convictions for violent, property and special offences.

More severe crime measures: indicator for ever having been issued a suspended prison sentence, and for an implemented (unsuspended) imprisonment sentence (incarceration), by age 16 and by age 21. Traffic offences excluded.

definitions.variable: Violent, property and special crime convictions
definitions.definition: Convictions by age 21 split by crime type: violent (e.g. manslaughter, rape, death threats), property (e.g. forgery, arson, burglary) and special offences (e.g. drug offences, illegal weapon possession, human trafficking). Denmark birth cohorts 1981-1990.

Ninth grade exit exam grades in reading and math from the School Registers, based on assessments by the student's teacher and an external reviewer; standardized to mean zero and unit SD within each cohort.

Indicator for having received, by age 10, a diagnosis at a Danish hospital of a disorder of psychological development, or a behavioural and emotional disorder (e.g. ADHD), from the National Patient Registry and Psychiatric Central Registry.
definitions.codes: ICD-10 F80-F89 (psychological development); ICD-10 F90-F98 (behavioural and emotional)

definitions.definition: Enrolment in out-of-home daycare at ages 1, 2 and 3, from the Register of Daycare Institutions (type and place of daycare observed yearly 1995-2008).

Mother's employment in each of years 0-10 after the child's birth: any employment, and full-time employment defined as employed at least 200 days in a year. Days of maternity leave also used as an outcome.

Birth order from the Birth Register (1960-2010 births) using exact birth dates and parent links; twins excluded; sample is the first two children of families with two or more children, restricted to full biological siblings (same mother and father) with a second-born boy (boy-boy and girl-boy families). Main crime sample is birth cohorts 1981-1990.
Maternal and paternal employment and family income are measured in the year before birth; missing parental education/employment (about 9-10 percent) are mean-imputed with a missing indicator.

authors: Paul Bingley, Petter Lundborg and Stéphanie Vincent Lyk-Jensen
title: The Opportunity Costs of Mandatory Military Service: Evidence from a Draft Lottery
summary: Uses the Danish draft lottery to estimate the effect of conscription on later outcomes. Military service delays education and labour market entry, and the paper quantifies the resulting losses in schooling and earnings for those who serve.
data: Danish Defence military register (Armed Forces Day draft records: IQ test, eligibility, height, lottery number)
Earnings from employer reports to tax authorities (income registers)
Education registers (UDDA)
Central Crime Register
National hospital discharge register (LPR)
Medical Birth Register (MFR) birth weight
Population register (BEF)
variables: Outcome: annual labour income at ages 25–35
Treatment: military service
Instrument: draft lottery number below the threshold
Heterogeneity: cognitive ability (draft board IQ test)
Mechanisms: years of schooling, employment, health care use, crime
sample_size: 152,269 men without missing earnings (military register covers 155,570 fit-for-service conscripts)
sample: Danish men born 1976–1983 declared fit for military service who drew a draft lottery number at the Armed Forces Day.

definitions.definition: Annual labour income from employment and self-employment, including sickness benefits and paternity leave benefits, from employer reports to the tax authorities (sum over all employments in the calendar year); excludes occupational pension contributions and study grants/loans. Measured at ages 25-35 and used in logs (zeros drop out); sensitivity measure excludes sickness and leave benefits.
registers: Employer income reports to tax authorities

definitions.definition: Among men judged fit for service at the Armed Forces Day who drew a lottery number (1 to 36,000), 'drafted' means drawing a number below the Army's announced cutoff, regardless of whether they served. Military register covers 155,570 fit conscripts in birth cohorts 1976-1983.
Men who start military service aged 18-24, regardless of whether drafted; those who serve without being drafted are volunteers.
Armed Forces Day IQ test score: number of correct answers out of 78 items; used to split the sample into ability quartiles.
Years of schooling imputed from Statistics Denmark's highest completed education, based on enrolment and qualifications reported by educational institutions.
Proportion of the year during which unemployment insurance benefits were received, at age 26; social assistance recipients are not counted as unemployed.
definitions.source_location: Section V, Table 9 panel A, footnote 18

definitions.definition: Bank assets minus bank debt at age 26 from financial institution reports to the tax authorities; mortgage debt and stocks/bonds excluded.
definitions.source_location: Section V, Table 9 panel B, footnote 19

definitions.definition: Indicator for having been convicted of any type of crime, excluding traffic offences, from age 25, from the Central Crime Register; pre-conscription values used as controls.

definitions.variable: Hospitalization, psychiatric diagnosis, psychiatric medication, addiction treatment
definitions.definition: Any admission to somatic or psychiatric hospitals including same-day patients (national hospital discharge register); psychiatric diagnoses and addiction treatment from the hospital discharge register; purchase of GP-prescribed mental-health medicine from the Danish Medicines Agency.
definitions.source_location: Section V, Table 9 panels D-G, footnote 22

definitions.definition: Statistics Denmark classification: native Danes are born in Denmark with at least one parent born in Denmark; others are first- or second-generation immigrants.

Out-of-home care: placed in out-of-home care (foster care or residential care homes) before age 18. Single-parent family: 0 if living with both legal parents on the 17th birthday according to the central person register.

authors: Anne Ardila Brenøe and Ulf Zölitz
title: Exposure to More Female Peers Widens the Gender Gap in STEM Participation
summary: Exploits idiosyncratic variation in the share of female peers across cohorts within Danish high schools. A higher share of female peers lowers women's probability of enrolling in and graduating from STEM programmes and raises men's, widening the gender gap in STEM.
data: Student/education registers with high school, track and cohort identifiers (UDDA)
Population register with parental links (BEF)
Parental income and education registers (IND, UDDA)
Earnings and employment registers
Occupation codes (STEM occupations)
Fertility from population/birth registers
variables: Outcome: STEM college enrolment and completion (ISCED fields 05, 06, 07)
Treatment: proportion of female peers in school-cohort of the math track
Identification: within-school across-cohort variation (school and cohort fixed effects)
Long-run outcomes: STEM occupation, earnings at age 36, gender wage gap, fertility
period: High school entry 1980–1994; outcomes followed up to 20 years after entry
sample_size: 182,211 students in 127 schools (1,877 school-cohort observations)
sample: All students entering the math track of Danish academic high schools between 1980 and 1994, excluding schools with tiny or atypical cohorts.
